  1) Inject increased eviction rate into two hosts in the staging cluster (use staging-only tokens).
  2) Observe alert firing, validate that Primary acknowledges within SLO.
  3) Execute runbook: cordon host, restart cache, monitor hit-rate recovery.
  4) Track MTTA and MTTR, collect logs and traces.
  5) Run customer-communication template in a simulated status page update.

Status Page & Customer Communication Templates
---------------------------------------------
Guiding principle: clarity, timeliness, and single-source-of-truth. Use the status page for public updates; use direct customer notifications for high-touch customers. All messages should be approved by SRE Bridge and CS Liaison before posting.

Template: Initial public notice (Status Page)
Title: Intermittent request latency for text-generation APIs in us-west-2
Body:
- Impact: Some customers may see elevated latency for text-generation endpoints in us-west-2.
- Scope: ~10% of requests between 11:03–ongoing local time. %PLACEHOLDER_CUSTOMERS%
- Mitigation: We are investigating and have routed traffic away from affected hosts.
- Next update: in 30 minutes.

Template: Customer-facing email (for impacted enterprise customers)
Subject: Service disruption affecting text-generation in us-west-2 — interim notice
Body:
Hi <Customer Name>,
We are experiencing elevated latency for text-generation workloads in us-west-2 which may affect <product-feature>. Our SRE team has identified a partial KV-cache eviction event and is executing mitigation steps. We will:
1) Route traffic to healthy hosts
2) Temporarily increase quota for critical workloads if needed
3) Provide hourly updates until resolved
Estimated impact: requests may experience 2–6s additional latency. We will follow up with a full post-incident report.
If you would like real-time updates in a bridge, reply to this message and we will invite you.
Regards,
Maya Alvarez (on behalf of Redwood SRE)

Internal cadence for updates
- P0: every 15 minutes until stable, then 30-minute cadence for 2 hours, then hourly.
- P1: every 30 minutes until stable.

Postmortem & Learning Review
---------------------------
- Postmortem template: summary, timeline, root cause, detection/mitigation gaps, action items (owner + due date), and impact to customers.
- Timing: draft within 72 hours; public summary within 7 days for customer-impacting incidents.
- Action item tracking: link to Jira epic (label: incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>) and require owners to set due dates no later than 30 days.

Measuring Effectiveness
-----------------------
Key metrics collected per incident and per quarterly game-lab:
- MTTA (mean time to acknowledge)
- MTTR (mean time to restore)
- Number of comms updates and average approval latency
- Runbook execution accuracy (did responders follow required steps?)
- Skill-lattice badge completions after labs

Appendix A: Cache sizing example (YAML snippet)
- This is an example config fragment used to adjust cache pool sizes after post-incident analysis.

# cache-sizing.yaml
cachePools:
  default:
    shardCount: "64"
    targetHitRate: "0.92"
  small-models:
    shardCount: "16"
    targetHitRate: "0.9"

Appendix B: CLI snippets
- Cordon host (LB):
  curl -XPOST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/lb/cordon -d '{"host":"host-23"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN'
- Trigger cache restart on host via runner:
  redwood-runner exec --host host-23 -- service cache restart

Appendix C: Evidence collection checklist
1. Attach traces for 5 representative failed requests (trace IDs).
2. Save screenshot of 5-minute dashboard view showing alert.
3. Export logs (time window + host list) to incident artifact storage.
4. Add links to synthetic test results used for validation.

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-06-20: Created by Maya Alvarez (initial draft).
- 2026-12-01: Expanded game-lab recipes and added customer comms templates (reviewers: Liam Carter, Priya Menon).

References
----------
- See related runbooks in the runbook library and the incident-postmortem template in /confluence/eng-sre/post-incident-learning-codex-handoff-and-synthesis-2025
- Observability dashboards: /grafana/d/ops/serving-latency

title: dsid_b38be7d5d5a642fba27a21e6495f464e__runtime-fidelity-onboarding-and-consumption-playbook-2028-07-14.txt
text:
Runtime Fidelity: Onboarding & Consumption Playbook

Overview

This playbook describes the recommended approach to onboard customers onto Runtime Fidelity profiles, how to measure and simulate consumption, and how to package pricing and SLAs for predictable economics. It combines a product overview, prerequisites, technical onboarding steps, pricing guidance, rollout milestones, and operational runbooks to enable cross-functional delivery (Product, Solutions, Sales, SRE, and Engineering).

Motivation

As customers adopt Redwood Inference across hosted, dedicated and private deployments they require: predictable latencies, clear fidelity tradeoffs, and transparent billing. Fidelity profiles (a bundle of model variant, quantization, and runtime configuration) enable customers to trade cost for output quality under well-defined SLOs. This doc standardizes onboarding and consumption simulation to reduce regressions and commercial disputes.

Scope

- Audience: Product managers, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success, Sales, Runtime Engineers, SRE.
- Applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private VPC deployments.
- Excludes: Marketplace third-party models (see reference design for third-party adapters).

Definitions

- Fidelity profile: Named configuration combining a model variant, quantization level, KV-cache behavior, batching target, and runtime kernel hints.
- Consumption unit: Token-equivalent used for billing and simulation (see Pricing section).
- Soft-fidelity SLO: Non-contractual quality target measured by eval prompts and acceptance thresholds.

High-level product overview

- Customers select a fidelity profile per route.
- The platform enforces runtime parameters and emits telemetry that maps to cost and quality.
- The Onboarding flow validates economics and quality via a Simulation Run, then issues entitlements (credits or SLO guarantees) as part of commercial packaging.

SLOs and acceptance criteria

- Latency (hosted): p95 <= 150ms for conversational short-turns (<=128 tokens).
- Latency (dedicated): p95 <= 120ms for pinned GPU pools.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated customers (see SLA appendix).
- Quality guardrail: regression < 2% on tenant preflight eval set (measured by ROUGE-like metric provided during onboarding).

Onboarding flow (recommended)

1. Discovery (Sales/SE): Collect target routes, expected qps, latency sensitivity, and example prompt sets.
2. Baseline capture (Customer+SE): Capture 24–72 hours of representative traffic samples or synthetic approximations.
3. Simulation run (Product): Run traffic through the Fidelity Simulator with 3 candidate profiles (High, Balanced, Low cost).
4. Acceptance test (Customer): Stakeholder reviews fidelity evals (10–50 prompts) and signs off on chosen profile.
5. Entitlements & packaging (Finance/Product): Map selected profile to pricing tier, SLA, and crediting (if applicable).
6. Rollout (Engineering/SRE): Canary deploy profile on 1–5% traffic, monitor signals for 72 hours, then expand.
7. Post-rollout (CS/Product): QBR + adjustments to profile parameters as usage stabilizes.

Simulation run: steps and checklist

- Inputs: representative request payloads, session distribution (session length histogram), expected concurrency, and acceptance prompts.
- Engine: Fidelity Simulator (internal tool: fidelity-sim). Use the following CLI to run a smoke simulation:

$ fidelity-sim run --profile balanced-2028 --input sample-traffic.json --duration 1h --out ./sim-results.json

- Required checks: token-per-response distribution, latency p95, model fallbacks triggered, cache hit rates.
- Output artifacts: sim-results.json (telemetry snapshot), fidelity-eval-report.md, cost-estimate.csv.

Packaging and pricing guidance

We recommend three packaged fidelity tiers for commercial offers. Table below shows suggested mapping; adjust for enterprise negotiations.

| Tier | Typical use case | Runtime config (example) | Expected relative cost | Commercial addon |
|------|------------------|--------------------------|------------------------|------------------|
| Fidelity:Premium | Latency-critical, high-Q | Model: variant-v3, quant: fp16, batching: low, KV-cache: full | 1.6x baseline | SLA 99.95%, priority support |
| Fidelity:Balanced | General-purpose conversational | Model: variant-v2, quant: int8, batching: adaptive | 1.0x baseline | Standard SLA, telemetry retention 30d |
| Fidelity:Economy | High-throughput, cost-sensitive | Model: variant-v1, quant: int8-q4, batching: aggressive | 0.55x baseline | Best-effort fallback to lower-cost models |

Pricing considerations (rules of thumb)

- Baseline unit: 1 consumption unit = 1k tokens equivalent for bundled pricing.
- Convert sim-estimate tokens -> consumption units and round up to nearest bundle.
- Offer warm capacity credits for dedicated customers to smooth bursts (recommended: 10–20% of committed qps).
- Preemptible or spot-backed capacity should have explicit crediting rules and shorter SLA windows.

Telemetry schema and signals to monitor

- Required telemetry fields: profile_name, route_id, tenant_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, quantization_tag, batch_size, processing_time_ms, cache_hit, fallback_reason (nullable).
- Key derived metrics: cost_per_1k_tokens, p95_latency_ms, fallback_rate, quality_regression_score, kv_cache_hit_percent.
- Alert thresholds (sample): fallback_rate > 2% over 10m => SEV3; p95_latency increase > 40% vs baseline => SEV2.

Operational runbook: fidelity-related incidents

1. Detect: fidelity-alerts dashboard surfaces spikes in fallback_rate or quality_regression_score.
2. Triage: Check firmware/runtime kernel mismatch, quantization fallback logs, and capacity pressure metrics.
3. Mitigate: Temporarily route affected tenant to an alternative fidelity profile (canary rollback) using routing policy "fidelity-fallback-route".
4. Postmortem: Capture root cause, update profile compatibility matrix and add regression prompts to tenant's preflight set.

Developer API and SDK examples

- Example JSON route configuration (HTTP):

POST /v1/routes HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "route_id": "support-chat-v1",
  "default_fidelity_profile": "balanced-2028-01",
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "model_hints": ["variant-v2","batching:auto"],
  "telemetry_enabled": true
}

- Sample SDK usage (pseudo-code):

client = RedwoodClient(api_key)
response = client.chat.create(route="support-chat-v1", messages=payload, fidelity_profile="balanced-2028-01")

Rollout roadmap and milestones (quarterly)

- Q3 2028: Launch public playbook and fidelity-sim v1.0; pilot with three enterprise customers.
- Q4 2028: Add automated fidelity-advisor suggestions in Console (beta).
- Q1 2029: Offer packaged warm-capacity credits bundled in Dedicated SKUs.

Governance and configuration control

- Fidelity profiles are versioned (semver-like): profile-name:major.minor (e.g., balanced-2028-01). Changes that impact model outputs require an approval from Product + Applied ML and must be accompanied by a regression report.
- All changes to commercial mappings must go through Finance & Legal review and SRE capacity signoff.

Quality & regression management

- Each tenant has a preflight prompt set (10–100 prompts) collected during onboarding. Every profile change runs the preflight set and reports delta metrics.
- If regression > 2% on the preflight set, the profile change is blocked from rollout.

Commercial escalation and credits policy

- If a fidelity profile causes a catastrophic regression (production-quality drop > 8% on customer preflight set), issue a remediation credit equal to 5% of that month’s consumption for the affected routes.
- Credits for degraded latency (p95 above contractual threshold for >72 hours) are tiered at 2% / 5% / 10% depending on SLA deviation.

Appendix A: Compatibility matrix (excerpt)

| Model Variant | Quantization | Supported runtimes | Recommended use |
|---------------|--------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| variant-v3 | fp16 | v3-runtime, dedicated GPUs | Premium conversational, long-context |
| variant-v2 | int8 | v2-runtime (hosted + dedicated) | Balanced conversational |
| variant-v1 | int8-q4 | v1-runtime (edge-friendly) | High-throughput, cost-sensitive |

Appendix B: Release notes (v1.0)

- Release date: 2028-07-14
- Highlights: Public playbook publication; fidelity-sim v1 with end-to-end token-cost simulation; three packaged fidelity tiers defined; default telemetry schema standardized.
- Known limitations: Quantization-aware evals are best-effort; hybrid private deployments may require additional network profiling during Simulation Run.

Appendix C: Owners and contacts

- Product owner: Priya Nambiar (product@redwood.ai)
- Runtime lead: Ethan Morales (eng-serving-runtime)
- Applied ML reviewer: Li Wei (applied-ml)
- Customer success liaison: Sophia Patel

Appendix D: Quick checklist for Solutions Engineers (deliverables)

- [ ] Capture sample traffic (24h).
- [ ] Run fidelity-sim and attach sim-results.json.
- [ ] Present fidelity-eval-report to customer and capture signoff.
- [ ] Apply profile and run 1% canary for 72h.
- [ ] Schedule QBR at 30 days.

If you have questions about mapping to contracts or need a custom fidelity profile, contact product@redwood.ai or open a ticket in #fidelity-onboarding.

title: dsid_50290e533197425e8f84c34b49531375__optimize-lite-launch-kit-product-brief-prd-and-launch-plan-2026-05-10.txt
text:
Optimize Lite - Launch Kit, PRD and Roadmap

Overview:

This document consolidates the product brief, minimal viable PRD, light design constraints, phased roadmap, pricing guidance, and the initial release notes for a compact optimization add-on named "Optimize Lite". Optimize Lite targets small engineering teams and early-stage customers who want measurable inference cost savings with minimal operations overhead.

Purpose:
- Single source of truth to align product, engineering, solutions, and GTM for the first release.
- Keep scope small and safe: automated, explainable suggestions; conservative canaries and shadowing; billing tied to auto-apply usage.

Audience:
- Product managers, engineering leads (Optimize & Runtime), Applied ML, SEs, Sales, Customer Success.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Optimize Lite provides per-tenant, per-route optimization suggestions (batching, prefix caching, curated quant profiles) surfaced in the Redwood Console and via a small Suggestions API. Customers can evaluate suggestions in shadow mode, then opt to canary and auto-apply changes. The goal is a low-friction cost-reduction product with built-in safety and clear commercial packaging.

Top-level goals (measurable):
1) Deliver three suggestion classes with console and API access within GA.
2) Demonstrate >=22% token-cost reduction for transactional benchmarks during pilot.
3) Ensure auto-applies do not increase 99p latency by >5% (automated rollback).
4) Convert 40% of beta customers to paid within 90 days of GA.

Out-of-scope:
- Full Optimize Conductor orchestration (no multi-model switching).
- Automated private/on-prem packaging in v1 (Phase 2 adds manual import/export).

MVE feature list:
- Console: per-route "Optimization Suggestions" panel showing ranked recommendations, estimated savings, risk level, and actions: "Evaluate (shadow)", "Apply (canary)", "Rollback".
- API: suggestions retrieval and apply endpoints (tenant-scoped).
- Suggestion types: batching (adjust batch window and thresholds), prefix/KV caching recommendations, curated quantization profiles (validated list).
- Safety: shadow evaluation, staged canaries, automated rollback triggers, audit trail.

High-level PRD (requirements):
- RQ-01 Suggestion API:
  - Tenant and route scoping required.
  - Response fields: suggestion_id, tenant_id, route, type, friendly_description, estimated_tokens_saved_per_1M, estimated_latency_delta_ms, confidence_score, risk_level.
- RQ-02 Console UX:
  - Suggestions appear on route page. Each suggestion shows an explanation, expected savings, and confidence. Buttons: "Shadow Evaluate", "Canary Apply" (with canary size/duration UI), "Rollback".
- RQ-03 Safety and SLOs:
  - Canary default: 1% traffic for 30m. Monitors: shadow-evaluator delta (default threshold 2%), 99p latency (>5% trigger), error rate increase (>0.5% absolute). On trigger, auto-rollback within 5 minutes and page owner.
- RQ-04 Billing & Quotas:
  - Track suggestions evaluated and suggestions auto-applied. Billing meter charged only for auto-applies and a low monthly add-on fee.
- RQ-05 Metrics & observability:
  - Emit metrics for suggestions_generated, suggestions_evaluated, suggestions_applied, canary_regressions, estimated_tokens_saved. Console shows time-series for these per-tenant.

Design notes and constraints:
- Reuse telemetry ingestion and sampling components from Optimize Conductor where feasible to reduce implementation scope.
- Suggestion ranking uses deterministic heuristics plus an offline-trained lightweight ranker updated weekly; no heavy online retrain in v1.
- All apply operations must be idempotent and accept a dry_run flag.
- Applies translate to runtime policy updates via an internal runtime policy API; the runtime owner must provide a backwards-compatible apply contract.

Data flow (textual):
1) Sampling agent collects request metadata -> profiler constructs distributions (seq_len, latency, prefix entropy).
2) Suggestion engine (rules + ranker) writes candidate suggestions to suggestions-store.
3) Console/API reads store; user triggers shadow/canary workflows which call evaluation service and runtime policy apply API.

Runtime apply contract (summary):
- Endpoint: POST /internal/runtime/policy/apply
- Required fields: tenant_id, route, apply_token, suggestion_id, dry_run (bool).
- Must respond with apply_id, status, and be idempotent for the same apply_token.

Example Suggestion (JSON as text for docs):
{
  "suggestion_id": "sug-20260601-042",
  "tenant_id": "t-01xWz",
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "type": "prefix_cache",
  "friendly_description": "Enable prefix cache for common 1-3 token prefixes and TTL 30s for requests with seq_len <= 128.",
  "estimated_tokens_saved_per_1M": "18,400",
  "estimated_latency_delta_ms": "-0.5",
  "confidence_score": "0.78",
  "risk_level": "low"
}

CLI example (apply canary):
redwood optimize-lite apply --tenant t-01xWz --suggestion sug-20260601-042 --canary-pct 1 --duration 30m --dry-run=false

Safety, monitoring, and alerts:
- Primary automated triggers for rollback: shadow loss delta > 2%, 99p latency increase >5%, error-rate delta >0.5% absolute.
- Alerts to create: P0 when any canary triggers; P1 when an apply occurs with no audit entry.
- Required dashboards: per-tenant suggestion health, canary outcomes, cumulative estimated tokens saved.

Acceptance criteria for GA:
- Suggestions API P95 latency < 200ms under expected load.
- E2E pilot shows >=20% token-cost reduction on target transactional benchmark with no >5% 99p latency regression during canary.
- Security review completed for suggestion-store access and apply workflow (KMS/SSO integration validated).

Roadmap and rollout plan (phased):
- Phase Alpha (4 weeks): internal pilot with 3 internal tenants. Deliver profiler, suggestion engine, suggestions-store, basic console view (read-only).
- Phase Beta (6 weeks): public beta for hosted tenants. Shadow-evaluation enabled; onboarding templates for SEs. Target: 25 external beta customers.
- Phase GA (6-8 weeks): enable canary auto-apply and billing integration. Launch Starter and Scale SKUs.
- Phase Dedicated Support (Q3 post-GA): add manual import/export of suggestion policies for Dedicated and on-prem customers; plan for automated on-prem runner in a future release.

Pricing & packaging guidance (proposal):
- Pricing objectives: low entry cost, transparent ROI, predictable unit billing.
- Proposed SKUs:
  - Free (shadow-only): 0-3 evaluations/month per tenant.
  - Starter: $99/month + 0.2% of monthly inference spend; up to 50 evaluations and 100 auto-applies/month.
  - Scale: $799/month + 0.1% of monthly inference spend; higher quotas and SLA options.
  - Enterprise: negotiated with Dedicated support and professional services for policy transfer.
- Billing meters to implement: suggestions_evaluated (count), suggestions_autopplied (count), estimated_tokens_saved (tokens).

GTM / Sales enablement notes:
- Core pitch: "Reduce inference spend safely with explainable, one-click optimizations".
- Key objections & suggested responses:
  1) "We fear quality regressions" -> emphasize shadow-eval, small canaries, automatic rollback, and SE review.
  2) "We already tune batching in-house" -> highlight easy operationalization, continuous suggestions as traffic patterns change, and quantization recommendations validated by Applied ML.
  3) "How are we billed?" -> clear quota-based monthly subscriptions plus per-auto-apply meter; free shadow-only tier.

SE onboarding checklist (for first deploy):
1) Capture 48-72 hours of representative traffic via profiler.
2) Produce and review first suggestion set with customer; agree risk appetite and observability signals.
3) Enable shadow evaluation for 72 hours and inspect loss and latency deltas.
4) If acceptable, enable canary apply at 1% for 30 minutes and review results.

Support & incident playbook (short):
- If canary triggers rollback automatically, notify customer and SE owner; create incident and collect request/response traces and shadow evaluation artifacts.
- If auto-rollback fails, manual rollback CLI: redwood optimize-lite rollback --tenant <id> --apply_id <id>.
- Escalation: Applied ML for quality investigations; Runtime oncall for performance/latency regressions.

GA Release Notes (v1.0) Summary:
- Release date: 2026-05-10
- Status: GA (hosted)

title: dsid_5751f3afbd1c4998abec8d61e6377af7__adr-0127-tp-watchdog-and-abort-semantics.txt
text:
ADR-0127: Tensor-Parallel (TP) watchdog and abort semantics

## Summary
This ADR defines how Redwood Serving Runtime detects tensor-parallel (TP) stalls and how we abort safely when a stall is detected. The goal is to replace indefinite waits (which manifest as request hangs and GPU wedging) with controlled, observable, and retryable failure behavior.

This decision covers:
- What constitutes a TP “stall”
- Watchdog thresholds and default behavior
- Abort semantics (what we cancel, what we drain, what we restart)
- How errors surface to the API layer (HTTP + SDK semantics)
- Retry policy and routing/fallback expectations

## Status
**Accepted** (implemented behind a feature flag; staged rollout beginning Runtime 1.19).

## Context / Problem
Under sustained multi-GPU TP load (mixed prefill/decode, long context, bursty concurrency), we have observed failure modes where one or more TP ranks stop making progress. Symptoms include:
- Requests stuck in streaming with no tokens and no error
- GPU utilization dropping to ~0% while the process remains alive
- NCCL collective calls waiting indefinitely due to ordering mismatches or stream/event synchronization bugs
- Scheduler starvation (collectives delayed by prefill-heavy work) that can look like a “hang” at the request level

Indefinite waits are unacceptable in production because they:
- Inflate p99 latency and cause downstream timeouts
- Trigger autoscaling thrash and cascading retries
- Increase blast radius: a single wedged replica can accumulate queued work and degrade a whole pool

We need a bounded-time failure mode with clear signals and safe recovery.

## Decision
We will introduce a TP watchdog that detects lack of forward progress and triggers a **controlled abort + replica drain**. When the watchdog fires:
1) The in-flight request(s) on that replica are failed with a structured, retryable error.
2) The replica transitions to **DRAINING** (stop accepting new requests).
3) The orchestrator replaces the replica (or restarts the worker process depending on deployment mode).
4) Observability signals (metrics/logs/traces) are emitted with enough detail to classify the stall (compute vs comms vs scheduler).

We explicitly choose **drain/replace** over “attempt to recover in-process” because TP stall conditions frequently leave the process in an unknown state (e.g., CUDA stream waits, NCCL communicator deadlocks). Recovery attempts have historically resulted in partial wedging and repeated timeouts.

## Definitions
### “Progress”
Progress is defined as at least one of the following within a bounded window:
- **Decode iteration advance**: step counter increments for an active sequence
- **Collective completion**: expected NCCL collective(s) for the step complete
- **Per-rank heartbeat**: ranks report liveness and the same logical step index (or a bounded skew) while in TP execution

### “Stall”
A stall is declared when:
- A request is in TP execution and **no progress** occurs for longer than the configured timeout, AND
- The runtime confirms it is not simply “waiting for input” (e.g., client backpressure) or intentionally paused by backpressure controls.

We classify stall reason codes as:
- `comms_suspected`: collective(s) in-flight with no completion
- `scheduler_starvation_suspected`: runnable work exists but collectives are not being scheduled
- `compute_suspected`: kernels launched but no step increment / watchdog sees no forward progress
- `unknown`: insufficient signals

## Watchdog: scope and thresholds
### Scope
The watchdog applies to:
- TP decode steps (most common source of visible streaming hangs)
- TP prefill steps (particularly long-context prefill under contention)
- Explicit NCCL collective regions (if instrumented by collective counters)

The watchdog does not attempt to time every CUDA kernel. Instead, it checks higher-level invariants: “Are we moving to the next logical step?” and “Are collectives completing?”

### Configuration
The watchdog is controlled by feature flags and runtime config. Names are standardized to support alerting and on-call guidance:
- `tp_watchdog_enabled` (bool; default off until rollout completes)
- `tp_watchdog_decode_step_timeout_ms`
- `tp_watchdog_prefill_step_timeout_ms`
- `tp_watchdog_collective_timeout_ms`
- `tp_watchdog_action` (enum: `fail_request_and_drain` | `fail_request_only` (debug) )

### Default timeouts (initial)
Defaults are conservative to avoid false positives; they will be tuned per model/hardware based on perf-canary data.

| Workload | Default timeout | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Decode step timeout | 15,000 ms | Bound: should exceed expected p99 decode-step under peak contention + margin |
| Prefill step timeout | 60,000 ms | Prefill is bursty and can be long for long-context prompts |
| Collective timeout | 10,000 ms | Used when we can confirm a collective is in-flight |

Notes:
- These are **per-step** timeouts, not per-request. A long request can legitimately run longer than these totals as long as it makes step-by-step progress.
- If the scheduler is intentionally throttling, it must still produce heartbeats and advance step accounting; otherwise it may be flagged as starvation.

## Abort semantics (what happens when the watchdog fires)
### High-level behavior
When a stall is detected, we will:
1) Mark the replica as **unhealthy** for routing.
2) Fail affected in-flight requests with a retryable runtime error.
3) Drain the replica (no new requests accepted).
4) Trigger a controlled shutdown/restart path (deployment-dependent).

### In-flight request handling
- **Non-streaming requests**: return an error response immediately.
- **Streaming requests**: terminate the stream with a structured error event and close the connection.
- **Batching**: if multiple requests share the stalled TP step, all are failed together (consistent abort boundary).

### Replica lifecycle
- Transition state: `HEALTHY -> DRAINING (watchdog) -> TERMINATING`
- Emit a single drain event per replica per stall incident (rate-limited/deduped) to reduce alert noise.

### Resource cleanup
We do not rely on CUDA/NCCL cleanup completing successfully in the same process in order to serve new traffic. The drain/restart boundary is the safety line. Best-effort cleanup is attempted, but restart is authoritative.

## Error surfacing to API layer
### Contract
The API layer must receive a structured error that allows:
- Customer-visible diagnostics without exposing sensitive internals
- Retry/fallback decisions by Redwood routing
- Correlation to replica/rank and stall reason for support escalation

### Error shape (server-internal)
The runtime raises a canonical error type:
- `RuntimeTpStallError`

Required fields (names may differ by language, but semantics must match):
- `error_code`: `runtime_tp_stall`
- `stall_reason`: one of the reason codes above
- `retryable`: `true`
- `replica_id`, `tp_world_size`, `rank` (if applicable)
- `watchdog_timeout_ms`
- `in_flight_collectives` (if available)
- `request_id`

### HTTP / SDK behavior
- HTTP status: **503 Service Unavailable** (retryable infrastructure failure) or **504** only when the caller’s gateway timed out. Our preference is 503 when we detect the stall.
- Response body includes `code=runtime_tp_stall` and `retryable=true`.
- Streaming: the final chunk is an error frame (SDKs map to an exception) with `code=runtime_tp_stall`.

### Logging and trace correlation
- Structured log line on watchdog fire includes: `replica_id`, `stall_reason`, `last_progress_timestamp`, `step_id`, `collective_seqno` (if present).
- Trace span annotations: attach collective counters and stall metadata to the request span so that a single trace can show “where progress stopped”.

## Retry policy
### Redwood-internal retries
Routing behavior when `runtime_tp_stall` occurs:
- Prefer retry on a different replica in the same pool/cluster.
- If capacity is constrained, apply configured fallback policy (e.g., different region or compatible model variant) only where permitted by product policy.
- Do not retry on the same replica once it is DRAINING.

### Customer guidance (SDK and docs)
- The error is retryable. Clients should use exponential backoff with jitter.
- For **non-streaming** calls, recommend using an **idempotency key** (or Redwood request ID) to avoid double-charging or duplicated side effects where applicable.
- For **streaming**, retries may produce different partial outputs; clients should treat the stream as failed and restart the request if they can tolerate non-determinism.

### Retry limits
- Redwood routing layer: max 1 retry by default for this class of error to avoid amplification during partial outages.
- Dedicated deployments may tune this via policy; changes must be coordinated with SRE to avoid retry storms.

## Why this approach (vs alternatives)
### Considered alternatives
1) **Indefinite waits** (status quo)
   - Rejected: causes unbounded latency, invisible failure, and wider blast radius.
2) **In-process recovery** (attempt to reset NCCL communicators / clear CUDA streams)
   - Rejected for default behavior: high complexity, unreliable, and risks leaving the worker in a corrupted state.
3) **Kill -9 on timeout**
   - Rejected as primary approach: fast but loses structured diagnostics and can drop buffered logs/traces.

### Chosen approach benefits
- **Bounded failure**: request hangs become explicit errors within a known time.
- **Operationally safe**: drain/replace limits blast radius to a single replica.
- **Actionable signals**: stall reason codes + counters help isolate scheduler vs comms vs compute.
- **Compatible with fallbacks**: retryable error supports smart routing and customer-side resilience.

## Rollout plan
1) Ship instrumentation first (heartbeats, collective counters, stall reason tagging).
2) Enable watchdog in **canary** with high timeouts; validate no false positives.
3) Roll out to Dedicated clusters first (highest impact), then Hosted.
4) Tighten thresholds after perf-canary confirms safe margins.

Feature flags:
- Start with `tp_watchdog_enabled=false` globally.
- Enable per-cluster / per-account during canary.

Rollback:
- Disable `tp_watchdog_enabled`.
- If false positives are suspected, increase timeouts and collect traces/logs for analysis.

## Operational considerations
- Alerts should page only on sustained rates (e.g., multiple drain events across replicas) to avoid paging on isolated one-offs.
- Runbook must include:
  - How to confirm watchdog-fired vs customer/network timeout
  - What metrics to check (heartbeat gaps, collective in-flight counters, drain rate)
  - Safe mitigation steps (concurrency caps, disable CUDA graph capture if implicated, reduce batch size) before/while rolling out fixes

## Security / Compliance
- Error messages returned to customers must not include internal hostnames, GPU serials, or NCCL debug dumps.
- Detailed NCCL debugging (e.g., NCCL logs, env vars) must be gated and time-bounded; see incident procedures and internal support ticketing for enabling extra logs.

## Consequences / Follow-ups
- Expected increase in explicit 503s during true stall events, replacing silent hangs. This is an improvement for end-to-end reliability.
- Perf impact: watchdog checks are designed to be low overhead (step/heartbeat-based), but added instrumentation must be monitored.
- Follow-ups:
  - Tune thresholds per model/hardware based on TP stress suite results.
  - Ensure scheduler fairness changes reduce “starvation-suspected” stalls.
  - Improve NCCL error surfacing so comms stalls are attributed correctly.

## Appendix: Glossary
- **TP**: Tensor parallelism; a single model replica spans multiple GPUs.
- **Replica drain**: Stop admitting new work, let orchestrator replace/terminate the worker.
- **Collective**: NCCL operations like all-reduce/all-gather that require consistent ordering across ranks.

title: dsid_62f1a9cc6477452b8946d618690c2195__hybrid-deployment-packages-consumption-guidelines-2026-11-15.txt
text:
Hybrid Deployment Packages and Consumption Guidelines

Summary
-------
This document defines a set of hybrid deployment packages (hosted+demanded dedicated capacity+private overlay) and the recommended consumption/pricing guidelines for engineering, sales, and finance. It covers package definitions, billing primitives, quota semantics, migration/upgrade flows, acceptance criteria, and rollout milestones. The goal is to provide predictable economics for customers that mix Hosted API traffic with Reserved/Dedicated and Private nodes while preserving latency SLAs and predictable unit economics for Redwood.

Intended audience
------------------
- Product managers and pricing owners
- Solutions engineers and sales
- Billing & finance
- Infra and runtime engineering (capacity and runtime teams)
- Customer success / account teams for enterprise adoption

Motivation and background
-------------------------
Large customers routinely require a mixture of: (A) occasional burst traffic routed through Hosted API, (B) reserved Dedicated pools for baseline throughput, and (C) a Private deployment for sensitive data/regions. Today our SKU model treats these as separate product silos which complicates quoting and causes friction on migration paths. A hybrid packaging model aligns incentives, simplifies quoting, and enables smoother onboarding to Dedicated/Private while retaining predictable unit economics.

High-level goals
------------------
1. Provide 3 composable packages (Baseline, Burst, Private Overlay) that map to customer deployment patterns.
2. Ensure unit economics are preserved: per-token or per-embedding price floor for hosted traffic, committed-rate pricing for Dedicated, and flat subscription for Private control plane.
3. Define clear quota and failover semantics when customers exceed reserved capacity.
4. Provide migration and rollback procedures that minimize service disruption and billing disputes.
5. Ship with billing primitives that allow proration, usage breakouts by route/model, and credits for cache/quantization savings.

Package definitions (summary table)
----------------------------------
| Package name | Primary intent | Billing primitives | Included guarantees | Typical customer fit |
|-------------|----------------|--------------------|---------------------|----------------------|
| Baseline | Host most traffic via Hosted API; low friction | per-token pricing, rate limits, monthly invoice | 99.9% control-plane SLA, 95th percentile latency targets | Startups, mid-market teams |
| Reserved (Dedicated Commit) | Predictable throughput and isolation | monthly commit ($/vGPU-hour) + overage at discounted rate | Dedicated pool with throughput SLOs, priority capacity | High-throughput SaaS, regulated workloads |
| Private Overlay | Private control plane + optional on-prem agents | subscription + per-node license | VPC/VPN support, audit logs, custom KMS | Enterprise with compliance requirements |

Billing primitives and formulas
-------------------------------
- Hosted unit price: P_hosted ($ per 1k tokens)
- Reserved commit price: P_commit ($ per vGPU-hour committed)
- Reserved overage price: P_overage (discounted per-token or per-vGPU-hour beyond commit)
- Private subscription: S_private (flat monthly) + N_node * L_node (per-node license)

Example blended cost calculation (monthly)
1. Customer commits to 500 vGPU-hours at $X per vGPU-hour (Reserved baseline).
2. Expected monthly hosted traffic: 200M tokens @ P_hosted.
3. Observed cache savings: 12% of token cost (credited).
4. Overage (burst) consumed: 120 vGPU-hours charged at P_overage.
Total = (500 * P_commit) + (200M/1k * P_hosted * (1 - 0.12)) + (120 * P_overage) + S_private (if applicable).

Quota semantics and failover rules
----------------------------------
1. Baseline traffic is charged against Hosted quota first.
2. If customer has an active Reserved commit and the routing policy is set to "prefer-dedicated", traffic is routed to Dedicated until commit capacity is consumed.
3. When dedicated commit is exhausted within a billing period:
   a. If auto-burst enabled -> traffic continues to be served via Dedicated at P_overage up to configured burst cap.
   b. If auto-burst disabled -> traffic is routed to Hosted and invoiced at P_hosted.
4. Private Overlay customers may opt to enforce strict isolation (no failover to Hosted) or allow graceful fallback to Dedicated/Hosted depending on contract.

Configuration options (customer-facing)
--------------------------------------
- routing.preference: ["prefer-dedicated", "prefer-hosted", "isolate-private"]
- auto_burst: [true|false]
- burst_cap_hours: integer (max vGPU-hours per billing period)
- cache_credit_enabled: [true|false]

API/CLI example (billing config)
--------------------------------
```json
{
  "account_id": "acct_123",
  "billing_package": "hybrid-500-reserved",
  "routing": {
    "preference": "prefer-dedicated",
    "auto_burst": true,
    "burst_cap_hours": 200
  },
  "private_overlay": {
    "enabled": false
  }
}
```

Key product requirements (PRD-style acceptance items)
------------------------------------------------------
1. Billing: Backend emits line-items that break down costs by primitive (hosted_tokens, reserved_commit_hours, reserved_overage_hours, private_subscription). Line-items must be queryable via the Billing API.
2. Quota & routing: Control plane must evaluate routing.preference and route to runtime pools accordingly with deterministic tie-breakers.
3. Observability: Console must show per-route token counts, commit consumption live, cache credits applied, and projected month-end overage estimate.
4. Invoicing: Support proration for mid-period changes to commit size and immediate reconciliation for credits.
5. Contract language: Support isolation clauses where Private Overlay customers can opt-out of cross-surface failover.
6. Tests & safeguards: Synthetic load tests that validate billing alignment to observed commit consumption within 2% for 95% of test scenarios.

Design notes and engineering implications
----------------------------------------
- Runtime routing hooks: Add routing decision API to router that accepts a BillingProfile and routing.preference to make deterministic routing decisions.
- Metering: Route-level metering tags (route_id, model_variant, surface) must be included in every emitted metric/trace for billing aggregation.
- Cache credits: Implement a monthly ledger that converts observed cache/quantization savings into a negative line-item applied against hosted token usage.
- Capacity model: SRE must provide capacity guidelines to guarantee that a 20% overcommit buffer exists for Dedicated pools with auto-burst enabled.

Roadmap & milestones
---------------------
1. Q1 2027 (alpha): API primitives, billing line-item prototype, routing.preference flag, internal-only console view.
2. Q2 2027 (beta): Console UI for commit consumption, proration, auto-burst controls, basic invoice breakout.
3. Q3 2027 (general availability): Sales quoting flow, private overlay contract templates, GA billing export formats (CSV + BI connectors).

Rollout and sales enablement checklist
-------------------------------------
1. Complete billing contract templates and legal sign-off. (Owner: Finance & Legal)
2. Build quoting calculator and SFDC product packages. (Owner: GTM/Product)
3. Run two pilot customers for Reserved+Hosted hybrid (3 month pilots). (Owner: Solutions Eng)
4. Publish migration guides and training for Customer Success. (Owner: Customer Success & Docs)

Migration & upgrade flow (high level)
-------------------------------------
1. Discovery: Assess current usage patterns and recommend hybrid package via estimator.
2. Pilot commit: Customer purchases a small Reserved commit (30–90 days). Configure routing.preference to prefer-dedicated.
3. Observe: Monitor commit consumption; enable auto-burst for controlled ramp.
4. Scale: Increase commit or enable Private Overlay depending on compliance needs.
5. Rollback: If SLA or cost regression occurs, disable prefer-dedicated and route back to Hosted within 15 minutes.

Operational playbook (when commit consumption unexpected)
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Alert: Billing forecast shows projected commit exhaustion in <48 hours.
2. Action: Notify customer success and account owner; suggest increasing commit or enabling temporary burst cap.
3. If customer is private-isolate-true: Engage SRE & Solutions Eng to plan capacity.
4. Reconciliation: Apply cache credits/discounts if behavior was traced to config mismatch.

Acceptance criteria
--------------------
- Console displays live commit consumption within 60s latency of ingestion.
- Billing exports include route-level breakdowns and cache credit line-items.
- Pilot customers report no more than 1% increase in latency after switching to prefer-dedicated routing.

Ownership and stakeholders
--------------------------
- Product (packaging & pricing): Maya Chen
- Billing & Finance: Priya Nair
- Runtime & Routing API: Daniel Kim (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE / Capacity: Elena Rossi
- Sales & Solutions Eng: Arjun Patel
- Legal & Contracts: Thomas Weaver

Appendix A — Example customer scenarios
---------------------------------------
Scenario A: SaaS company with spiky traffic
- Needs: predictable monthly cost with ability to burst during launches.
- Recommended: Reserved 300 vGPU-hours commit + auto_burst=true, burst_cap_hours=150.
- Expected: ~30% unit cost reduction vs pure-hosted at scale.

Scenario B: Regulated enterprise migrating from on-prem model
- Needs: Private control plane + governed fallback to Redwood Dedicated in region.
- Recommended: Private Overlay subscription + a 100 vGPU-hours Dedicated commit for baseline.

Appendix B — Example billing line-item CSV schema
--------------------------------------------------
| invoice_id | account_id | period_start | period_end | line_type | quantity | unit | unit_price | amount | tags |
|------------|------------|--------------|------------|-----------|----------|------|------------|--------|------|
Example line_types: hosted_tokens, reserved_commit_hours, reserved_overage_hours, private_subscription, cache_credit

Appendix C — Quick CLI to preview cost (internal tool)
-------------------------------------------------------
$ redwood-cost-estimator --account acct_123 --commit-hours 500 --expected-tokens 200000000 --cache-savings 0.12
Estimated monthly: $XX,XXX (breakdown: commit=$YY,YYY hosted(after credits)=$ZZ,ZZZ overage=$A,AAA)

Notes and open questions
-------------------------
- Should we expose per-model quantization discounts as explicit line-items or fold them into cache credits? Tradeoff: visibility vs complexity.
- Pricing: finalize P_overage and burst caps with Finance to ensure margin targets are met for 95th percentile usage patterns.
- Compliance: Private Overlay customers may require dedicated billing accounts; confirm with Payments team.

Next steps
----------
1. Align with Billing & Finance on P_commit and P_overage floors by 2026-12-10.
2. Implement routing.preference flag and prototype metering tags (engineering spike) by 2027-01-15.
3. Schedule first pilot customer onboarding for Q1 2027.

References
----------
- Deployment surface and consumption implications (internal): /confluence/product-docs/product-overview/deployment-surface-consumption-pricing-implications-2026
- Token bundle & enterprise metering: /confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/token-bundle-flex-enterprise-metering-2026-08-20

title: dsid_6a99900d2a6a4a8c9ef62133e2798a11__rights-and-procurement-operations-handbook-2024.txt
text:
Rights and Procurement Operations Handbook

Summary

This handbook consolidates company-wide operational policies for access & permissions, change management that impacts authorization, data classification and handling, procurement and expense approval, vendor lifecycle management, and travel rules. It is intended for managers, finance, security, procurement partners, and people ops staff who execute or approve operational requests.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and third-party vendors interacting with company systems, purchasing on behalf of the company, or handling company data. Exceptions must be documented and approved by Finance + Security.

Definitions

- PO: Purchase Order
- IAM: Identity and Access Management
- SSO: Single Sign-On
- KMS: Key Management Service
- PII: Personally Identifiable Information

Ownership and escalation

- Policy owner: Finance-Legal (owner_team)
- Operational steward: Procurement Guild (finance operations)
- Security author for access rules: Security Engineering
- Travel coordinator: People Ops travel team
- Dispute/exception escalation: Head of Finance -> General Counsel

1) Access & Permissions

Goal: Provide least-privilege access with auditable requests, approvals, and automated deprovisioning.

Access request flow (standard):
1. Requestor creates an access request in the Access Portal (Confluence link: /access-portal).
2. Request includes justification, duration (if temporary), and list of systems or roles.
3. Manager approval (must be the requestor's direct manager).
4. Owner approval for the target resource (service owner or team oncall).
5. Security reviews if request includes elevated privileges (admin/root, production data access).
6. Provisioning executed via IAM automation within 2 business days.

Emergency access (break-glass):
1. Submit an urgent request via the PagerDuty channel and file a standard Access Portal entry within 24 hours.
2. Emergency access is time-limited to 8 hours by default and requires retrospective review.

Approval matrix (example):
| Role/request type | Manager approval | Resource owner | Security review | Notes |
|-------------------|------------------|----------------|-----------------|-------|
| Non-prod read-only | Required | Auto-approve for team-owned resources | No | Self-serve for common tools |
| Prod read-only | Required | Required | Optional | Logged for 90 days |
| Prod write/admin | Required | Required | Required | 2FA + justification |
| PII access | Required | Required | Required | Data handling training required |

Deprovisioning

- Access automatically removed 7 days after termination events in HR feed.
- Managers must review active accesses quarterly; security will flag stale roles older than 90 days.

2) Change Management (authorization-impacting changes)

Purpose: Ensure changes that affect permissions, network access, or data flows are evaluated for security and cost impact.

Change classification:
- Standard change: routine, pre-approved changes (e.g., scheduled key rotation)
- Major change: architecture work that modifies routing, IAM roles, or storage boundaries
- Emergency change: production-fix required to restore service

Procedure for major changes:
1. Submit a Change Request in the Change Registry with owner, roll-back plan, and test validation steps.
2. Security and Finance review risk and cost implication within 3 business days.
3. Schedule a change window; communicate to stakeholders 48 hours prior.
4. Post-change validation: run smoke tests, IAM audit, and cost delta report.

Rollback and canary policy:
- All major changes must include a rollback plan and at least 1-hour canary with health checks.
- If error budget impact exceeds 5% or cost delta >10% of baseline, rollback immediately.

Emergency changes:
- Follow the emergency change runbook: notify SRE, Security, and Finance within 1 hour of deployment.
- Complete a retrospective and RCA within 7 days.

3) Data Management

Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: information freely shareable (e.g., blog posts)
- INTERNAL: internal business info without PII or trade secrets
- CONFIDENTIAL: contains business-sensitive info, low-risk PII, internal roadmaps
- RESTRICTED: high-sensitivity PII, customer data, keys, source code

Handling rules (selected):
- RESTRICTED data must be stored in approved buckets with encryption-at-rest (KMS) and limited to roles granted via IAM groups.
- CONFIDENTIAL data may be exported only with Manager + Security approval.
- All PII access requires completion of Data Safety training in LMS every 12 months.

Retention and deletion

- Default retention: 2 years for INTERNAL; 5 years for CONFIDENTIAL; RESTRICTED retention per contract.
- Data deletion requests (e.g., GDPR/CCPA) are processed by Privacy Ops and must be completed within 30 days.

Audit and monitoring

- Logs: Access to RESTRICTED data requires detailed audit logs retained for 1 year.
- Weekly automated audits: Security runs a stale-permissions scan and reports to the owner.

4) Procurement and Expense Approvals

Principles: Centralize vendor spend visibility, enforce PO discipline, reduce invoice leakage.

Approval thresholds (effective policy):
- Expenses (employee spend):
  - <$250: auto-approved by manager via expense tool
  - $250 - $2,500: manager approval required; finance lead review for vendor-related costs
  - >$2,500 up to $25,000: Manager + Finance Director approval
  - >$25,000: Manager + Finance Director + CFO approval (PO required)
- Purchasing (vendor contracts):
  - <$5,000: Standard procurement form + approver (manager)
  - $5,000 - $50,000: PO required; Procurement review and Finance approval
  - >$50,000: Procurement + Legal + Finance Director + CFO sign-off; SLA review mandatory

Standard procurement workflow:
1. Requestor completes the Procurement Request form (link) and attaches Scope of Work and estimated budget.
2. Procurement team validates vendor, pricing, and conflict-of-interest disclosures.
3. Finance issues PO or routes to Legal for contract review if T&Cs deviate from template.
4. Procurement issues PO and confirms delivery milestones.

Invoice handling and 3-way match

- Preferred process: 3-way match (PO, invoice, receipt). If no PO, invoices must be tagged with an approved procurement request. Payment net-30 unless contract specifies otherwise.

Expense reimbursements (travel & misc):
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Per diem: $75 domestic, $150 international (overnight).
- Personal expenses are not reimbursable. Examples and edge cases are listed in the travel section.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding

Goals: Protect company data, ensure performance and contractual clarity.

Vendor lifecycle: Evaluate -> Contract -> Onboard -> Monitor -> Renew/Offboard

Minimal vendor vetting checklist (must be completed before onboarding):
- Business verification: company legal name, tax ID, contact points
- Security questionnaire: complete the standard vendor security assessment (link)
- Compliance evidence: SOC2 / ISO27001 where applicable or compensating controls documented
- Contract terms: Data processing addendum (DPA), liability caps, termination rights
- SLA: measurable uptime, incident response time, and escalation path

Onboarding steps:
1. Procurement creates vendor record and issues onboarding packet.
2. Security verifies network/data flows; if vendor requires network access, put in a separate VPC with least-privilege routes.
3. Access credentials for vendor agents must be time-bound and tied to vendor employee lists.

Monitoring and renewal:
- Quarterly vendor performance reviews for vendors with >$10k/month spend or who handle RESTRICTED data.
- Offboarding checklist: revoke credentials, archive vendor data, confirm deletion per DPA or contract terms.

6) Travel Policy (selected highlights)

Booking and approvals:
- All international travel requires manager approval and Finance pre-clearance for trips >5 days.
- Use corporate travel provider for bookings where available. Exceptions require manager note.

Allowed classes and per-diem:
- Domestic coach for flights <5 hours; premium economy for flights >5 hours with manager approval.
- Hotel: standard room; upgrades require manager approval and justification.
- Meals: per diem applies. Meals included in conferences must be deducted.

Safety and exceptions:
- Emergency contact list is maintained by People Ops and must be reviewed annually.
- For high-risk destinations, Travel Safety Assessment must be completed by People Ops + Security before booking.

7) Templates and Checklists (quick index)

Available templates (links to Confluence pages / document store):
- Procurement Request Form: /templates/procurement-request
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSAQ): /templates/vendor-security-questionnaire
- Standard Purchase Order (PO) template: /templates/po-template
- Travel Request & Approval form: /templates/travel-request
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA) template: /templates/dpa

Example: Procurement Request YAML (for automation)

---
requestor: "firstname.lastname@redwood.com"
project: "Feature X model hosting"
estimated_cost: "12000"
vendor: "Acme Inference Ltd"
justification: "Dedicated capacity for model benchmarking"
required_by: "2024-05-15"
items:
  - sku: "gpu-reservation-monthly"
    qty: 1
    unit_cost: 12000
---

8) Compliance and Evidence

- Finance maintains procurement trail for audit (POs, invoices, approvals) for minimum 7 years.
- Security maintains evidence for vendor assessments and IAM audits for 3 years (or as contract requires).

9) Exceptions and Amendments

- Exceptions: Documented exception requests are reviewed monthly by a cross-functional panel (Finance, Security, People Ops). Exceptions expire after 90 days unless renewed.
- Policy changes: Major amendments require Finance + Security + Legal sign-off and all-staff notification.

Contacts and escalation table

- Procurement team: procurement@redwood.com
- Finance approvals: approvals@redwood.com
- Security: security-ops@redwood.com
- People Ops (travel): travel@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com

Appendix A: Quick runbooks and commands

- List active IAM roles for a user (example CLI):
  aws iam list-attached-user-policies --user-name alice@example.com

- Revoke temporary credentials (example):
  ./access-portal revoke --user alice@example.com --reason "termination"

Appendix B: Quarterly review checklist

1. Procurement: review top 20 vendors by spend and confirm SLAs.
2. Security: run stale-privileges audit and confirm remedial actions.
3. Finance: reconcile POs vs invoices and identify exceptions.
4. People Ops: validate travel policy adherence and approve any rate changes.

Document history and approvals

- Drafted by: Maya Thompson (Finance-Legal) 2024-03-15
- Reviewed by: Liam O'Connor (Security), Priya Desai (Procurement), Jordan Alvarez (People Ops) 2024-04-02
- Published: 2024-05-01
- Last reviewed and amended for thresholds and retention updates: 2025-11-02

End of handbook.

title: dsid_75609dd3f1c9460081ee2f443d00f933__docs-site-content-lifecycle-and-local-preview-2026.txt
text:
docs-site-content-lifecycle-and-local-preview

Overview

Purpose: This page documents the content lifecycle, local preview workflow, and canonical fix process used by the Developer Experience team to keep SDK guides, API examples, quickstarts and docs-site content high-quality and production-ready. Use this as the single-source procedural reference for creating, reviewing, publishing, and maintaining developer-facing content.

Goals
- Reduce time from draft -> published to under 5 business days for small changes.
- Ensure all SDK and API example snippets are runnable and have CI coverage.
- Maintain a lightweight canonical-fix path for urgent support-driven fixes.
- Provide a reproducible local preview and linting workflow for contributors.

Scope
- Applies to: SDK guides, Quickstarts & templates, API examples, Docs-site operating procedures, and Canonical fixes for recurring support issues.
- Excludes: internal meeting notes, experimental research writeups (kept in Google Drive).

Ownership and Roles
- Author: creates the initial draft and is responsible for code sample correctness.
- Reviewer(s): at least one DX engineer and one product-owner reviewer for API/behavior changes.
- Docs Site Maintainer: owns CI checks, deploy pipeline, and rollback playbook. (Team: developer-experience/docs-site)
- Support Triage Lead: coordinates quick canonical fixes for critical customer-facing regressions.

Content Types and Metadata (frontmatter)
All docs in the docs-site repo must include a standardized frontmatter block. Key names and allowed values: 

- title: string
- description: short string (1–2 lines)
- sidebar_label: string
- sdk: one of [javascript, python, go, java, rest] or omitted
- language: one of [en-US, fr-FR, de-DE] (default en-US)
- product_area: one of [api, embeddings, streaming, console]
- api_examples: ["list of example ids"] (optional)
- last_updated_by: author name
- last_updated_at: YYYY-MM-DD
- canonical_fix_tag: freeform tag used for triage (optional)
- severity: one of [low, medium, high] (default low)

Example frontmatter (YAML-like):
---
title: Quickstart: Calls with the JavaScript SDK
description: Minimal example showing streaming + function calls
sdk: javascript
language: en-US
product_area: api
last_updated_by: Maya Chen
last_updated_at: 2025-02-10
---

Content Lifecycle (step-by-step)
1) Proposal / Intention (Owner creates a short proposal):
   - Create a short Confluence stub with the proposed scope, sample code language(s), and acceptance criteria. Add label `docs-proposal`.
2) Draft (Author produces full draft in the docs repo or as a Confluence draft):
   - Use the SDK quickstart template (see section "Templates & scaffolding").
   - Include runnable code blocks and tests where applicable.
3) Review (peer review + SME):
   - Request at least one DX and one Product/Model reviewer.
   - Run `yarn docs:lint` and `yarn docs:link-check` locally before requesting review.
4) CI & Staging (automated checks):
   - PR must pass: ESLint/remark-lint, link-checker, sample-code smoke tests, accessibility checks.
   - Docs Site Maintainer verifies staging preview and signs off.
5) Publish
   - Merge to main -> automatic deployment to https://docs.redwood.ai/staging.
   - After 24-hour smoke window, Docs Site Maintainer triggers production deploy.
6) Maintenance
   - Every document must have a `last_review` tag and be touched at least once per year.

Templates & Scaffolding
- Location: docs-repo/templates/quickstarts/ (monorepo path).
- Quickstart template includes: title, 1-paragraph intro, prerequisites, step-by-step commands, runnable code in 2 languages, test snippet, and troubleshooting section.

Minimal quickstart skeleton (example):

# Quickstart: Name
> Short one-liner about what this quickstart enables.

Prerequisites:
- Account with API key set in env var REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Node 18+ (or Python 3.10+)

Steps:
1) Install the SDK
   - JavaScript: `npm install @redwood/inference --save`
2) Run a simple call
   - JS snippet:

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rw-open-7b', prompt: 'Write a short haiku about devx.' });
console.log(res.output_text);
```

3) Validate locally with `node example.js`

Local Preview & Developer Workflow
Requirements: Node 18+, yarn, Docker (for link-check container).

Typical flow:
- git checkout -b docs/<short-topic>
- yarn install (root)
- cd docs-site && yarn && yarn start:dev

Commands (docs-site repo using Docusaurus v2):
- yarn start:dev           # local server with live reload (http://localhost:3000)
- yarn build:staging       # build static site (staging bundle)
- yarn docs:lint           # runs remark + eslint for MDX and code blocks
- yarn docs:format         # run prettier on MDX and code samples
- yarn docs:smoke-test     # run sample snippets (via node/pytest harness)
- docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/src linkchecker/linkchecker:latest http://localhost:3000

Notes on running the preview:
- If you change an SDK API example, update the smoke-test fixture under tests/docs-fixtures.
- Use `yarn docs:smoke-test --file=path/to/snippet` to validate a single snippet quickly.

CI Integration
- PR Checks: `docs-lint`, `link-check`, `snippet-smoke-tests`, `accessibility-check`
- If a snippet test fails, CI posts a comment with the failing command and reproducer.
- Docs CI postings include a staging preview URL that expires after 7 days.

Canonical Fix Process (for priority customer issues)
When Support or an SRE flags a customer-facing regression tied to documentation or example code (e.g., broken auth pattern, model-compat mismatch, streaming cancellation behavior), follow the canonical fix runbook: 
1) Create an Issue in the docs repo with label `canonical-fix` and severity tag.
2) Assign to Support Triage Lead and add immediate owner.
3) Hotfix steps (author + maintainer):
   - Make minimal change that corrects customer impact (usually code snippet or short warning).
   - Run `yarn docs:smoke-test --fast` and `yarn docs:lint` locally.
   - Open PR with `canonical-fix` in title, request expedited review (24-hour SLA for high severity).
   - Once merged, Docs Site Maintainer triggers an expedited deploy to production and updates the issue.
4) Postmortem: If the problem was severe or repeated, create a short incident note and attach to the issue.

Common support-to-docs canonical examples
- Auth errors: missing or mis-ordered header examples (fix: show exact header order and example curl).
- Streaming cancellations: examples that omit `signal`/AbortController usage (fix: add minimal cancellation snippet).
- Embeddings mismatch: examples that use the wrong vector dims for a model (fix: add model-specific dims table).
- SDK version mismatches: quickstart referencing deprecated constructors (fix: update to current constructor and add deprecation note).

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fix Templates
- Template PR title: `[canonical-fix][high] Fix auth header example in quickstart - <short-desc>`
- PR body checklist:
  - [ ] Reproduced issue locally
  - [ ] Added/fixed code snippet and smoke test
  - [ ] Ran `yarn docs:lint` and `yarn docs:smoke-test`
  - [ ] Added link to support ticket or issue number

Sample CLI snippet showing correct curl auth (include exact spacing and header):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
  -d '{"model":"rw-open-7b","input":"Hello world"}'

Monitoring & Post-deploy Checks
- After any publish, the Docs Site Maintainer verifies:
  - Staging preview is accessible and smoke tests pass for 24 hours.
  - Production pages are reachable (HTTP 200) and no new 404s introduced.
  - Page-level analytics show expected traffic; anomalous spikes trigger investigation.

Rollback & Emergency Procedure
- If a production deploy introduces a regression:
  1) Docs Site Maintainer reverts the merge commit and triggers deploy.
  2) Notify #docs-channel and assigned reviewers.
  3) Open a postmortem if rollback is followed by an incident.

Maintenance Cadence
- Quarterly content sweeps by product area owners.
- Annual review for all quickstarts and SDK guides to ensure language parity across SDKs.

Appendix: Troubleshooting checklist for contributors
- Snippets failing smoke-test: confirm the local env var REDWOOD_API_KEY is valid and model name is correct.
- Link checker failing: run link-checker locally and fix absolute vs relative links. Prefer relative links for internal pages.
- Formatting diffs: run `yarn docs:format` before committing.

Related resources
- Docs site repo README (internal): docs-repo/README.md
- SDK smoke-test harness: tests/docs-smoke/README.md
- Canonical fix tracker board: Jira board 'DOCS-CANONICAL'

Contact
- For CI or deploy issues: @docs-site-maintainer (team alias)
- For canonical-fix triage: Support Triage Lead (see team roster)

Last updated: 2025-02-10 by Maya Chen

title: dsid_926174fc4900408c89c98abde46b7225__first-production-launch-checklist-template.txt
text:
First Production Launch Checklist (Canonical Template)

## Purpose
This page defines the **canonical step catalog** for the “Guided onboarding + First Production Launch” checklist.

This template is the **single source of truth** for:
- Step IDs (stable identifiers used by Console + progress service + telemetry)
- Step ordering, dependencies, and completion criteria
- Deep links in the Redwood Console
- Canonical docs + quickstart/example links (with language parity expectations)

This template is used in:
- **Redwood Console** checklist UI
- **Docs** (mirrors the same steps and order)
- **Support playbooks** (triage by step state)

---

## Template versioning and change control
**Template version:** 1.0

**Rules**
1. **Step IDs are immutable.** Do not reuse an ID for a different meaning.
2. Any change that affects completion logic (criteria or event mapping) requires review from:
   - DevEx (Docs/Quickstarts): Wei Chen / Elliot Price
   - Console PM/Eng: Marissa Cole / Dylan Brooks
   - Telemetry: Logan Wright
   - Support enablement: Dev Patel
3. Backward compatibility: existing tenants’ progress must not regress due to template edits.

**Update cadence**
- Minor copy/link changes: anytime (no code changes required).
- Criteria/event changes: batched; target 1–2 releases/month.

---

## Definitions
- **TTFS (Time to First Success):** elapsed time from tenant creation → first successful (2xx) Hosted API response for a supported endpoint.
- **TTFP (Time to First Production Traffic):** elapsed time from tenant creation → first request classified as production traffic per telemetry rules.

**Checklist step states**
- Not started: no evidence yet
- In progress: partial evidence (where applicable)
- Completed: acceptance criteria met
- Blocked: step cannot complete due to detected error state (Console may show guidance)

---

## Supported environments (MVP)
This template is authored for **Hosted API** onboarding (self-serve and sales-assisted). Dedicated/Private steps will be added later.

Supported language tracks for “Quickstart/Examples” links:
- Python
- TypeScript/Node
- Go
- cURL

Parity expectation: each step should have at least one canonical docs URL and at least two language tracks with working code samples by GA.

---

## Canonical step catalog (ordered)

### Step 1 — Create an API key
**Step ID:** ONB_API_KEY_CREATED

**Goal:** Ensure the developer has a valid key and knows where to rotate/revoke it.

**Acceptance criteria (completion):**
- At least one active API key exists for the tenant in the Console.

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/settings/api-keys

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/api-keys
- Quickstart (cURL): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/first-call#curl

**Common pitfalls to address in step detail UI:**
- Using the wrong environment variable name
- Copying a key with extra whitespace
- Using an org admin key in a restricted project context

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: api_key.created (source=console)

---

### Step 2 — Configure environment (SDK + env vars)
**Step ID:** ONB_ENV_CONFIGURED

**Goal:** Ensure the key is stored safely and the SDK can authenticate reliably.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Tenant has at least one successful authenticated request (2xx) OR explicit verification event from Console “Test connection”.

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/developer/quickstart

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/authentication#environment-variables
- Quickstart (Python): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/first-call#python
- Quickstart (TypeScript): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/first-call#typescript
- Quickstart (Go): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/first-call#go

**Notes:**
- Step detail should recommend using a secrets manager for production deployments.

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: auth.success (first occurrence)
- Optional client hint: sdk.initialized (no secrets; SDK name/version only)

---

### Step 3 — Make your first successful request (non-streaming)
**Step ID:** ONB_FIRST_2XX_REQUEST

**Goal:** Achieve TTFS and validate basic request/response.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- First 2xx response from one of: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank (Hosted API).

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/usage/requests (filtered to last 15 minutes)

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/first-request
- Example (TypeScript): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (folder: examples/first-request-ts)
- Example (Python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (folder: examples/first-request-py)

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: request.2xx.first

---

### Step 4 — Try streaming (and handle disconnects)
**Step ID:** ONB_STREAMING_ESTABLISHED

**Goal:** Validate streaming works end-to-end and the client behaves correctly on disconnect.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- At least one streaming response established (server confirms stream opened and at least one token chunk delivered).

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/developer/streaming

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/streaming
- Troubleshooting: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/streaming#disconnects
- Example (prod-ready): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (folder: examples/streaming-chat-prod-ready)

**Implementation guidance to surface in step detail:**
- Recommend read timeouts appropriate for long generations
- Recommend reconnect pattern (resume vs retry) and how to avoid duplicate side effects

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: streaming.opened.first
- Server-side event: streaming.chunk.sent.first

---

### Step 5 — Set production-safe timeouts and retries
**Step ID:** ONB_RETRIES_TIMEOUTS_CONFIGURED

**Goal:** Prevent common early-production failures (hanging requests, spiky error rates, retry storms).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Tenant has generated at least one request using an SDK client configured with recommended presets OR Console “Prod defaults acknowledged” action (for non-SDK use cases).

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/developer/production-defaults

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/production-readiness/timeouts-retries
- Python SDK guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/sdk/python#retries-timeouts
- TypeScript SDK guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/sdk/typescript#retries-timeouts
- Go SDK guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/sdk/go#retries-timeouts

**Recommended defaults (for docs + SDK presets):**
- Connect timeout: 2–5s
- Overall request timeout: 30–90s (non-streaming); streaming uses read timeout/keepalive guidance
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; retry on 429/408/409/5xx where safe
- Max attempts: 3–5 (cap total retry time)

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Client hint (preferred): sdk.retry_policy.enabled (no config values, only preset name)
- Server-side fallback: request.retry_observed (inferred; less reliable)

---

### Step 6 — Review usage and latency in the Console
**Step ID:** ONB_USAGE_DASHBOARD_VIEWED

**Goal:** Ensure the user knows where to see token usage, latency, and errors; reduce “usage dashboard mismatch” tickets.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- User visits usage dashboard page OR API call to /usage summary is made.

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/usage/overview

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/usage-and-billing/usage-dashboard
- Notes on data freshness: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/usage-and-billing#data-freshness

**Copy requirements (Console step detail):**
- Clearly state expected ingestion delay (e.g., “Usage may take up to ~5 minutes to fully reflect in dashboards.”)

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: console.page_view (page=usage_overview)

---

### Step 7 — Configure quotas and budget alerts
**Step ID:** ONB_QUOTAS_BUDGETS_SET

**Goal:** Prevent surprise spend and reduce 429 confusion by making limits explicit.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Tenant has set at least one of:
  - Monthly budget alert threshold, OR
  - Per-minute request/token limit policy, OR
  - Project-level quota override

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/settings/quotas-budgets

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/usage-and-billing/quotas-budgets
- Terraform snippet: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-terraform (path: examples/budget-alerts)

**Guidance to surface in step detail:**
- Explain how 429s work (quota vs rate limit vs concurrency)
- Recommend adding client-side backoff and server-side circuit-breakers

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: quotas.updated
- Server-side event: budgets.updated

---

### Step 8 — Pin a model version (avoid surprise changes)
**Step ID:** ONB_MODEL_PINNED

**Goal:** Stabilize production behavior by pinning a model and (where applicable) a revision.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Tenant has set a default model for the project and pinned to a specific version/revision OR explicitly acknowledged “floating model” risk.

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/models (then “Set default”)

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/models/model-versioning
- Quickstart section: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/production-readiness#model-pinning

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: model.default_set
- Server-side event: model.version_pinned

---

### Step 9 — Configure fallback policy (reliability under load)
**Step ID:** ONB_FALLBACK_POLICY_CONFIGURED

**Goal:** Ensure the application stays online during capacity constraints or model-specific incidents.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A fallback policy exists for at least one route (same family or compatible variant), OR the tenant acknowledges “no fallback” for the project.

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/routing/fallbacks

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/reliability/fallbacks
- Quickstart section: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstarts/production-readiness#fallback-policy

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: routing.fallback_policy.updated

---

### Step 10 — Add basic observability hooks (request IDs + tracing)
**Step ID:** ONB_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED

**Goal:** Make debugging first production incidents fast (correlate customer logs ↔ Redwood request IDs, add traces/metrics).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- At least one of:
  - Request ID propagation enabled in client logs, OR
  - Tracing headers enabled and seen by gateway, OR
  - Webhook/log export integration configured (if available)

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/observability/overview

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/observability/request-ids
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/observability/tracing
- Example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (folder: examples/observability-headers)

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: observability.request_id_seen
- Server-side event: observability.trace_context_seen

---

### Step 11 — Send first production traffic
**Step ID:** ONB_FIRST_PRODUCTION_TRAFFIC

**Goal:** Mark TTFP and ensure “go-live” is measurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- First request classified as production traffic according to telemetry rules (e.g., environment tag, header, allowlisted domain, or production API key).

**Recommended Console deep link:** /console/usage/requests?filter=production

**Docs / quickstarts:**
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/production/go-live
- Checklist doc (canonical): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/onboarding/first-production-launch-checklist

**Telemetry / progress evidence:**
- Server-side event: request.production.first
