    retry();
  } else if (err.code === 'DEPRECATED') {
    console.warn('Deprecated param used', err.meta.migration_guide);
    // still return the response if present, or surface as warning
  } else {
    throw err; // propagate to caller
  }
}
Appendix: JSON Schema (human-readable)
-------------------------------------
- error: object (required)
  - code: string (required)
  - message: string (required)
  - status: integer (required)
  - retryable: boolean (required)
  - request_id: string (required)
  - meta: object (optional)
  - documentation_url: string (optional)

Decision links and references
-----------------------------
- See ADRs on API evolution and fallback policies for related decisions.
- Aligns with observability SLI guidance for error tagging and tracing.

Ownership and next steps
------------------------
- Owner: API Platform (engineering).
- Action items: SDK maintainers to add typed exceptions (deadline 2025-05-15), infra team to emit new error envelope (canary by 2025-04-01), product to publish migration docs and examples.

Notes and rationale
-------------------
Typed error envelopes reduce fragmentation in client logic, make retry behavior explicit, and improve signal quality for SLOs and incident response. They intentionally separate human-facing messages from machine tokens to prevent brittle parsing.

Document history
----------------
- 2024-10-12: initial draft by Aisha Kapoor.
- 2024-12-03: added PARTIAL_RESPONSE handling and observability tags (reviewers: Michael Chen).
- 2025-03-05: published after cross-SDK compatibility validation.

title: dsid_ac95fcc92a424c6584336e7ba0aa8c4b__secure-offline-update-operator-toolkit-2026.txt
text:
Secure Offline Update & Operator Toolkit for On‑Prem Deployments

Purpose and scope

This page describes the Secure Offline Update & Operator Toolkit: a prescriptive playbook for preparing, delivering, validating, and rolling back offline (air-gapped) updates to Redwood Private runtime bundles. It combines packaging requirements, operator CLI recipes, safety windows, tests, telemetry guardrails, and a concise operator checklist for day‑2 field operations.

Audience

- Field operators performing on‑prem upgrades
- SREs who build offline update bundles
- Security/compliance reviewers validating update artifacts
- Solutions engineers responsible for customer runbooks

Goals

1. Ensure updates for private/on‑prem deployments are delivered with cryptographic provenance and verifiable rollback capability.
2. Provide operator-friendly commands and automation templates for safe staged rollouts in air‑gapped environments.
3. Define minimal telemetry and evidence artifacts required for post‑upgrade audits.

When to use this guide

- Customer environment is air‑gapped or uses restricted egress
- The update touches runtime or model artifacts (kernel, quantization tables, model binaries)
- Regulatory requirement mandates offline delivery and preserved evidence

Prerequisites

- Operator workstation with GPG/cosign and sha256sum installed
- Customer acceptance of maintenance window and SLA impact
- Signed operator access key (short‑lived) provisioned per customer operator account
- Secure physical or logically isolated bundle transfer channel (USB, controlled SCP jump-host, or couriered media)

Artifact & bundle format (required fields)

All offline bundles MUST be tarball archives with a deterministic layout and the following files (example manifest below):

- bundle.manifest.json — canonical manifest listing artifact names, semantic version, build id, and checksums (sha256)
- bundle.signatures.sig — cosign or GPG detached signatures for the manifest and each artifact
- runtime.tar.zst — runtime binaries & kernels
- models/ — folder containing model artifacts (quantization variant metadata included)
- migrations/ — optional state migration scripts with idempotency guarantees
- upgrade-plan.yaml — operator steps (precheck, apply, verify, rollback)
- verify-scripts/ — signed scripts used for post‑apply assertions (read‑only by default)

Example bundle.manifest.json (excerpt, replace placeholders):

{
  "bundle_version": "2026.02.1",
  "build_id": "runtimes-prod-20260210-94ab",
  "artifacts": [
    { "path": "runtime.tar.zst", "sha256": "<sha256hex>" },
    { "path": "models/llama-16b.q4.bin", "sha256": "<sha256hex>" }
  ],
  "upgrade_plan": "upgrade-plan.yaml"
}

Verification & signature model

- All bundles MUST be signed with the Redwood release key using cosign v2 or GPG (customer can provide their own attestation key in managed engagements).
- Operators must verify both the manifest signature and individual artifact checksums before ingest.

Commands (operator workstation examples)

# Verify manifest signature (cosign):
cosign verify-blob --key /keys/redwood-release.pub bundle.manifest.json bundle.signatures.sig

# Validate artifact checksums:
sha256sum -c bundle-checksums.txt  # bundle-checksums.txt generated from manifest

# Optional GPG verification: 
gpg --verify bundle.signatures.sig bundle.manifest.json

Safety window and planning

1. Schedule a maintenance window with customer and ensure at least one rollback slot reserved (30 minutes per tenant for rollback decision).
2. Run the preflight suite on a representative staging cluster offline snapshot (see preflight checklist).
3. Establish an operator hot path: primary operator, secondary operator, and on‑call SRE.

Preflight checklist (run before transfer to customer site)

- Build artifact deterministic re‑creation verified
- Smoke VM with runtime.tar.zst deployed and run smoke generator for 2,000 synthetic tokens
- Migration scripts validated in an isolated replica of the target KV cache
- Telemetry masks applied: PII redaction rules validated

Operator apply sequence (canonical steps)

1. Ingest stage — verify signatures and checksums, unpack to staging volume (read‑only by default).
2. Snapshot — take a full runtime snapshot (KV caches and ephemeral state) and export pointer to evidence bundle.
3. Dry‑run apply — run upgrade-plan.yaml in dry‑run mode (no state changes) and capture logs.
4. Apply — execute upgrade-plan.yaml with controlled concurrency (tenant groups of 10% first wave).
5. Verify — run verify-scripts/ and sampling queries (liveness, tail latency, model continuity).
6. Promote — remove read‑only flags and switch traffic to the new runtime variant.
7. Evidence archive — collect signed logs, verification artifacts, and store in customer evidence bucket.

Upgrade-plan.yaml pattern (illustrative fragment)

steps:
  - id: prechecks
    action: run
    script: verify-scripts/prechecks.sh
  - id: snapshot
    action: snapshot
    ttl: 72h
  - id: apply-runtime
    action: replace-files
    path: /opt/redwood/runtime
    concurrency: 10%
  - id: post-verify
    action: run
    script: verify-scripts/post-verify.sh
  - id: finalize
    action: promote

Canary & staged rollout policy

- Wave 0 (canary): 1 host or 0.5% traffic for 30 minutes. Must pass health checks and model-quality smoke set.
- Wave 1: 10% tenant groups for 60 minutes. Monitor tail p95/p99 latency and error budget.
- Wave 2: 50% for 2 hours.
- Wave 3: full capacity.

Abort conditions (automatic/manual)

- Any host with >1.5x historical p99 latency for 30s
- Error rate >0.5% for control routes or >1% for non‑control routes
- Model quality regression flagged by eval harness (precision drop exceeding 3% for critical prompts)

Rollback strategy

- Rollback MUST be possible within the defined maintenance window. Keep two full generations of runtime snapshots: pre‑upgrade and last‑known‑good.
- Rollback steps:
  1. Trigger rollback via operator CLI: rdu-rollback --snapshot <snapshot-id> --reason "auto|manual"
  2. Wait for raft/leader stabilization (monitor leader election logs)
  3. Run post‑rollback validations (see verification checklist)
  4. Archive rollback evidence and trigger incident creation if rollback was due to service regression

Operator CLI examples

# Ingest and verify bundle locally
rdu-ingest --bundle /media/bundle-2026.02.1.tar.zst --verify --key /keys/redwood-release.pub

# Dry run apply (no traffic switch)
rdu-apply --plan upgrade-plan.yaml --dry-run --output logs/dryrun-2026-02-15.log

# Apply to canary tenants
rdu-apply --plan upgrade-plan.yaml --wave canary --concurrency 1

# Rollback to snapshot
rdu-rollback --snapshot pre-upgrade-20260215 --reason "p99-regression-detected"

Verification checklist (post‑apply)

- Service health: all processes up, pod restarts = 0, disk pressure = none
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 within expected thresholds (p99 increase <10% allowed for bursty workloads)
- Model outputs: run 50 golden prompts and compare embedding similarity thresholds
- KV consistency: checksum of hot KV namespace unchanged (unless migration expected)
- Telemetry: evidence archive created and signed

Telemetry & privacy guidance

- Minimum telemetry for update evidence: signed syslogs for apply, verify script outputs, checksums, and bundle.manifest.json.
- Do NOT include raw customer prompts or embeddings in evidence; instead include hashed prompt identifiers and aggregated quality metrics.
- Sampling policy: 1% random sampling for human readable traces, 100% for error events.

Evidence package contents (required)

| Artifact | Purpose | Retention 
|---------|---------|---------
| bundle.manifest.json | Provenance | 2 years
| bundle.signatures.sig | Attestation | 2 years
| pre/post apply logs (signed) | Forensics | 1 year (hipaa/reg sites: 2 years)
| verify-scripts outputs | Validation | 1 year
| snapshot pointer ID | Rollback anchor | 90 days

Customer requirements (minimum acceptance contract)

1. Customer must provide an operator contact and maintenance window approval.
2. Customer provides an ingress channel (USB device or approved transfer host) and a defined acceptance test harness (list of golden prompts).
3. Customer agrees to evidence retention policy and provides KMS public key for attestation if required.

Field operator checklists (condensed)

Pre‑transfer (service owner):
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window and customer contact
- [ ] Generate evidence package template and preflight smoke results

At customer site (operator):
- [ ] Verify signatures and checksums
- [ ] Snapshot runtime state
- [ ] Dry‑run apply and collect logs
- [ ] Apply to canary, monitor for 30 minutes
- [ ] Escalate on abort conditions
- [ ] If safe, continue staged rollout
- [ ] Produce and sign evidence archive

Post‑operation (postmortem & archive):
- [ ] Upload evidence to customer evidence bucket
- [ ] Create short postmortem if rollback occurred
- [ ] Update bundle compatibility matrix if any manual patches were made

Operational roles and escalation

- Primary operator: executes the bundle ingestion and apply steps.
- Secondary operator: validates evidence and readiness.
- SRE on‑call: available for leader/raft issues and cross‑tenant regressions.

Common failure modes & mitigations

- Checksum mismatch: abort ingest, request re‑transfer, validate transport integrity
- Migration script error: run migration in isolated replica and apply hotfix; if urgent, rollback to snapshot
- Latency spike during canary: abort and roll back, escalate to SRE

Appendix: useful scripts and snippets

- generate-checksums.sh (example):
for f in runtime.tar.zst models/*; do sha256sum "$f" >> bundle-checksums.txt; done

- quick-verify.sh (example):
#!/bin/bash
set -e
cosign verify-blob --key /keys/redwood-release.pub bundle.manifest.json bundle.signatures.sig
sha256sum -c bundle-checksums.txt

Related pages

- Airgap packaging and day2 hardening (onprem-packaging) — follow for packaging hygiene.
- Operator sentinel & rollback procedures (upgrade-and-rollback) — for durable rollback evidence retention.

Glossary

- Evidence bundle: Signed archive containing manifest, signatures, logs, and verification outputs.
- Snapshot: Point‑in‑time exported runtime state used for rollback.

Feedback & revision history

- 2026-02-15 Jordan Patel — initial published version
- 2026-03-05 Reviewed and updated canary thresholds (reviewers: Ariela Gomez, Marcus Chen)

Contact

For questions or to request a private‑deploy readiness review, contact eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai or file an internal request via the operator‑tooling Slack channel.

title: dsid_62ccc5887b894e41abae8c8645a79141__rapid-escalation-routing-playbook-and-multi-audience-status-canvas-2026.txt
text:
Rapid escalation routing playbook and multi-audience status canvas

Overview

This playbook defines a fast, deterministic escalation routing layer for incidents that require cross-functional coordination, and a set of status templates mapped to audience lanes (customers, internal engineering, executive stakeholders, and security/legal). It is intended for on-call engineers, bridge operators, SREs, and customer success leads.

Scope
- Applies to incidents impacting: API availability, sustained latency / SLO regressions, data-plane integrity, and model-quality regressions with customer impact.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance (use Maintenance Status SOP) and low-impact alerts that fit the Operational Alert handbook.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-action for Sev-1 / Sev-2 to under 5 minutes.
- Provide clear, audience-tailored status messaging within 20 minutes of bridge creation.
- Ensure single-source-of-truth (bridge) and automatic routing to the right escalation lanes.

Key concepts
- Escalation lanes: pre-defined recipient groups (On-call Service Owner, Incident Engineering Pool, Customer Success Triage, Legal & Security standby, Executive Liaison).
- Routing policies: rules that map signals and tags to escalation lanes (signal = SLO breach, error spike, KV cache eviction storm, model-sampling drift).
- Bridge templates: standardized meeting/bridge artifacts pre-populated with incident metadata.
- Audience lanes (status canvas): distinct status message templates for Customers, Internal Eng, Executives, and Security.

Escalation routing matrix (high-level)
| Trigger | Primary lane | Fallback lane | Pager policy | Owner if no ack (10m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| API 5xx > 1% sustained 5m | On-call Service Owner | Incident Engineering Pool | Pager | Escalate to SRE lead |
| P95 latency > SLO x2 for 10m | On-call Service Owner | Incident Engineering Pool | Pager | Escalate to Platform SWE |
| KV cache evictions > threshold | Incident Engineering Pool | Storage team | Pager + Slack | Escalate to Runtime Lead |
| Model quality regression (regression-detector) | Model Onboarding Oncall | Applied ML | Email + Pager (if customer-facing) | ML Lead |

Routing policy implementation notes
- Signals are tagged at ingestion (kafka topic or alertmanager webhook) with metadata: service, region, model_tag, severity_guess, suspected_component.
- A central routing service (incident-router) evaluates rules and calls PagerDuty / Slack / Email based on lane policies.
- All escalations create a bridge document and populate the status canvas skeleton via API.

Runbook: first 10 minutes (operator checklist)
1) Acknowledge the primary pager (0–2 minutes). Record time in the bridge header.
2) Confirm customer impact using metrics dashboards: request-rate, 5xx, p95, error types (2–5 minutes).
3) If the outage meets Sev-1 or Sev-2 criteria, kick off the standard bridge (use bridge-template: rapid-escalation).
4) Tag the bridge with: severity, suspected-component, affected-regions, customer-facing-flag, and impacted-models.
5) Populate the Customer Status lane (see Status templates) and post first customer-facing note within 20 minutes.
6) Assign primary owner and secondary (backup) in the bridge.
7) Enable data collection hooks: capture request traces, logs slice, model-run inputs, and a copy of the most recent deployment manifest.

Bridge operator responsibilities
- Keep the bridge single-threaded: avoid parallel fragments. Use threads for deep-dive subteams.
- Maintain timeline entries (who did what, exact timestamps).
- Coordinate evidence snapshot uploads to the incident artifact store with labels for later postmortem indexing.
- Execute rollback/hotfix policies only with owner and SRE approval.

Audience-specific status canvas (templates)
- Customer lane (external, plain language):
  - Title: [Company] API Degraded — Region {region} — {short impact summary}
  - Body: "We are investigating increased errors for requests in {region}. Impact: customers may see timeouts or 5xx responses. We have an active incident (INC-{id}) and will post updates at least every 30 minutes. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff; set lower concurrency per client while we stabilize."
  - Tone: transparent, non-technical, action oriented.

- Internal Engineering lane (technical):
  - Title: [INC-{id}] {service} — Bridge open — {severity}
  - Body: include: service dashboards links, alert rules firing, recent deploy hashes, KV cache stats, stack traces, and temporary mitigation steps.
  - Tone: explicit about hypotheses, actions run, and next steps.

- Executive lane (briefing):
  - Title: Service Impact — High level summary (INC-{id})
  - Body: impact summary (customers affected estimate), business impact (percent of traffic), ETA for next update, mitigation in progress, and ask (need exec comms approval / sales outreach).
  - Tone: concise, risk-focused, no technical jargon.

- Security & Legal lane:
  - Title: Potential Data / Compliance Impact — {INC-{id}}
  - Body: short description of suspected scope, data classes at risk, immediate containment actions, and request for legal review.
  - Tone: factual and conservative.

Status cadence and templates
- Initial announcement: within 20 minutes of bridge creation. Use Customer lane template if customers affected.
- Regular updates: every 30 minutes while active, then every 60 minutes as stabilization proceeds.
- Post-incident notification: final status and mitigation summary within 24 hours.

Customer comm templates (examples)
- Initial (20m):
"We've detected elevated errors for requests to Redwood's Text Generation API in {region}. Our engineering team is actively investigating (INC-{id}). We will post an update within 30 minutes. If you need immediate support, contact your CSM or open a support ticket with priority 'Incident'."

- Follow-up (60m):
"Update on INC-{id}: Root cause hypothesis: {brief hypothesis}. Mitigation in progress: {actions}. Partial restoration observed in {region}; customers may see intermittent errors. Next update in 30 minutes."

- Resolution (final):
"INC-{id} resolved at {time}. Impact: {summary of impact and affected customers}. Root cause: {root cause}. Actions taken: {mitigation and long-term fixes planned}. If you experienced data loss or customer-facing regressions, contact support at [support@redwood.ai]."

Escalation decision ladder (who calls the execs / sales / legal)
1) If >5% traffic impacted for >30 minutes -> notify Sales Leadership and CSMs.
2) If PII/exfiltration suspected -> notify Security & Legal immediately (pager) and set confidentiality to restricted.
3) If SLA credit or regulatory report likely -> notify Finance & Legal and prepare remediation plan.

On-call rotations, handoffs and expectations
- Primary on-call model: blended SRE + product-service rotation. Typical cadence is 1 week for primary on-call, with 48h shadowing for new members.
- Handoff checklist (to be filled in the handoff channel):
  - Current open incidents and statuses.
  - Recent deploys (last 24h) and known risky changes.
  - Nightly synthetic job health and anomalies.
  - Any escalations to watch.
- Quiet-window policy: no non-emergency merges within the on-caller's first 24 hours and last 12 hours of a shift.

Game day exercises and drills
- Quarterly scenario: Multi-region latency spike with KV cache evaporation. Objectives: validate routing rules, status canvas timelines, and rollback procedures.
- Annual scenario: Model-quality regression affecting top-tier customers. Objectives: exercise product/machine-learning coordination, customer comms, and regulatory escalation.
- Scoring rubric: time-to-bridge, time-to-first-customer-note, time-to-restore, and postmortem action completion rate.

Post-incident process and template
- Within 48 hours: write a 1,000–1,500 word postmortem with the following sections: Summary, Timeline, Impact, Root Cause Analysis (5 whys), Mitigations (short-term and long-term), Action owners, and Customer communications chronology.
- Postmortem quality gate: at least one cross-functional reviewer from SRE, Product, and Customer Success.
- Action completion tracking: actions are tracked in the incident tracker board with due dates and owners; unresolved actions >90 days require escalation to the CTO for review.

Evidence & SLO artifact checklist
- Metrics and dashboards snapshot URLs (UTC timestamps).
- Alertmanager/Signal ingestion raw payloads.
- Request-level traces for 10 representative requests during the incident window.
- Deployment manifests and model checksum at time of incident.
- Customer impact table (tenant IDs, request volume, percent of traffic).

Rollback and hotfix authorization matrix
| Type | Who can authorize | Required approvals | Communication step |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Hotfix to config (non-code) | On-call Owner | SRE lead | Post to bridge + changelog |
| Code rollback (service) | Service Owner + SRE lead | Product Director | Notify Exec lane and customers if >10% traffic |
| Model rollback / hotpatch | Model Oncall + Applied ML lead | Security review if data-sensitive | Coordinate with CSMs before large customer-facing change |

Operational KPIs to track (post-incident)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev-1: target < 3 minutes.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) for Sev-1: target < 45 minutes.
- Customer update latency (time to first external message): target < 20 minutes.
- Postmortem completion within 72 hours: target 100% for Sev-1, 75% for Sev-2.

Ownership and contacts (examples)
| Responsibility | Team | Primary contact | Pager |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Incident bridge ops | SRE | oncall-bridge@redwood.ai | Pager: incident-ops |
| API service owner | Platform | api-owner@redwood.ai | Pager: api-service |
| Model incidents | Applied ML | ml-oncall@redwood.ai | Pager: ml-oncall |

Related runbooks and references
- See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-and-retention-playbook-2025
- See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/first-five-minutes-operator-cookbook-and-csr-scripts-2026
- See: Maintenance Status SOP (internal)

Appendices
A. Incident-router rule examples (pseudo-JSON)
  - "if alert.labels.component == 'kv-cache' AND alert.value.evictions > 100000 -> route: incident-engineering-pool"
B. Bridge template fields (minimum): Incident ID, Severity, Affected services, Primary owner, Timeline, Evidence links, Customer impact table.

Document ownership and updates
- Owned by: SRE Incident Response Guild.
- Review cadence: bi-annual or after any Sev-1 where MTTR > target.
- Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 (see reviewers above).


Playbook for deterministic escalation routing, audience-specific status templates, operator checklists, rotation and game-day guidance, and post-incident process tailored for multi-audience communications.

title: dsid_bd4cfd315c2143a0a1199056b9bc35be__regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024.txt
text:
Regression Impact Index and Prioritization Framework

Summary:
This document defines the Regression Impact Index (RII), a lightweight but rigorous scoring system that consolidates signal-level regressions into a single numeric index used to prioritize investigations and rollbacks. The RII is intended for use by the eval, inference, and SRE teams during post-deploy monitoring, regression triage, and model promotion decisions.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide a repeatable, explainable numeric index (0-100) that summarizes the business and technical impact of a model regression.
  - Standardize prioritization across teams and deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
  - Drive consistent action thresholds and SLAs for response.
- Non-goals:
  - Replace domain-specific human judgment. RII is a triage tool, not an absolute gate.
  - Replace longer-form root cause analysis (RCA) or formal postmortems.

Definitions:
- Regression: any measurable degradation in model behavior relative to the promoted baseline (accuracy, latency, cost, or safety).
- Slice: a workload segment defined by input type, customer cohort, locale, or prompt family.
- Signal: a concrete metric (e.g., top-1 accuracy on slice, median latency p50, error-rate).
- RII: weighted aggregate of normalized signal deltas mapped to a 0-100 index.

High-level RII formula (conceptual):
1) For each impacted slice compute normalized impact per-signal: N_s = clamp((observed - baseline) / baseline_scale_s, -3, +3)
2) Multiply N_s by signal weight W_s and slice exposure E_slice (fraction of traffic or business criticality)
3) Sum across signals and slices, map to [0,100] via sigmoid scaling and max cap

Example signals and default weights (configurable):
- Accuracy / Quality (weighted by 0.40) — primary quality metrics: top-1 / F1 / task-specific score
- Safety / Toxicity regressions (0.25) — policy matches, safety-sentinels triggered
- Latency p95 (0.15) — user-facing latency tail regressions
- Cost per-req (0.10) — token usage and compute shift regressions
- Availability / Error-rate (0.10) — 5xx or model-run-time errors

Default slice exposure tiers (examples):
- Tier A: core product traffic (exposure 1.0)
- Tier B: paid enterprise customers (exposure 0.8)
- Tier C: low-volume or synthetic probes (exposure 0.2)

Threshold table and recommended actions:
| RII range | Action | SLA | Owner | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-----|-------|-------|
| 0 - 9     | Monitor | 72h | Eval owner | Auto-ticket for tracking, low urgency |
| 10 - 29   | Investigate | 48h | Model owner + SRE | Run targeted probes, check canary logs |
| 30 - 59   | Triage + Mitigation | 12h | Oncall eval + SRE | Hotfix prompts, rate-limit, temporary fallback |
| 60 - 84   | Rollback candidate | 4h | Product + Oncall | Engage incident channel; consider immediate rollback |
| 85 - 100  | Critical incident | 1h | Incident commander | Full incident process, public comms if customer-facing |

Note: SLAs are business-guided. Individual customers or compliance classes may have stricter rules (see related private-deployment runbooks).

Computation details and normalization constants:
- Baseline selection: For promoted models, baseline is the last stable production snapshot. For blue/green or canary flows use the control arm snapshot.
- baseline_scale_s: signal-specific normalization constants tuned from historical variance. Example defaults: accuracy 0.02 (2pp), safety 0.5 (sentinel hit rate), latency p95 0.2 (relative), cost-per-req 0.15, error-rate 0.01.
- Clamp: extreme outliers are clipped at +/-3 to avoid one-off noise dominating RII.
- Sigmoid mapping: R = int(100 * sigmoid(0.5 * raw_score)) where raw_score is weighted sum. This compresses extremes while preserving ordering.

Operational workflow (step-by-step):
1) Alerting: telemetry pipelines calculate per-slice, per-signal deltas every 5 minutes and emit candidate regressions when a positive delta exceeds tuned thresholds.
2) Auto-RII calculation: a nightly and on-alert job recomputes RII; values are stored in the regression index table with metadata (slice_id, baseline_id, model_id, timewindow).
3) Triage queue: RII >= 10 opens a ticket in the triage board with automated prefilled diagnostics (seed prompts, top-n examples that changed, canary logs, KV-cache hit-rate).
4) Fast checks (0-2 hours): run the smoke probe harness, compare token distributions, and check quantization profile changes.
5) Decision: based on RII band and findings, perform mitigation (prompt patch, rate limit), rollback, or schedule RCA.
6) Post-action monitoring: RII must return below 10 for 24h after mitigation or rollback to close incident.

Runbook: quick play actions by RII band:
- RII 10-29 (Investigate):
  1. Pull top 50 changed responses for high-exposure slices.
  2. Run golden prompt suite (local evaluator) and compare embeddings/semantics.
  3. Check whether quantization profile or kernel change rolled in the same window.
  4. If suspect, pin traffic to previous model variant for affected slices.
- RII 30-59 (Mitigate):
  1. Apply short-term prompt scaffolding or guardrail to avoid worst-case responses.
  2. Apply autoscaler / routing policy to divert heavy traffic to dedicated capacity if load-induced.
  3. Reach out to product owners and schedule a hotfix deployment.
- RII >= 60 (Rollback candidate or incident):
  1. Execute rollback checklist (see section: Rollback checklist).
  2. Notify legal and CS if customer-affecting.
  3. Start RCA and capture snapshot of evaluation artifacts.

Rollback checklist (condensed):
1) Confirm baseline snapshot id and record runtime traces.
2) Pin routing rules in the control plane to baseline model for affected routes.
3) Scale baseline instances up while draining failing instances (graceful).
4) Validate smoke probes against production traffic mirror for 15 minutes.
5) Update status page and communicate to impacted stakeholders.

Telemetry and query examples (clickhouse / bigquery-like pseudocode):
- Compute slice-level accuracy delta:
  SELECT slice_id, AVG(task_score) as observed, baseline_score FROM evals.daily_scores WHERE model_id = "mX" GROUP BY slice_id;
- Aggregate exposure-weighted raw score (pseudo):
  WITH deltas AS (SELECT slice_id, signal, (observed - baseline)/baseline_scale as norm FROM ...)
  SELECT SUM(norm * weight * exposure) FROM deltas;

Example calculation (toy):
- Slice A (core product, exposure 1.0): accuracy drops from 0.86 to 0.80. baseline_scale_accuracy=0.02 -> N_acc=(0.80-0.86)/0.02=-3 (clamped). Weighted contribution = -3 * 0.40 * 1.0 = -1.20
- Slice B (enterprise, exposure 0.8): latency p95 increases by 30% (baseline_scale_latency=0.2) -> N_lat=(0.30)/0.2=1.5. Contribution = 1.5 * 0.15 * 0.8 = 0.18
- Raw sum = -1.02 -> sigmoid mapping -> RII ~ 12 (investigate band).

Governance and tuning:
- Quarterly review: owners must review weights, baseline choices, and normalization constants quarterly or after any major infra change (kernel update, quant pipeline revamp).
- Post-incident calibration: after any RII-triggered rollback, reconciliate the RII score vs. actual impact and adjust baseline_scale to reduce false positives/negatives.

Tooling and integrations checklist:
- Alerting: integrate with PagerDuty for RII >= 60, GitHub triage board for 10-59.
- Dashboards: per-model RII trend, top contributing slices, per-signal heatmap.
- Artifacts: persist top-200 changed prompts, seed-probe results, and evaluation artifacts to the regression bucket (S3 path convention).

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Eval team: compute signals, maintain slice definitions, own the RII calculation code.
- Serving/runtime team: provide kernel/quant release windows and flags; work mitigation routing.
- SRE/oncall: enforce SLAs, perform runbook steps for mitigation and rollback.
- Product: decision authority for roll-forward vs rollback when customer impact is ambiguous.

Privacy and compliance notes:
- Private deployments: for VPC/on-prem instances, RII computation might run locally and only metadata (not PII) should be reported upstream. See the private deployment telemetry charter for required anonymization.

Appendix A — Example JSON payload produced by the RII service (schema):
{
  "model_id": "mX",
  "baseline_id": "mX-20240401",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-31T14:12:00Z",
  "rii_score": "12",
  "contributions": ["sliceA:accuracy:-48", "sliceB:latency:18"],
  "artifacts": ["s3://redwood-regressions/mX/2025-10-31/top200.json"]
}

Appendix B — Calibration notes and historical false-positive mitigation:
- We observed a period (Q2 2024) where p95 volatility produced inflated RII values. Remedies applied: increase latency baseline_scale to 0.25 and require persistence across 3 windows before RII inclusion.
- For safety sentinels, prefer absolute deltas rather than relative when rates are low (example: sentinel hit-rate moving from 0.001 to 0.002 represents 100% relative but low absolute).

Contact and escalation matrix:
- Primary contacts: Sofia Martinez (eval lead), Ethan Park (serving lead).
- Emergency escalation: PagerDuty 'regression-critical' -> incident commander -> CTO on-call if public-facing.

Related documentation:
- See onboarding playbooks and shadow-run guidelines for running the probe harness in private/dedicated environments.
- Link: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/inference-readiness-eval-matrix-and-promotion-playbook-2026

Revision history:
- 2024-05-15 (S. Martinez): initial draft and proto RII formula.
- 2024-09-02: added latency normalization updates and tooling checklist.
- 2025-11-02: refined thresholds, expanded governance section, published.

title: dsid_50e1629ad060446da86cf9b9c28890bc__zero-trust-access-lifecycle-and-procurement-alignment-2024.txt
text:
Zero-Trust Access Lifecycle and Procurement Alignment — Playbook and Templates

Overview:

This playbook defines the Zero-Trust Access Lifecycle used at Redwood Inference and prescribes how access decisions, change management, data handling, procurement approvals, and vendor onboarding must align. The goal is to reduce blast radius, maintain auditable approvals, and ensure procurement decisions reflect operational security and least-privilege requirements.

Intended audience:
- Engineering managers and platform owners
- Security reviewers and compliance owners
- Finance and procurement teams
- People Ops for role updates and offboarding

Scope:
- All systems and services that store or process customer or internal data (hosted, dedicated, private)
- User access patterns (person, service account, CI/CD token)
- Hardware and software procurement that will be onboarded to production or private deployments

High-level Principles:
1) Least-Privilege by Default: every grant should be scoped to the minimum resource and time necessary.
2) Explicit Approval and Traceability: all requests require approver identity, business justification, and expiration.
3) Separation of Duties: procurement approvals and technical provisioning require independent reviewers.
4) Continuous Verification: periodic entitlement review, automated attestations where possible.
5) Procurement Security Gate: any vendor or purchase that touches customer data or infra must pass a security checklist before ordering.

Definitions (short):
- Entitlement: permission granted to a principal to access a resource.
- Owner: the team responsible for the resource and first point of contact for approvals.
- Sensitive Resource: any asset categorized as PII, IP, or production-infrastructure.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Requester: initiates access or procurement request with justification and expected duration.
- Resource Owner: validates technical need, selects grant scope, defines SRE/DR contact.
- Security Reviewer: evaluates the request for exposure, vendor risk, and compliance.
- Procurement/Finance Approver: verifies budget, contract terms, and vendor eligibility.
- People Ops: ensures role changes and terminations trigger entitlement revocation.

Access Lifecycle (Detailed Procedure):
1) Request Phase (Tooling: Access Portal / ServiceNow integration)
   - Requester populates: resource identifier (ARN or service name), purpose, least-privilege role, requested duration, and business justification.
   - Request must reference the ticket ID for any procurement tied to the access (e.g., new VM or external vendor account).

2) Approval Phase (two-step minimum for sensitive resources)
   - Step 1: Resource Owner approves scope & duration. For role-specific grants, the owner must select a pre-approved role template.
   - Step 2: Security Reviewer validates risk and selects compensating controls (MFA requirement, IP allowlist, monitoring hooks).
   - Step 3: Finance/Procurement approves if the access requires a new subscription, vendor account, or billed service.

3) Provisioning Phase (automation encouraged)
   - Automated provisioning preferred: IAM policy generated from templates, short-lived credentials, and audit log enablement.
   - Manual provisioning requires the provisioning engineer to attach the request ticket and record the change ID.

4) Active Use & Monitoring
   - All granted entitlements produce an audit event captured in the central logging pipeline.
   - Teams must create alerting for anomalous privilege elevation and high-volume data exports tied to newly-issued entitlements.

5) Expiration & Review
   - Every temporary grant is auto-expired at its requested end date.
   - Permanent grants must have an explicit quarterly attestation by the resource owner.
   - Annual entitlement review: owners receive the entitlement roster and must attest by the SLA date. Non-attested entitlements will be flagged for revocation.

6) Revocation & Offboarding
   - People Ops triggers revocation for terminated employees within 2 hours for production and 24 hours for non-prod.
   - For vendor contracts ending, the vendor account must be revoked and any keys rotated within 5 business days.

Change Management Intersection:
- Any change to access patterns that affects production or sensitive resources must follow the change control matrix: change category (minor/major/emergency), required approvers, rollout window, and backout plan.
- Example: Adding a new role that provides read access to billing data is a "major" change — requires Resource Owner, Security, and Finance signoff plus a canary rollout to a single user for 48 hours.
- Emergency changes (security patching, immediate revocation) must be recorded retroactively with documented justification and post-change review within 48 hours.

Procurement Alignment Checklist (applies pre-order):
- Does this purchase create new identities or vendor-managed accounts that will access Redwood infrastructure? If yes, attach vendor security checklist.
- Does the vendor process customer data? If yes, require contract clause with data processing addendum (DPA) and encryption requirements.
- Follow cost thresholds for approvals:
   - Under $5k: Team lead approval (documented in ticket).
   - $5k–$50k: Finance + Procurement approval.
   - >$50k: Finance + Procurement + VP-level approval and legal review.
- If hardware (GPU/servers) is procured for Dedicated or Private, include a network segmentation plan and KMS/HSM integration notes.

Vendor Security Gate (required artifacts before onboarding):
- Completed vendor security questionnaire and attestation to standards (ISO/ SOC / relevant checklist).
- Evidence of data handling controls: encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, logging retention.
- Contact matrix for incident response and escalation windows.
- Proof of required certifications or SOC2 reports if handling customer data.

Templates and Example Artifacts (copy/paste friendly fields):
1) Access Request Template (fields to capture in portal):
   - requester_name
   - team
   - resource_id (service/ARN)
   - access_role_template (link to role library)
   - justification (business)
   - desired_duration (ISO 8601)
   - linked_procurement_ticket (optional)
   - risk_mitigation (monitoring/MFA)

2) Procurement Fit-Gap Table (to be attached to vendor requests):
   - column headers: requirement | vendor_compliance | notes | evidence_link
   - sample rows: encryption-at-rest | yes/no | algorithm & key ownership | link-to-report

3) Approval Matrix (example):
   - team-lead: approve purchases <$5k and non-sensitive grants
   - procurement: approve purchases $5k–$50k and confirm vendor onboarding steps
   - finance-director: approve >$20k ongoing subscriptions
   - security: mandatory approver for any resource marked Sensitive or vendor-managed account
   - legal: mandatory for all customer-data-handling vendors and contracts >$50k

Operational Runbook Snippets (for oncall SREs):
- Revoke compromised key:
  1) Identify key ID and associated principals.
  2) Create revocation ticket in "Access Portal" referencing incident ID.
  3) Rotate any dependent keys, notify asset owner and security.
  4) Document actions and mark the incident for postmortem if exposure to customer data occurred.

- Emergency vendor account disablement:
  1) Security issues escalated to vendor-contact; disable account via vendor console or block IP ranges.
  2) Provision temporary alternative if service is essential; route traffic to fallback vendor if configured.
  3) Engage Legal and Procurement within 4 hours for contract remediation.

Data Management and Retention (short):
- Access decisions must reference the data classification for the resource. Data classification labels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Retention policies are applied at the dataset level; procurement of storage services requires agreeing to retention, deletion, and e-discovery terms.

Monitoring, Metrics & SLOs:
- Entitlement Review SLA: resource owners must attest to entitlements within 30 days of the attestation request (SLO 90%).
- Offboarding Revocation SLA: 2 hours for production accounts (SLO 99%), 24 hours for non-prod (SLO 95%).
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist Completion: 10 business days target from purchase approval to live onboarding (SLO 80%).

Audit and Evidence Collection:
- Every approval path must produce an immutable ticket with approver identity, timestamps, and justification.
- Security keeps 3 years of entitlement change logs for audit and internal review.

Example CLI snippets and IAM policy examples (illustrative):
- Short-lived token creation (example):
  $ accessctl issue --principal user:marcus --role read-only:billing --expires 72h --ticket TKT-12345

- Sample minimal IAM policy (text):
  {
    "Version": "2022-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["billing:GetInvoices"],
        "Resource": ["arn:redwood:billing:prod:::invoices/*"]
      }
    ]
  }

Rollout and Adoption Plan:
1) Q2 2024: Pilot with Platform and Finance teams for procurement gating and short-lived access.
2) Q3 2024: Enforce automated expirations and connector integrations with People Ops.
3) Q4 2024: Expand enforcement to Dedicated and Private deployment onboarding flows.
4) Ongoing: Quarterly training for managers and procurement; update templates based on audit feedback.

Escalation Paths & Contacts:
- Security Pager: sec-oncall@redwood.example (for immediate exposure)
- Procurement Ops: procurement@redwood.example
- People Ops: peopleops@redwood.example
- Security Owner (document owner): aisha.morgan@redwood.example

Related policies and references:
- RBAC and Authentication Standards (/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth)
- Procurement Playbook (see procurement team pages)
- Change Management Matrix (/confluence/policies-and-process/change-management-matrix)

Appendix: Example attestation email (one-click):
Subject: Quarterly Entitlement Attestation — Resource: billing-service
Body: Please confirm the list of active users and approve or mark for revocation. Link: <attestation-link>

Document maintenance:
- Owner (Security) will review annually or after any audit finding.
- Proposed changes appear as PRs in the policy repo; major updates require cross-functional signoff from Security, Finance, and People Ops.
