text:
Autoscaling Fidelity Marketplace PRD and Commercialization Playbook

Overview

This document defines the Product Requirements (PRD) and launch playbook for the Autoscaling Fidelity Marketplace — a product capability that automatically selects and scales response-fidelity variants (model variants, quantization levels, KV-cache profiles) against a commercial marketplace of fidelity SKUs. The feature couples runtime autoscaling decisions with commercial entitlements so customers can trade token-cost, latency, and quality dynamically.

Audience
- Product managers, commercial ops, pricing, engineering (serving runtime, platform), and solutions engineering.

Goals
- Provide a production-ready API and Console UX that allows tenants to:
  - Opt into an autoscaling fidelity marketplace with guardrails.
  - Define fidelity budgets and per-route fidelity SLAs.
  - Observe fidelity-driven economics in near-real-time and receive recommendations.
- Reduce average per-token cost for medium-to-high throughput tenants by 18–35% for conversational workloads without measurable quality regressions on customer-defined eval sets.
- Ensure autoscaling decisions respect latency SLOs and tenant isolation (no cross-tenant leaking of cost/variants).

Non-goals
- Not intended to replace manual model-pinning for customers requiring deterministic outputs.
- Not an open marketplace of third-party models in initial launch; variants are Redwood-verified and curated.

Key persona scenarios
1) SaaS product engineer: Wants to lower monthly inference bill while maintaining 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for interactive routes.
2) Platform lead at enterprise: Needs per-route fidelity SLAs and the ability to cap upstream spend per team.
3) Solutions engineer: Onboards customers to a fidelity budget and needs a reproducible rollout plan.

Functional requirements
- FR1: Autoscaler Policy Engine
  - Accepts per-route policy with fields: budget (credits/min), latency_SLO_ms, min_fidelity_variant, max_fidelity_variant, fallthrough_strategy (pin|downgrade|queue).
  - Computes per-request variant assignment and scaling action (promote/demote) in < 5ms on median decision path.
- FR2: Marketplace Catalog
  - Exposes curated fidelity SKUs with metadata: quality_score, expected_tokens_per_response_multiplier, average_latency_ms, quantization_level, recommended_use_cases.
- FR3: Entitlement and Billing Hooks
  - Integrates with billing to charge per-FU (fidelity unit) at time of request; supports committed and overage pricing.
- FR4: Telemetry and Explainability
  - Emit per-decision telemetry (variant_id, reason, pre/post estimated cost delta) to runtime telemetry stream and Console.
- FR5: Eval and Regression Capture
  - Shadow-eval mode captures outputs for a fraction of traffic for side-by-side quality checks; supports per-tenant promptsets.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR1: Isolation — decisions for one tenant must not use other tenants' telemetry as direct inputs (only aggregated market signals).
- NFR2: Availability — autoscaler control-plane must meet 99.95% uptime and 99.9% for marketplace reads.
- NFR3: Latency — additional decision latency must not increase tail response latency by more than 10ms p95 for interactive routes.
- NFR4: Cost accuracy — billing exposures from autoscaling must reconcile within 1 hour with offline metering.

Acceptance criteria
- AC1: End-to-end demo where a test tenant reduces average cost-per-token by >= 20% while keeping specified eval metrics within +-2% of baseline.
- AC2: Rollout automation (canary -> staged -> global) implemented in Console with rollback triggers: fidelity-regression-alert, cost-overrun-alert (>20% above budget), latency-SLO-breach (>5% violation).

Telemetry and success metrics
- Metrics to monitor (per-tenant and aggregated):
  - Average FU per request, FU variance, tokens-per-request, cost-per-1000-tokens.
  - Quality regression rate (eval set pass/fail), fidelity-promote/demote counts, decision latency distribution.
  - Business KPIs: average customer spend reduction, churn correlation, activation rate of autoscaler.

Console UX and admin flows
- New page: "Fidelity Marketplace" under Tenant Settings.
- Key screens:
  - Setup wizard (select routes, upload eval promptset, choose budget template).
  - Policy editor (JSON and guided form).
  - Live insights (heatmaps of variant usage, per-route cost waterfall).
  - Rollout control (canary %, rate, and automatic rollback toggles).

API contract (example)
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/fidelity-policies
- Request body (example):
  {
    "route_id": "chat.send",
    "budget_credits_per_min": 1200,
    "latency_slo_ms": 250,
    "min_variant": "gpt-lite-q4",
    "max_variant": "gpt-standard-fp16",
    "fallthrough": "downgrade",
    "canary": {"enabled": true, "initial_pct": 5}
  }

- Decision response sample (streamed to telemetry):
  {
    "request_id": "r_12345",
    "variant_assigned": "gpt-lite-q4",
    "reason": "budget_pressure",
    "estimated_cost_delta": "-0.0025"
  }

Pricing and packaging model (commercial options)
- Pricing design principles:
  - Keep per-FU pricing transparent and additive to baseline per-token pricing.
  - Offer committed FU bundles with sliding discounts and a preemptible warm-capacity option for batch-heavy workloads.

- Example packages (table):
  | SKU | Committed FUs / month | Typical target workload | Discount vs on-demand | Notes |
  | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
  | FM-Silver | 100k | Low-throughput dev & sandbox | 10% | On-demand overflow at standard FU price |
  | FM-Gold | 1M | Production interactive apps, 10–50 qps | 22% | Includes 1 dev support review & monthly recommendation report |
  | FM-Enterprise | 10M+ | High-throughput transactional apps | 35% | SLA-backed allocation & dedicated recommender hook |

Billing hooks and exposure controls
1) Per-route soft budget: automatic throttling and optional email alerts at 75/90/100% thresholds.
2) Hard spend caps: enforced via request rejection with clear error codes and mitigation guidance.
3) Reconciliation: daily FU usage rollups and an hourly delta stream for near-real-time charge surfaces.

Rollout plan (engineering + go-to-market)
1) Phase 0 (Q1) — Internal beta with Redwood teams: validate decision latency, billing reconciliation.
2) Phase 1 (Q2) — Closed private preview with 3 pilot customers from different segments (SaaS, marketplace, enterprise).
3) Phase 2 (Q3) — Public beta with Console UX and limited GA SKUs (Silver, Gold).
4) Phase 3 (Q4) — GA launch: Enterprise SKU, SLA contracts, partner enablement and documented playbooks for migration.

Launch playbook checklist (owner assignments included)
1. Product: final PRD sign-off, pricing SKUs defined (owner: Maya Chen).
2. Engineering: autoscaler policy engine implementation, telemetry pipeline, billing integration (owner: Rajesh Iyer).
3. SRE: capacity planning and chaos-testing runbook (owner: Emily Rios).
4. Solutions & SE: pilot onboarding templates, sample promptset evals (owner: Diego Alvarez).
5. Commercial: legal terms, SLA addendum and negotiated pricing templates (owner: Priya Singh).

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Quality regressions for long-tail prompts. Mitigation: mandatory shadow-eval capture and per-tenant rollback window; require quality pass before enterprise activation.
- Risk: Unexpected billing spikes from misconfigured policies. Mitigation: default soft budgets and enforced hard caps for first 30 days of tenant activation.
- Risk: Decision latency causing tail latency SLO breaches. Mitigation: fall back to pinned-variant path and provide telemetry-driven alerting.

Open questions (for product & pricing committee)
- Q1: Should committed FU bundles be refundable or transferable across routes?
- Q2: What price elasticity targets should we bake into the recommender for the first 6 months?

Ownership and next steps
- Primary product owner: Maya Chen.
- Engineering lead (serving/runtime): Rajesh Iyer.
- Commercial/GTN lead: Priya Singh.

Next immediate actions (within 2 weeks)
1) Align on pricing floor and reimbursement policy (commercial).
2) Finalize telemetry schema and event names (engineering + SRE).
3) Prepare three pilot customer invitations and onboarding templates (solutions).

Appendix: Example policy JSON (full schema)
- See attached policy-schema.json in repo: git.redwood/inference/policies/schemas (link: git.redwood/internal/policies/schemas/policy-schema.json).

References
- Variant marketplace design (design-specs/variant-price-signal-orchestrator).
- Fidelity staging SDK and eval playbook (requirements/prd-fidelity-staging-sdk-and-eval-playbook-2026-12-22).

Document history
- 2027-01-10: Drafted (Maya Chen).
- 2027-03-18: Engineering feasibility review added (Rajesh Iyer).
- 2027-07-22: Pricing committee notes incorporated (Priya Singh).
- 2027-11-01: Updated rollout plan and packaging (Maya Chen).

title: dsid_2dd9ded726a440d89eaebe4a4e7a6ca6__sli-deprecation-and-telemetry-archival-playbook-2026.txt
text:
SLI deprecation and telemetry archival playbook

Summary

This playbook describes a standardized process for retiring (deprecating) an SLI and archiving the associated telemetry and dashboards. It covers pre-deprecation validation, stakeholder approvals, data retention decisions, dashboard migration or removal, alert rule transitions, automation steps, and rollback procedures. The goal is to avoid data loss, preserve historical context for postmortems and audits, and keep our dashboard surface area manageable.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to SLIs owned by platform services and tenant-facing inference services.
- Covers metric series, dashboard panels, synthetic checks, alerting rules, and related runbooks.
- Does NOT change SLO contracts without explicit billing/sales/legal signoff. SLO change is a separate process linked in Related Pages.

Goals

1. Safely remove noisy or redundant SLIs within a 6-week window.
2. Archive telemetry (raw or rolled) to a cold storage tier for at least 1 year unless compliance requires longer.
3. Ensure dashboards and alerts are updated or removed with minimal operational disruption.
4. Keep an auditable trail of approvals and migration steps.

Key stakeholders and roles

- SLI Owner: service/team that created and owns the SLI (required for signoff).
- Platform Observability (Obs) Team: reviews archival plans, runs queries, manages long-term storage.
- Platform Operators: run the automation and update dashboards/alerts.
- Incident Response (IR): notified of retired SLIs that are part of incident playbooks.
- Compliance/Billing: consulted when retention affects legal or billing evidence.

Decision criteria for deprecation

Deprecation may proceed when one or more criteria are met:

- SLI duplicates another signal that is in active use and provides no incremental actionability.
- SLI has shown zero-variability (flatline) for >90 days and is not expected to change.
- Ownership is unknown after a 30 day ownership-sunsetting campaign.
- New consolidated SLI replaces the old one (migration plan exists).

Pre-deprecation checklist (required before deprecation window opens)

1. Confirm SLI identity and metric names (series keys): 
   - metrics example: service.response.latency.p50, service.kv_cache.hit_rate, platform.request.error_rate
2. Verify SLI usage: dashboards referencing panels, runbooks, alerting rules (list locations).
3. Query historical variability: provide 90-day, 1-year rolls (p50/p95/stddev). Attach sample queries.
4. Notify owners and consumers: email + #channel post with link, 14-day notice (minimum).
5. Propose retention target: active hot tier (30 days), warm tier (31-90 days), cold archive (>=91 days).
6. Create an Approval Issue (JIRA or internal tracker) with approvers: SLI Owner, Obs Lead, Platform Eng Manager.

Approval and scheduling

- Approvers must respond within 7 business days. Silence after 7 days does NOT imply approval; escalate to Platform Eng Manager.
- Approved deprecations are scheduled into a 6-week window with the following phases:
  Week 0: Announcement and snapshotting of dashboards/queries.
  Week 1–3: Data re-routing to archival pipeline and synthetic check adjustment.
  Week 4: Alert mute and dashboard hide-by-default.
  Week 5: Soft-delete metric ingestion (stop production writes).
  Week 6: Hard-archive and dashboard removal.

Detailed procedures

1) Inventory and snapshot dashboards

- Export all referenced dashboards (JSON) and save to: gitlab.com/redwood-observability/archives/<service>-sli-retirements.
- Collect exact panel IDs and queries. Example export CLI (Grafana):

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAFANA_TOKEN" https://grafana.redwood.internal/api/dashboards/uid/<UID> > dashboard-<UID>.json

- Record the mapping table: | dashboard_uid | panel_id | metric_series | consumer_playbook |
  Example row: | infra-latency-2025 | 7 | service.response.latency.p95 | infra/foreground-latency-playbook |

2) Archive telemetry pipeline

- For Prometheus metrics, create a rule that writes rollups to the long-term TSDB (Thanos/MetricStore) with retention tags. Example PromQL rollup: 

  - record: archived:service_response_latency_p95:30d
    expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, service_response_latency_seconds[30d])

- For tracing/trace-derived SLIs, export span aggregates to the cold bucket (S3 path: s3://redwood-obs-archives/<service>/sli-archives/YYYYMMDD).
- All archival writes must include labels: archived_by=platform-sli-deprecation, origin_sli=<original_metric_name>.

3) Alert transition plan

- Identify alert rules tied to the SLI. For each rule: 
  - Replace condition with equivalent on the new signal if one exists.
  - If no replacement exists, create a temporary alert that fires to a designated mailbox (not Ops channel) for 30 days before full removal.
  - Mute alerts at the policy layer during the soft-delete phase to avoid alert storms.

- Example Datadog rule change (pseudocode):

  FROM: avg(last_5m):anomalies(service.response.latency.p95, 'basic', 2, direction='above', alert_window='last_5m')
  TO:   avg(last_5m):anomalies(archived:service_response_latency_p95:30d, 'basic', 2, direction='above', alert_window='last_5m')

4) Dashboard lifecycle actions

- Week 4: Set panels to hidden_by_default=true and add an explanatory banner to the dashboard header: "This panel is scheduled for removal (see SLI deprecation playbook)."
- Week 6: Remove panels and delete dashboards only after a final sweep confirms no active runbook references.

5) Communicate changes and training

- Publish a consolidation note in #platform-observability with links to: Approval Issue, archived JSON, and sample queries.
- Update the Platform Oncall Runbook page with the new canonical signals and add a migration note where appropriate.
- Host a 30-minute Q&A with consumers in the first week after announcement.

Retention and compliance matrix

| Data type | Hot | Warm | Cold / Archive | Minimum retention | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Raw Prom metrics | 30d | 60d | S3 cold bucket | 365d | Compliance may require longer for audits |
| Rolled TSDB (1h) | 90d | 180d | S3 compressed store | 1095d | Useful for long-term trend analysis |
| Traces (aggregate) | 14d | 90d | S3 aggregate | 365d | Full traces retained only on request |

Automation snippets

- Archive rollup creation (example script):

  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  SERVICE=$1
  curl -X POST $PROMETHEUS_API/rules -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROM_RULE_TOKEN" -d '{"record":"archived:'$SERVICE'_p95:30d","expr":"quantile_over_time(0.95,'$SERVICE'_response_seconds[30d])"}'

- Dashboard export helper (python):

  import requests, os
  headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('GRAFANA_TOKEN') }"}
  r = requests.get(f"https://grafana.redwood.internal/api/dashboards/uid/{os.getenv('UID')}", headers=headers)
  open('dashboard.json','w').write(r.text)

Audit, rollback, and verification

- Verification steps after archival: 
  1. Confirm sample queries return expected archived rollup values.
  2. Confirm dashboard panels are hidden and linked references reported as resolved.
  3. Confirm alert rules are either migrated or set to mailbox-only.

- Rollback procedure (if issue detected during Week 5 or 6):
  1. Re-enable ingest for the metric (flip the soft-delete flag in the ingest gateway).
  2. Re-import dashboard JSON from the archive repo and unhide panels.
  3. Recreate alerts from exported definitions.
  4. Record the rollback in the Approval Issue and notify stakeholders.

Operational metrics to track success

- Number of SLIs retired per quarter. Target: 8–12.
- Mean time from approval to hard-archive. Target: <= 6 weeks.
- Percentage of retired SLIs with archived dashboards and rollback artifacts. Target: 100%.
- Incidents attributable to SLI removal. Target: 0 (investigate any occurrence).

Post-retirement retrospective cadence

- Two weeks after hard-archive, Obs Team runs a 60-minute retrospective with SLI Owner and Platform Operators to review any surprises, edge-cases, or gaps in the checklist.
- Outcomes recorded in the Approval Issue and this playbook is updated as needed.

Housekeeping and lifecycle policy

- All SLI deprecation events are logged under the git repo path and a single line summary is posted to the platform-ops monthly digest.
- Every 12 months the Obs Team runs an SLI audit to identify candidates for consolidation.

Appendix: quick lookup table

| Action | Responsible | Command / Location | SLA |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Export dashboards | Platform Operators | gitlab.com/redwood-observability/archives | 2 business days |
| Create archival rollup | Obs Team | Prometheus rules API | 3 business days |
| Mute alerts | Platform Operators | Datadog mute API | 1 business day |
| Final hard-archive | Obs Team | s3://redwood-obs-archives | 1 business day |

References

- SLI economics and mapping guide: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/sli-economics-mapping-and-runtime-decision-guide-2026
- Dashboard export standard: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dashboard-export-standards-2024
- Incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/incident-playbook-2025

Contact

For questions or to request exceptions, contact Observability (obs@redwood.ai) or open the Approval Issue template: templates/sli-deprecation-approval.

title: dsid_662978747ddb47338b62f7d87c391ca2__private-installation-docs-offline-bundles.txt
text:
Docs plan: Redwood Private offline bundles (signed) — public vs private docs, examples, and release alignment

## Purpose
This page defines the documentation plan for **Redwood Private offline bundles with cryptographic signing** (air-gapped / restricted networks). It clarifies:
- What content belongs in **public docs** vs **private/customer docs**
- The **minimum set of guides** required for pilots and GA
- Canonical **CLI examples** (installer preflight, bundle inspection, signature verification)
- How we keep docs **synchronized with shipped artifacts** (bundle layout, manifest schema, installer flags, error codes)

This is a DevEx/Docs plan (not the spec). Technical source-of-truth is in the engineering design/ADR pages linked above.

---

## Audience
Primary:
- Customer platform operators installing Redwood Private in **air-gapped** or **egress-restricted** environments
- Solutions Engineering / Professional Services supporting pilots
- Support engineers triaging install failures

Secondary:
- Security reviewers evaluating Redwood’s supply-chain controls (artifact signing, provenance, auditability)

---

## Documentation surfaces & access model
We will split content across three surfaces. The same content should not be duplicated unless required for access control; when duplicated, it must reference a single canonical source section.

### 1) Public docs (docs.redwoodinference.com)
**Goal:** Provide high-level understanding of offline install support and security posture without leaking customer-only operational details.
Include:
- One overview page: “Redwood Private deployment modes (Connected vs Offline/Air-gapped)”
- A short security statement: “Signed offline bundles: integrity + provenance”
- A minimal prerequisites list (high-level) and a pointer: “Contact Support/SE for the air-gapped install guide”

Exclude (keep private):
- Exact bundle directory layout, manifest schema details, and error-code taxonomy
- Break-glass override instructions and approval workflow
- Trust-store update procedures (key rotation) beyond a conceptual statement

### 2) Private/customer docs (Customer portal / authenticated docs)
**Goal:** Provide the step-by-step operational guide needed to install, upgrade, and troubleshoot offline.
Include:
- Full end-to-end air-gapped install and upgrade guides
- Offline bundle verification and inspection commands with expected output
- Troubleshooting (hash mismatch, unknown key, time skew) and log locations
- Key rotation / trust store update procedure (customer action steps)
- Support escalation and “what to collect” checklist

### 3) Internal-only docs (Confluence + internal runbooks)
**Goal:** Enable Support/SE/Engineering to execute pilots, triage incidents, and maintain release quality.
Include:
- Detailed runbooks and error taxonomy
- Break-glass process (policy, approvals, audit markers)
- Release checklist/gating and how docs are validated per release

---

## Information architecture (IA)
### Private/customer docs pages (must-have for GA)
1) **Overview: Offline bundles (signed) for Redwood Private**
   - What’s inside a bundle (high level)
   - What signing protects (manifest + referenced artifacts)
   - What verification does and when it runs (preflight, install, upgrade)

2) **Install: Air-gapped installation with signed bundles**
   - Prereqs (Kubernetes version range, container runtime, storage, CPU/RAM, OS tooling)
   - Transfer guidance (USB / secure media) and integrity preservation tips
   - Step-by-step install

3) **Preflight + Verify: Verify bundle signature and manifest before install**
   - Mandatory verification flow
   - Expected success output
   - Common failure messages → next steps

4) **Upgrade & rollback: Offline bundle upgrade flow**
   - Supported upgrade paths
   - Downgrade prevention behavior
   - Rollback procedure (and what is / isn’t allowed offline)

5) **Key rotation / Trust store updates (offline environments)**
   - How Redwood rotates signing keys
   - How customer updates the installer trust store offline
   - What happens if trust store is not updated (unknown key failure)

6) **Troubleshooting: Offline bundle verification failures**
   - Hash mismatch
   - Signature invalid/untrusted
   - Not-yet-valid / expired due to time skew
   - Bundle corruption due to unzip tooling or line ending conversion

7) **FAQ & common errors**
   - Error codes reference (stable identifiers)
   - “What logs do I send Support?”

### Public docs pages (minimal)
- “Redwood Private: Offline / air-gapped deployments (overview)”
- “Security: Signed offline bundles (integrity & provenance overview)”

### Internal-only pages (examples)
- “Support playbook: verification failures” (detailed triage + escalations)
- “Release docs checklist: signed bundles” (gating, validation steps)
- “Exception process: unsigned bundle hotfix (break-glass)”

---

## Canonical examples (CLI snippets)
**Note:** Examples below use proposed/implemented CLI patterns from the installer workstream. Docs must match the currently shipped installer. If flags or subcommands differ for a given release, the release notes and versioned docs must call that out explicitly.

### Bundle inspection (recommended first step)
Use when validating transfer media or when opening a support ticket.

Command:
- `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /mnt/media/redwood-private-offline-bundle-2026.01.0.tar.zst`

Expected output (example):
- Shows bundle version, build ID, manifest digest
- Shows signature verification result and signing key ID
- Prints a short artifact summary (charts/images/models/runtime)

### Explicit signature verification (preflight mode)
Command:
- `redwood-private-installer preflight --airgap --bundle /mnt/media/bundle.tar.zst --verify-only`

Expected behaviors:
- Fails closed if signature is invalid, manifest hash mismatch, or key is untrusted
- Prints remediation steps including log path

### Verify using an updated trust store (after key rotation)
Command:
- `redwood-private-installer preflight --airgap --bundle /mnt/media/bundle.tar.zst --trust-store /etc/redwood/trust/keys.json`

Docs must include:
- Trust store file location options (embedded default vs customer-supplied path)
- How to stage trust store updates offline

### Time skew diagnostics (air-gapped clusters)
When customer has inaccurate system time and signature validation fails due to validity window.

Command (diagnostic only; do not recommend as a permanent configuration):
- `redwood-private-installer preflight --airgap --bundle /mnt/media/bundle.tar.zst --time-override "2026-01-27T12:00:00Z"`

Docs must:
- Clearly label this as **diagnostic**
- Provide guidance on fixing system time source and rerunning verification normally

### Break-glass override (internal/private docs only)
Break-glass must never appear in public docs. In private docs, it should be behind an “Emergency only” section and require explicit warnings.

Command (example):
- `redwood-private-installer install --airgap --bundle /mnt/media/bundle.tar.zst --break-glass-allow-unsigned`

Docs requirements:
- Must include the approval path and required audit annotations
- Must state that Support may ask for additional evidence/logs and that the cluster may be marked “unsupported until remediated”

---

## Keeping docs aligned with release artifacts
### Principle
Docs should be treated as a **versioned interface** to a release artifact. If the installer behavior or bundle layout changes, docs must change in the same release train.

### Source-of-truth mapping
- Bundle layout + manifest fields: Engineering spec page (Confluence) and schema in repo
- Verification behaviors + error codes: Installer repo + docs error reference page
- Key rotation/trust store: Security/Release runbooks + customer-facing procedure

### Versioning strategy
- Customer docs should be **versioned by Redwood Private release** (e.g., 2026.01, 2026.02) when installer flags, manifests, or error codes change.
- Always provide:
  - “Latest” (default)
  - A version selector (at least last 3 minor releases)

### Release gating checklist (docs)
For every Redwood Private release that includes offline bundles:
1) Docs PR merged for:
   - Install (offline)
   - Verify/preflight
   - Upgrade/rollback
   - FAQ + error codes
2) Commands and outputs validated against the **release candidate** bundle:
   - Run `bundle inspect` against RC artifact and compare to docs
   - Validate at least one failure mode screenshot/output (tampered bundle) to ensure messages match
3) Confirm that the docs include the correct:
   - Minimum installer version required
   - Bundle version string format and build ID location
   - Trust store update instructions (if new key introduced)

Ownership:
- Docs owner: DevEx Docs (Elliot Price / Kira Thompson)
- Validation sign-off: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien) + Installer Eng (Ethan Park)
- Security wording review: Marcus Lin (esp. break-glass + trust root statements)

### Automation (recommended)
To prevent drift, we should generate docs fragments directly from build artifacts where feasible:
- Auto-generate a “Bundle contents summary” table from the manifest (artifact names + versions)
- Auto-sync error code reference from installer constants
- Publish checksums/signature metadata (read-only) as an appendix section

Implementation suggestions:
- Add a CI job in `redwood-docs` that pulls the RC manifest (or a fixture manifest checked in per release) and validates:
  - CLI snippets compile (command exists)
  - Referenced flags exist
  - Error codes referenced exist

---

## Content standards (tone, precision, and security)
### Tone and clarity
- Use direct, operator-focused language.
- Prefer “Do X, then Y” procedures with expected output and next steps.

### Security constraints
- Do not publish:
  - Internal key ceremony details
  - Internal signing infrastructure identifiers
  - Break-glass flags in public docs
  - Any internal-only log redaction policies or SIEM exporter internals

### Required doc elements for install/verify pages
Each operational page must include:
- Preconditions and “What you need on the air-gapped side”
- A “Verify before install” step (signature + manifest)
- Log locations
- A “What to send Support” checklist

---

## Draft outline for the private/customer “Air-gapped install” page
1) Overview
2) Requirements
3) Acquire the offline bundle (from Redwood)
4) Transfer to secure media
5) Verify bundle:
   - `bundle inspect`
   - `preflight --verify-only`
6) Install
7) Post-install validation
8) Troubleshooting

---

## Open questions / follow-ups
1) Finalize canonical command names and flags (installer): confirm `bundle inspect`, `preflight --verify-only`, trust store path flag.
2) Decide where the trust store lives by default (embedded vs file) and document exactly one recommended path for customers.
3) Confirm whether we expose signing key IDs / fingerprints in customer output and if yes, define the stable formatting (and redaction rules).
4) Decide how we present downgrade prevention behavior in customer docs (what is blocked vs allowed rollback steps).

Tracking:
- Docs execution ticket: ENG-4850 (Docs and runbooks for offline bundle verification)
- GA criteria: PM-894

---

## Appendix: quick reference tables
### What goes where
Public docs:
- Conceptual overview of offline install support
- High-level explanation of signed bundles

Private/customer docs:
- Step-by-step procedures, commands, expected output
- Troubleshooting, error codes, trust store updates

Internal Confluence:
- Runbooks, break-glass policy, release gating checklist, internal triage

### Definition of “aligned with release artifacts”
Docs are considered aligned when:
- Commands and flags match the shipped installer version
- Bundle layout references match the actual bundle
- Error codes/messages match installer output closely enough for Support scripts
- Release notes mention any required doc-visible behavior changes (new trust root, verification behavior changes)

title: dsid_541b51c4a3c04cd4b9155f773fc4c932__gatekeeper-spend-and-access-guidelines-2026.txt
text:
Gatekeeper: Spend, Access, and Change Guidelines

Overview

This document (the Gatekeeper guide) defines a single, cross-functional playbook for approving and executing access requests, infrastructure and configuration changes, procurement and expense flows, vendor onboarding, travel approvals, and basic data handling obligations. The goal is to reduce latency for routine operations while preserving security, compliance, and predictable financial control.

Scope and purpose

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and short-term vendors interacting with company systems and purchasing resources.
- Covers: access and permissions, change management for production and platform components, data classification and retention rules, procurement and expense approvals, vendor onboarding/offboarding, and travel booking/expense rules.
- Excludes: long-term contracts (handled by Legal), specialized classified-data projects (see security-and-compliance restricted policies).

Definitions and role matrix

- Requester: person initiating access/purchase/change/travel request.
- Approver: person or role responsible for authorizing the request per the matrix below.
- Gatekeeper: delegated finance or security role who performs final verification for spend over the threshold or high-risk access.

Approval matrix (summary)

- Low-risk access (read-only to non-sensitive services): Team Lead approves.
- Developer access to non-production infra: Team Lead + Infra Owner approves.
- Production access (any write/exec in prod): SRE Manager + Security Reviewer, must be time-bound.
- Purchases under $3,000: Requester’s Manager.
- Purchases $3,000–$50,000: Manager + Finance Gatekeeper.
- Purchases > $50,000: Manager + Finance Gatekeeper + Legal + VP sign-off.
- Travel (domestic): Manager approval. International travel or travel including high-risk jurisdictions: Manager + Security review.

Access and permissions

Principles

1. Least privilege by default: Only grant minimum permissions required to complete the task.
2. Temporary access: Production access must have an explicit expiry. Default expiry is 30 days; critical tasks should use a temporary jump-host or ephemeral role.
3. Justification and auditability: Every access grant must include a brief justification and an associated ticket id.

Process: requesting access

1. Open an Access Request in the central tools (Confluence link: /access-requests or via the corporate ServiceNow instance).
2. Include: system name, exact resource(s), justification, expected duration, and approval chain.
3. Team Lead performs initial review for completeness; infra or SRE owner validates technical scope.
4. Security performs elevated review for production or sensitive-data systems.

Break-glass and emergency access

- Emergency access is allowed only via the break-glass process: phone escalation to on-call SRE and Security, followed by a temporary token issuance documented in the incident ticket.
- All break-glass actions must be logged in the audit trail and reviewed within 48 hours by Security and the requester's manager.

Change management (config and infra changes)

Categories

- Low-risk: documentation updates, non-prod config updates.
- Medium-risk: schema migrations in staging, infra scaling operations.
- High-risk: production schema migrations, config changes affecting customer traffic or security posture.

Change workflow

1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the central tracker with rollforward and rollback plans and a risk assessment (low/med/high).
2. For medium/high risk, schedule a Change Window aligned to the SRE calendar and notify stakeholders 72 hours in advance.
3. Pre-change checklist (must be completed in the CR): test results, canary plan, monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds, communication plan, rollback steps.
4. Post-change validation: owner documents validation steps and marks the CR as complete within 24 hours.

SLOs and guardrails

- All high-risk changes require a postmortem within 7 days if they trigger any P1/P2 incident.
- Medium- and high-risk changes require a production readiness review at least 48 hours before the window.

Data management and classification

Classification table (summary)

| Classification | Examples | Encryption | Retention | Access control |
|----------------|----------|------------|-----------|----------------|
| Public | Marketing site content | Not required | 3 years | Open to all employees |
| Internal | Internal docs, non-sensitive logs | At rest recommended | 7 years | Team-level role-based |
| Confidential | Customer metadata, billing records | Mandatory (KMS) | 7 years | Justified, audited access |
| Restricted | PII, regulated customer data | Mandatory (KMS + HSM option) | Per contract/legal | Minimal, controlled by Security |

Key rules

- Use only company-approved storage locations for Confidential and Restricted data. Approval from Data Governance is required to create any new data store for Restricted data.
- Retention schedules are enforced via automated lifecycle policies where possible; manual retention overrides must have Governance approval.

Procurement and expenses

Principles

- Clear documentation for approvals, separation of duties, and cost center tagging are mandatory.
- Preferred vendors should be used where contracts exist. Use the vendor registry before initiating new procurement.

Quick purchase procedure (<= $3,000)

1. Submit a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement system with line-item detail and cost center.
2. Manager approves.
3. Finance Gatekeeper validates budget coding and issues a Purchase Order (PO) or credit card instruction.

Standard procurement (> $3,000)

1. Require at least one comparison quote or a vendor justification when a sole-source is used.
2. Finance Gatekeeper engages Legal for contract review when vendor terms exceed standard risk thresholds or include data processing.

Vendor onboarding and offboarding

Checklist for onboarding

- Complete Vendor Intake Form with security questionnaire.
- Confirm insurance and SOC2/ISO documentation as required by risk tier.
- Assign vendor account owner and access scope (principle of least privilege).
- Establish contract with data handling and termination clauses.
- Enter vendor into the vendor registry and tag by risk tier.

Offboarding steps

- Revoke all access and API keys within 24 hours of contract termination.
- Confirm deletion or return of data in accordance with contract.
- Close vendor accounts and archive the onboarding package in vendor registry.

Travel policies and expense rules

- Travel must be pre-approved through the corporate travel tool. Manager approval required for all trips.
- For international travel: Security review for region-specific advisories, and Finance approval for per-diem and budget impact.
- Standard booking class: economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business only with VP approval.
- Hotel: mid-range business hotels preferred; nightly rate caps are maintained in the expense system per region.

Expense reporting and reconciliation

- Submit expenses within 30 days of travel end. Include receipts for all items above $25.
- Cardholders must reconcile corporate card transactions weekly.
- Finance performs monthly audits of random expense reports (target 10% sample).

Templates and forms (where to find them)

- Access Request template: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change Request template (CR): /confluence/templates/change-request
- Purchase Request form: /confluence/templates/purchase-request
- Vendor Intake and Security Questionnaire: /confluence/templates/vendor-intake
- Travel pre-approval form: /confluence/templates/travel-request

Operational responsibilities and escalation

- Team Lead: first-level approver for low-risk actions, maintains access rosters.
- Security: final reviewer for restricted data and production access.
- Finance Gatekeeper: validates purchases, budget alignment, and vendor risk.
- Legal: mandatory for contract reviews that include non-standard terms or >$50k spend.
- SRE/Platform: approves production changes and defines rollback procedures.

Escalation path

1. Manager -> Gatekeeper (Finance/Security) -> Legal as required.
2. If timing is critical and approvals would block a business-critical activity, request an expedited review via the "gatekeeper-express" channel with explicit business justification; the Gatekeeper team target is 4 business hours for expedited approvals.

Monitoring, audits, and reporting

- All access grants, changes, and high-value purchases are logged in the central governance ledger. The ledger is exported monthly for reconciliation and audit.
- Quarterly reviews: Security and Finance run a joint audit of production access lists, vendor registry entries, and top 50 spenders.

Exceptions and risk acceptance

- Exception requests must be submitted to the Governance board with a compensating control plan and defined expiry (maximum 6 months).
- Risk acceptance for residual risks over $50k or critical customer impact must be signed by VP of Product and Legal.

Appendix: sample checklists

Purchase checklist (short)

- Business case attached
- Cost center tagged
- Manager approval recorded
- Vendor in registry or vendor justification provided
- Finance Gatekeeper approval for > $3k

Production change pre-flight checklist

- Tests passed in staging (include test ids)
- Canary plan defined and automated
- Monitoring and alerts validated
- Rollback steps tested
- Communications plan with incident contacts

Contact and ownership

- Finance Gatekeeper: Marcus Chen (finance-gatekeeper@redwood.ai)
- Security lead (policy contact): Aisha Reynolds (security-policies@redwood.ai)
- Data Governance: David Morales (data-governance@redwood.ai)

Revision history

- 2025-02-14: Initial publication by Priya Kapoor.
- 2025-09-10: Adjusted procurement thresholds and added vendor risk tiers.
- 2026-01-12: Added expedited approval path and updated retention table.

End of document

title: dsid_7b972e9b7ac847bba3f4145f56970301__private-deploy-playbook-vpc-onprem-2026.txt
text:
Private Deploy Playbook — VPC & On‑Prem Packaging

Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's recommended process for delivering private deployments that run inside customer VPCs or on-prem clusters. It covers network reference architecture, packaging and installer options, day-2 operational procedures, and deterministic upgrade + rollback steps. Use this document during pre-sales scoping, delivery planning, and handover to SRE/Customer Success.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, audit-friendly delivery path for VPC and on‑prem deployments.
- Reduce downtime and customer risk by standardizing upgrade and rollback flows.
- Clarify customer minimal requirements and sizing expectations.

Owners & contacts:
- Delivery lead: eng-private-deployments (primary) — eng-delivery@redwood.com
- Runtime owner: serving-runtime team — runtime-oncall@redwood.com
- Packaging & Installer: infra-systems team — packaging@redwood.com
- Escalation: SRE pager -> #sre-oncall -> oncall@redwood.com

1) Quick architecture overview
- Supported deployment modes in this playbook:
  - VPC-hosted: customer-managed cloud VPC with private subnets, NAT, and optional Transit Gateway.
  - On‑prem k8s: customer-managed Kubernetes (>=1.24), with node pools for GPU and CPU and private registry access.
  - Hybrid (edge+cloud): control plane in Redwood Private with data plane inside customer network.

2) Customer prerequisites checklist (must be validated before kickoff)
- Network & connectivity:
  - BGP/VPN or AWS Transit Gateway/VPN: IP connectivity between Redwood control plane and customer VPC.
  - CIDR ranges: allow list for control-plane IPs (see Appendix A).
  - DNS: internal DNS for service discovery or split-horizon DNS configured.
- Identity & secrets:
  - KMS/HSM request approved and keys provisioned for at-rest encryption.
  - Service account (cloud) or dedicated namespace (k8s) with least privilege.
- Compute & storage:
  - GPU types required (e.g., A10G, H100) and minimum counts.
  - Block storage performance: 6000 IOPS baseline for model shards.
- Security & compliance:
  - Audit log sink (S3/GCS/SMB) and retention policy; TLS mTLS between services required.

3) Reference network topology (VPC)
- Minimum design (three-tier):
  - Public subnet: NAT gateway, bastion (optional).
  - Private compute subnet: inference nodes, autoscaling groups, EKS worker nodes.
  - Data subnet: persistent model stores and cache nodes (prefer separate AZ placement).
- Routing and SLOs:
  - Cross-AZ latency target: <= 5ms for KV cache lookups within region.
  - Egress policing: limit burst bandwidth for model downloads during rollout to avoid bucket storms.

4) Packaging and installer options
- Option A — K8s Helm bundle (recommended for cloud & on-prem k8s):
  - Releases baked as chart: redwood-runtime, redwood-proxy, redwood-operator.
  - Bundle verifies cluster prerequisites during helm pre-checks.
  - Example install:
    - helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood.ai/charts
    - helm install redwood-base redwood/redwood-runtime -n redwood --create-namespace --set image.tag=2026.01.0
  - Supports values.yaml overrides for GPU nodeSelector, tolerations, and registry credentials.
- Option B — System packages + systemd (for air-gapped or non-k8s):
  - RPM/DEB installer with a declarative config at /etc/redwood/config.yaml
  - Systemd unit: redwood-runtime.service (restarts on failure, journald collection).
- Air-gap pattern:
  - Provide tarball of images and a signed manifest. Customer loads images into private registry and runs installer with --airgap flag.

5) Day‑2 operations (SRE checklist)
- Observability:
  - Ensure Prometheus scrape targets: redwood-metrics:9090, proxy:9100.
  - Logging: forward /var/log/redwood and container stdout to customer ELK/Datadog.
- Capacity management:
  - Autoscaling policy: target 70% GPU utilization; scale up policy 5–10 nodes at a time, cooldown 300s.
  - Warm pool: keep 10% reserved nodes for burst.
- Common runbook items (fast paths):
  1. Model cache saturation — clear LRU caches: curl -X POST https://redwood.local/admin/cache/evict
  2. High latency tail — verify CPU steal, inspect dmesg for OOM or GPU driver faults.
  3. Disk pressure — run offload: /usr/local/bin/redwood-offload --models older-than 30d

6) Upgrade procedure (standard k8s Helm path)
- Preconditions:
  - CI pipeline green for new tag; integration tests passed against staging.
  - Backup: snapshot model store and PVs, export Prometheus metrics for 48h window.
- Step-by-step:
  1. Announce maintenance window and enable read-only mode via API: POST /admin/maintenance {"mode":"drain"}.
  2. Increase replica counts of stateful services to maintain in-flight sessions (see scaling table below).
  3. Run helm upgrade with --atomic and --wait: helm upgrade redwood-base redwood/redwood-runtime -f production-values.yaml --timeout 20m
  4. Monitor SLOs for 30m. If errors exceed threshold (see rollback triggers below), initiate rollback.
- Rollback triggers:
  - 5xx rate > 2% for 10 minutes
  - Median latency increase > 100ms sustained for 15 minutes
  - Outage of >1 AZ in region

7) Rollback procedure (fast rollback)
- Fast rollback path (if helm used): helm rollback redwood-base <previous_revision> --wait --timeout 15m
- Manual rollback steps (if stateful changes applied):
  1. Revert configmap and secrets to previous version: kubectl apply -f previous-config.yaml
  2. Scale down new pods and scale up old replicas progressively (max surge = 20%).
  3. Validate session continuity: run smoke tests (smoke/run-smoke.sh) against /health endpoints.

8) Sizing & configuration reference (example table)
- Minimal production single-region (8k rps inference mix)
  - GPU nodes: 4 x A10G (16 vCPU, 64GB RAM)
  - CPU nodes: 3 x m5.xlarge for proxy & workers
  - Persisted storage: 5TB multi-AZ block store, 6k IOPS
- High‑availability production (50k rps)
  - GPU nodes: 16 x H100 (high-throughput)
  - CPU nodes: 12 x c6i.4xlarge
  - Cache layer: 3 x redis-cluster (m5.2xlarge)

9) Customer requirements library (pooled checklist for contracts)
- Contract-level items to capture in Statement of Work:
  - Network topology and IP allow-list
  - Dataset residency constraints and retention policies
  - Supported hardware list and replacement SLAs for failing GPUs
  - Backup frequency, restore RTO and RPO targets
  - Audit and log retention (minimum 1 year)

10) Troubleshooting appendix (common failure modes)
- GPU driver mismatch:
  - Symptom: CUDA initialization errors in redwood-runtime logs.
  - Fix: validate driver version and reinstall NVIDIA driver package matching runtime kernel.
- Model load hot-loop:
  - Symptom: repeated model load/unload and high S3 egress.
  - Fix: pin model versions, enable aggressive prefix cache, and throttle model download concurrency via config.download.max-concurrency=3

Appendix A — Allow-list & endpoints
- Control plane IPs (example, replace with per-customer list): 52.12.34.56/32, 34.56.78.90/32.
- API endpoints:
  - Control-plane: https://control.redwood.private
  - Metrics ingest: https://metrics-redwood.private:443

Appendix B — Sample values.yaml snippet (Helm)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  runtime.conf: |
    gpu.pool: a10g
    cache.size_gb: "256"
    metrics.enabled: "true"
  registry.credentials: "<base64-encoded>"

Change log & notes:

- 2025-06-03: Added air-gap installer pattern and amended storage sizing guidance (Marcus Lee).
