This document defines the cohort-driven eviction and fidelity-escalation strategy used by Redwood's serving runtime. It describes the architecture, kernel scheduling interactions, operational runbooks for incidents, and recommended profiling and benchmarking steps to validate policy changes. The guidance focuses on minimizing user-visible fidelity regressions while preserving SLOs for latency and availability.

Goals:
- Maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes while maximizing throughput on cost-sensitive routes.
- Provide deterministic, observable escalation paths: eviction -> quantized fallback -> reduced-context variant -> full degrade to lower-cost model.
- Ensure safe, auditable rollouts of eviction/fidelity policies with canaries and automated rollback triggers.

Scope and components referenced:
- runtime-orchestrator: policy engine that maps requests to cohorts and routes.
- gpu-dispatcher: low-level kernel invoker and per-GPU slot allocator.
- kvcache-manager: session/KV cache lifecycle controller and warmstart hints.
- kernel-allocator: chooses kernel variants (e.g., fused-attn, tiled-attn, quantized path).
- fidelity-adapter: component that surfaces fidelity presets (max_tokens, sampling_temperature, context_prune).

Traffic cohorting model:
1) Cohort definition: requests are classified at ingress by route, customer-tier, and latency-sensitivity tag. Example cohorts:
   - realtime-high (interactive chat, enterprise, latency < 150ms goal)
   - batch-cost (embeddings, background rerank, throughput preferred)
   - degraded-tolerant (internal test, can tolerate reduced fidelity)

2) Cohort weights and priorities: Each cohort has numeric priority and eviction weight configured in the policy manifest. Higher priority prevents eviction; weights are used for proportional eviction during pressure.

3) Signal inputs: Eviction decisions use a sliding window of signals: GPU memory pressure, kernel queue backlog, tail latency (>95th), KV cache hit rate, and burst concurrency. These signals are normalized per-pool and reported to the runtime-orchestrator.

Kernel scheduling policy interaction:
- Kernel selection: kernel-allocator maps model + request cohort -> kernel variant. Preference order (by default): fused-opt -> tiled-opt -> quantized-path -> CPU-fallback. The allocator can be overridden per-cohort.
- Batch slicing: gpu-dispatcher slices batches with priority-aware buckets; realtime-high requests form a minimum-preserve slice to keep latency low.
- Hedging and speculative kernels: For cohorts marked "hedge-enabled", the runtime may launch a lightweight quantized kernel after timeout T_hedge_ms (default 40ms). First response wins; other kernels are cancelled.

Eviction and fidelity escalation ladder:
The ladder is a deterministic sequence a request can experience under resource pressure. Configurable at service-level in the policy manifest.
1) Soft eviction: drop queued low-priority requests before dispatch. Threshold: queue_length > Q_soft_threshold (default 250).
2) KV cache eviction: eject less-recent contexts from cache (policy: LRU with cohort weights). Trigger when cache_mem_util > 0.78.
3) Quantized runtime path: switch kernel variant to 8-bit or 4-bit quantized execution for eligible models. Trigger on node_mem_pressure or sustained tail latency > 2x SLO.
4) Context trimming: fidelity-adapter prunes non-critical tokens (system prompts or long histories) based on prune_policy.
5) Model variant swap: route to a smaller model variant with explicit fidelity delta recorded.
6) Slow-path fallback: route to dedicated lower-cost pool with higher latency but preserved throughput.
7) Circuit-break to return HTTP 503 for clearly out-of-budget requests after grace period.

Operational thresholds (recommended defaults):
| Metric | Normal | Soft-evict | Hard-evict | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GPU mem util | < 0.72 | 0.72 - 0.88 | > 0.92 | Use averaged 30s window |
| Kernel queue length | < 80 | 80 - 250 | > 250 | Per-dispatcher queue |
| KV cache hit rate | > 0.85 | 0.85 - 0.70 | < 0.70 | Consider cohort-weighted eviction |
| 95th latency | < SLO | > 1.5x SLO | > 2.5x SLO | SLO defined per-route |

Example policy manifest (YAML):

'''yaml
service: text-gen
cohorts:
  realtime-high:
    priority: 100
    preserve_min_slots: 2
    hedging: true
  batch-cost:
    priority: 40
    preserve_min_slots: 0
eviction_policy:
  kv_cache_watermarks: [0.6, 0.78, 0.92]
  soft_queue_threshold: 250
  hard_queue_threshold: 500
fidelity_presets:
  quantized_path: true
  prune_percentage: 0.2
rollout:
  canary_percent: 5
  rollback_on: [95th_latency > 2xSLO, error_rate > 1%]
'''

Note: replace triple single-quotes with code block markers in Confluence when rendering.

Profiling and benchmarking guidance:
- Bench environment: use the runtime-operational-simulator to mirror cohort mix. Always run new policy tests in a shadow cluster before canary.
- Benchmark steps:
  1. Create synthetic corpus representative of median and tail sequences (use sequence-length histogram from production).
  2. Run three experiments: baseline (no eviction), policy-on shadow, policy-on canary.
  3. Collect metrics: per-cohort 50/95/99 latency, kernel utilization, kernel-switch rate, kvcache hit rate, end-to-end error rate, token-cost delta.
  4. Validate fidelity by automated evals (prompt-sets tied to feature flags) to detect regressions > 2% BLEU/ROUGE or domain-appropriate metric.

Profiling playbook snippets:
- To capture a latency fingerprint for a cohort:
  - Enable cohort-trace on runtime-orchestrator for 10 minutes.
  - Collect GPU dispatch traces (gpu-dispatcher: /opt/runtime/bin/trace --cohort realtime-high --duration 600).
  - Run kernel heatmap extraction: /opt/runtime/tools/kernel-heatmap --trace-file traces.bin --output heatmap.png

- Useful commands:
  - runtimectl policy diff --service text-gen --from v2 --to v3
  - kvcachectl evict --cohort batch-cost --dry-run
  - gpuutil top --pool gpu-pool-1 --interval 10s

Runbook: incident triage (fidelity escalations causing customer impact)
1) Detect: Alert threshold triggers (95th latency > 2xSLO for > 3 minutes) -> SEV2.
2) Initial diagnostics (first 10 min):
   a) Check runtime-orchestrator decision log: /var/log/orch/decisions.log for last 15 min.
   b) Confirm kernel-switch rates: query telemetry: metric kernel_variant_switch{service="text-gen"}[5m].
   c) Check kvcache hit-rate: /metrics/kvcache/hit_rate by cohort.
3) Mitigation steps (order matters):
   1. Increase realtime-high preserve_min_slots by 1 via runtimectl: runtimectl set-cohort --service text-gen --cohort realtime-high --preserve_min_slots 3
   2. If queue backlog persists, temporarily raise soft-evict_threshold to reduce queued load: runtimectl set-eviction --service text-gen --soft_queue_threshold 320
   3. If tail latency still bad, toggle hedging off for batch-cost cohorts to reduce cross-kernel contention: runtimectl set-cohort --service text-gen --cohort batch-cost --hedging false
   4. As a last resort, flip fidelity flag to disable quantized path for sensitive tenants: runtimectl set-fidelity --service text-gen --cohort enterprise --quantized_path false
4) Post-incident: attach traces, kernel heatmaps, and a table of pre/post metrics to the incident ticket. Schedule a retro within 72 hours.

Rollback and safe deployment practices:
- Canary plan: 5% traffic to canary for 30 minutes with automatic escalation to 25% then 100% if rollup checks pass.
- Rollback triggers (automated): 95th latency increase > 1.5x baseline AND user-facing error rate increase > 0.5% OR fidelity eval regression > 2% on baseline prompt set.
- Safety nets: maintain a hot-path fallback pool (dedicated nodes that preserve previous runtime flags) to route canary traffic if model swap oscillation is detected.

Compatibility and release notes considerations:
- Any change that affects kernel-allocator mappings must include a compatibility table for model variants and quantization support. Example YAML excerpt in release notes:
  - model: meta-llama-2-13b
    supported_kernels: [fused-opt, tiled-opt, 8bit-quant]
  - model: small-rerank-3b
    supported_kernels: [tiled-opt, 4bit-quant]

- Note kernel ABI changes in release notes: if kernel op signature changes, annotate which runtime and gpu-dispatcher versions are incompatible.

Observability and dashboards to maintain:
- cohort-slo-overview: per-cohort latency and error SLOs.
- kernel-variant-switch-rate: heatmap by service and cohort.
- kvcache-watermarks: rolling 5m/30m hit-rate and evictions by cohort.
- fidelity-eval-regressions: continuous evals mapped to feature flags and cohorts.

Ownership and contact list:
- Oncall escalation: runtime-sre oncall -> eng-serving-runtime primary -> product-owner for route.
- Primary owners:
  - runtime-orchestrator: Miguel Santos
  - gpu-dispatcher & kernel-allocator: Tomás Rivera
  - kvcache-manager: Priya Nair
  - fidelity-adapter: Lauren Chen (author)

Appendix: quick checklists
- Pre-deploy policy change:
  1. Run shadow simulation with production traffic mix.
  2. Run fidelity eval suite and verify no regression > 2%.
  3. Verify observability dashboards created and thresholded for new metrics.
  4. Create rollout manifest with canary_percent and rollback_on policies.

- Emergency immediate mitigation cheat sheet:
  - runtimectl set-service-mode --service text-gen --mode conserve-memory
  - runtimectl disable-hedging --service text-gen --cohort batch-cost
  - kvcachectl bulk-evict --pool pool-a --percentage 10

Related reading and links:
- See the runtime decision graph for example escalation flows.
- Refer to kernel-handshake-and-adaptive-fallback-patterns for kernel safety nets.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Lauren Chen.
- 2026-01-08: Added hedging and quantized path guidance after perf experiments.
- 2026-02-14: Finalized operational thresholds and incident runbook; marked published.

title: dsid_2f06a42b8a4c41da863601a9a7c17b5b__oncall-cadence-game-day-scripting-and-customer-signal-protocol-2026.txt
text:
Oncall cadence, game-day scripting, and customer signal protocol

Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood’s operational cadence for oncall rotations, provides ready-to-run game-day scripts for common failure modes, and standardizes the customer signal protocol used for status page and targeted customer notifications. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, service owners, and incident commanders.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for production degradations.
- Provide reproducible, testable game-day scenarios that validate end-to-end tooling (alerts, status page, comm templates).
- Ensure consistent, clear customer communication tied to objective signals.

Scope:
- Production services for Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private control-plane components.
- Incident types covered: SLO breaches (latency/error-rate), capacity exhaustion (GPU pool saturated), model-serving regressions (inference errors/invalid outputs), control-plane outages (auth, billing), and region failovers.
- Out of scope: localized developer environment issues and feature branch CI failures.

Key Definitions:
- Incident Commander (IC): person coordinating response and cross-team communication.
- Oncall Engineer: first responder responsible for initial triage.
- Escalation Lead: second-tier SME to handle deeper remediation (e.g., runtime, infra).
- Customer Signal: a verifiable metric or event that warrants customer-facing comms (see section "Customer Signal Matrix").

Roles & Responsibilities:
1) Oncall Engineer (primary):
   - Acknowledge paging alerts within 5 minutes.
   - Run the appropriate runbook checklist for the alert type.
   - If containment not achieved in 15 minutes, request IC.

2) Incident Commander (IC):
   - Assemble responders and assign clear tasks.
   - Own the timeline and public comm cadence.
   - Decide on status page updates and severity classification.

3) Escalation Lead / SME:
   - Focus on remediation steps that require deep knowledge (kernel, GPUs, model graph).

4) Communications Lead (usually IC or delegated PM from customer-success):
   - Draft and publish status page entries and customer emails.

Oncall Cadence & Handoff:
- Rotation length: 7 days for primary oncall, 14 days for backup (shadow).
- Weekly handoff brief: automatic Slack post by rotation-bot containing open incidents, known issues, and any pending action items.
- Handoff checklist (must be completed in rotation-bot form):
  1. Confirm escalation contact list is current.
  2. Review SLO burn rate dashboard links.
  3. Confirm runbook ownership annotations.

Escalation Ladder (example):
- Pager alert -> Oncall Engineer (5 min ack) -> Escalation Lead (15 min) -> IC (30 min) -> Exec Notification (60+ min for Sev1).

Customer Signal Matrix (select signals that require public communication):
- Severity: Sev1 (complete outage or >90% API error rate), Sev2 (partial outage, large SLO breach), Sev3 (isolated customer impact).
- Objective signals: sustained 5m error rate > 10% for Hosted API, 5m median tail latency (p95) > 2x baseline, Dedicated: active queued requests > 80% of pool for 10+ min, Control-plane auth failures > 1% of requests for 5+ min.
- When any objective signal is met, trigger status page entry and classify customers by impact for targeted messages.

Runbook Templates (use as copy/paste checklists):
- SLO breach (high error-rate or high latency):
  1. Validate alerts and check raw traces dashboard: /dashboards/slo-burn-rate.
  2. Identify rollback candidate model versions or scalar config changes in nightly config PRs.
  3. Check recent deploys: `git log --since=2h --services=service-name`.
  4. If model-serving: verify KV cache health and GPU memory pressure via `nvidia-smi` and `runtime-inspect --node`.
  5. Mitigation options: scale replicas, enable degraded-mode routing to small-quantized model variant, or route to Dedicated fallback region.
  6. If containment not achieved in 15 minutes, IC publishes initial status page as "Investigating".

- GPU pool saturation (Dedicated):
  1. Confirm queue length and active allocation: /dashboards/gpu-pool-util.
  2. Identify noisy tenants via token-level cost telemetry.
  3. Apply emergency throttling policy for offending route: `redwood admin rate-limit set --route <route> --qps 10 --reason "noisy-tenant"`.
  4. Provision burst capacity if reserve pool available.
  5. Notify sales/CS for impacted customers and map to SLA entitlements.

- Control-plane auth failures:
  1. Check KMS/HSM and OIDC provider health.
  2. Validate certificate rotations: `openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.internal:443 -showcerts`.
  3. If certificates rotated incorrectly, fallback to previous cert bundle and roll forward with correct chain.

Status Page & Customer Communications (templates below):
- Status page template (short form):
  Title: [Investigating] Reduced inference throughput for Hosted API in us-west-2
  Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or timeouts.
  Latest update: We are investigating increased queue times in the inference tier. Oncall engineers are actively diagnosing and have isolated a throttling condition.
  Next update: 30 minutes or when we have a remediation plan.
  Owner: Incident Commander: @<IC-slack-handle>

- Customer targeted email (template):
  Subject: Immediate notice: Intermittent inference latency in us-west-2
  Body: Hello <Customer> team,

  We want to let you know we are currently investigating intermittent inference latency affecting a subset of requests routed to us-west-2. Our oncall team has identified increased queueing in the inference pool and is validating a mitigation plan (scaling + temporary routing to quantized variants). We estimate a remediation window of 30–60 minutes.

  Impact: Potentially higher latency or request timeouts for models served in the region.
  Mitigation: We are applying emergency throttling and routing changes to reduce queueing. No customer data is affected.

  We will follow up with updates on the status page: <status-link>. If you have specific SLAs impacted, reply to this message and we will prioritize direct assistance.

  — Redwood Support

Escalation Communication Checklist (IC must verify):
- Have we classified severity? (Sev1/Sev2/Sev3)
- Has a status page entry been created within 15 minutes of classification?
- Were customer-facing teams (sales, account execs) notified within 30 minutes for affected customers?

Game-Day Scripts (executable scenarios to validate process):
1) Scenario: Synthetic SLO degradation (Hosted API p95 spike)
   Script steps:
   - Inject synthetic load into staging mirrors with p95 latency doubled.
   - Verify that SLO burn rate alert fires in PagerDuty.
   - Execute oncall triage checklist and create a status page draft.
   - Validate that rotation-bot posts handoff notes and that comm templates can be sent from the status tool.
   Success criteria: Alerts, paging, status updates, and CS notifications are successful end-to-end.

2) Scenario: GPU pool noisy-tenant isolation (Dedicated)
   Script steps:
   - Simulate burst of queued allocations from test-tenant.
   - Confirm throttling policy triggers and noisy-tenant identification matches telemetry.
   - Apply emergency rate-limit and observe queue length return to baseline.
   Success criteria: Noisy tenant correctly throttled, metrics return to normal within 20 minutes, and dedicated alert suppressed post-mitigation.

Game Day Playbook (run cadence):
- Quarterly full-scale game day (all hands SRE + platform + CS).
- Monthly focused mini-drills (1 hour) for specific runbooks (auth, GPU, model-serving).
- After each game day: publish an exercise report with findings, owners, and remediation tickets.

Postmortem & RCA Template (mandatory for Sev1/Sev2 with >30 min customer impact):
- Title: [Postmortem] Short description + service affected
- Summary: 3–4 sentence customer-facing summary.
- Impact: list of affected customers, regions, SLOs missed, duration.
- Timeline: chronological bullet list with timestamps (UTC) of detection, actions, and recovery.
- Root cause: concise technical cause.
- Contributing factors: systemic or process gaps.
- Corrective actions: short-term and long-term (owner + due date).
- Validation plan: how we will verify the fix (dashboards, unit tests, game-days).
- Learning: changes to runbooks or oncall cadence.

Monitoring & Dashboards (minimum set for each service):
- SLO burn rate dashboard (5m, 1h windows).
- Request-latency histogram (p50/p95/p99).
- Error rate by route and token bucket.
- Queue depth and GPU memory pressure.
- External dependencies (OIDC, KMS) success rates.

Alert Threshold Examples (reference):
| Metric | Threshold | Pager | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API error rate (5m) | > 5% | P1 | Sev2->Sev1 if > 10% |
| p95 latency (5m) | > 2x baseline | P1 | Use regional baselines |
| GPU queue length | > 80% capacity (10m) | P1 | Dedicated pools only |
| Auth failures | > 1% | P2 | Control-plane impact |

Testing & Runbook Ownership:
- Every runbook must have a documented owner and a test that runs at least annually.
- Owners update runbook after any incident; review cadence is quarterly.

Automation & Tooling Integration:
- rotation-bot manages schedule and posts weekly handoff notes.
- incident-bot templates status page drafts and pushes to /statuspage-api.
- escalation-bot performs automatic paging escalation at configurable intervals.

Oncall Wellness & Burn Mitigation:
- Max consecutive paid rotations: 6 months; re-evaluate heavy rotations with manager.
- Silent paging hours: 22:00–06:00 local (only P0 pages unless explicitly opted in).
- Psychological safety: All responders are expected to avoid blame in public write-ups; focus on remediations and learning.

Appendix A — Example CLI commands and snippets:
- Check recent deploys: `git --no-pager log --since="2 hours ago" --pretty=format:"%h %s (%an)" -- services/service-a`
- Query GPU pool: `redwood infra pool describe --name gpu-pool-usw2 --json`
- Apply emergency throttling: `redwood admin rate-limit set --route conversions --qps 5 --reason "noisy-tenant"`

Appendix B — Post-game checklist:
1. Write exercise report and tag owners.
2. Create remediation JIRA with clear acceptance criteria.
3. Schedule runbook updates in the next weekly ops review.

Related links:
- SLO definitions: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-definitions
- Incident communication templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- Runbook library: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

Contact & Ownership:
- Primary owner: Ana Patel (Platform SRE Lead)
- Secondary: Marcus Liu (Runtime Reliability)
- For questions about this document, open a PR on the ops-docs repo or ping #sre-oncall in Slack.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-03: Created by Ana Patel.
- 2026-02-15: Expanded game-day scenarios and added customer signal matrix (reviewed by Marcus Liu, Sofia Gonzalez).

title: dsid_75795889eb474473bd660e9405d051c2__authorization-board-synthesis-and-retention-catalog-2026.txt
text:
Authorization Board: Evidence Synthesis and Retention Catalog

Purpose:
This page codifies the Authorization Board's approach to assembling, validating, and retaining evidence for authorization-related decisions across RBAC, audit logging, data residency, SDLC gates, incident response, and risk exceptions. It is intended for Board members, InfoSec, Engineering leads, and Compliance owners.

Scope:
- All production-facing access changes that affect model serving, customer data access, or tenant isolation.
- SDLC release gates that touch entitlement, cryptographic key handling, or logging schemas.
- Incident evidence for authorization-related incidents (unauthorized access, privilege escalation, service-account compromise).

Summary / Executive guidance:
The Authorization Board must be able to answer three questions for every decision or exception:
1) Who made the change? (provenance)
2) What did they change and why? (scope and rationale)
3) How long will we retain evidence and where? (retention and locality)

Primary Roles & Responsibilities:
- Authorization Board (chair: Security PM): final sign-off for cross-domain exceptions and high-impact entitlement changes.
- InfoSec (owner): maintains evidence schemas, runbooks, and audit-query templates.
- Engineering (service owners): produce change artifacts, rollout notes, authorizing PR IDs, and test evidence.
- SRE / Observability: ensure streaming audit logs, retention, and immutable store integrations.
- Legal / Compliance: set regulatory locality & retention requirements for specific customers or tenants.

Principles:
- Minimal Blast Radius: prefer timebound, scoped entitlements with automated deprovisioning.
- Immutable Evidence: critical authorization events must be persisted to an append-only store (see Audit Schema).
- Contextual Packaging: combine logs + PR metadata + deployment artifact + incident timeline into a single evidence bundle for audits.
- Defense in Depth: combine RBAC, attribute filters, and runtime policy checks; evidence must reflect all relevant layers.

RBAC Patterns and Required Artifacts:
- Pattern: Role-Based + Attribute Filtered (recommended for customer-facing endpoints).
  Required artifacts per change: role-definition YAML, PR link, authorizing ticket, canary/rollback plan, access-review snapshot (pre-change), sampling of affected identities (<= 20 ids for review).
- Pattern: Timebound Elevation (JIT): must include justification, duration, automatic expiry timestamp, and post-expiry verification job.
- Pattern: Service Identity Change (keys/roles): key rotation proof, new key fingerprint, previous key revocation proof, CI build artifact IDs.

Audit Logging Requirements (minimum contract):
- Every authorization decision must emit a structured event with the following fields (pipe table):

| field | type | description | retention-tier |
|-------|------|-------------|----------------|
| event_id | uuid | unique event identifier | hot:30d / cold:3y |
| timestamp | ISO8601 | event time | hot:30d / cold:3y |
| actor_id | string | user or service principal | hot:30d / cold:3y |
| actor_type | enum | human | service | system | hot |
| action | string | e.g., grant_role, revoke, evaluate_acl | hot:30d / cold:3y |
| target_resource | string | resource identifier (model, dataset, route) | hot:30d / cold:3y |
| outcome | enum | allowed | denied | error | hot:30d / cold:3y |
| evidence_refs | list | links to PRs / tickets / deployment IDs | cold:3y |
| locality_tag | string | region/residency label | cold:3y |

Notes: the "evidence_refs" field must contain internal links or object ids; logs without evidence_refs trigger a pre-review alert.

Data Residency & Retention Mapping (catalog):
- Table (pipe):
| artifact | default-retention | storage-class | residency constraint | owner |
|---------|------------------|---------------|----------------------|-------|
| auth-audit-hot | 30 days | hot-ssd (central observability) | none (index only) | observability-team |
| auth-audit-cold | 3 years | object-store-immutable | region-tagged per-tenant | observability-team |
| evidence-bundles | 7 years | immutable-archive | per-customer residency if requested | security |
| sdlc-gate-artifacts | 5 years | object-store | global | eng-platform |
| exception-approvals | 10 years | secure-vault | restricted (legal sensitive) | security/legal |

SDLC Gate Checklist (authorization-impacting changes):
Pre-merge (owner):
1) Attach role-definition and sample policy to PR.
2) Add "authorization-impact" label and link to ticket.
3) Run unit tests including attribute-filtered access tests.
4) Provide mock audit events showing expected log output.

Pre-release (release manager):
1) Confirm evidence_refs are populated with PR and ticket IDs.
2) Confirm canary target and rollback policy.
3) Confirm retention-class of produced logs conforms to tenant residency.

Emergency patch flow (2-step signoff):
1) Quick-approve by on-call engineer + on-call security; create post-facto authorization ticket within 4 hours.
2) Evidence bundle must be assembled and presented to Authorization Board within 48 hours.

Incident Response: Evidence Collection Steps (authorization incidents):
1) Triage: tag incident as AUTHZ and attach incident-id to all artifacts.
2) Preserve hot logs (copy snapshot) and mark snapshots immutable.
3) Export evidence bundle:
   - PRs, merge commits, CI logs (build ids)
   - Deployment manifests and rollout timestamps
   - Audit events (filter: event_type in [grant_role, revoke_role, evaluate_acl])
   - Key material rotation proofs and KMS audit events
   - Access reviews and approval tickets
4) For tenant-impact incidents, consult Legal on cross-border copies before exporting.
5) Hand off to Forensics: provide query templates and a preferred time window.

Compliance Evidence Workflow (packaging & submission):
1) Create evidence-bundle object in Evidence Service (artifact id).
2) Populate metadata: incident_id/exception_id, owner_team, retention_class, residency_tag.
3) Attach artifacts (log snapshots, PRs, tickets, screenshots) and a short executive summary (<=300 words).
4) Board Review: Authorization Board evaluates bundle within 15 business days for high-risk items.
5) Archive: on approval, evidence-bundle is sealed to immutable-archive and retention starts.

Decision & Exception Handling (Authorization Board procedure):
1) Submission: engineering or security submits an Exception Request with the minimal required artifacts.
2) Triage: Board Secretary assesses completeness within 3 business days.
3) Review: Board meets (synchronous or async) and votes; required vote thresholds: security + one engineering + one compliance/legal.
4) Conditions: Board may add conditional mitigations (e.g., additional logging, scoped timebound limits).
5) Approval: Board records decision and shipping ticket; evidence-bundle is created at approval time.
6) Expiry & Re-evaluation: all approvals default to 90 days unless a longer term is justified and documented.

Retention schedule (quick reference):
- Hot auth audit: 30 days
- Cold auth audit (immutable): 3 years (default), extended per regulation to 7+ years
- Evidence bundles for incidents: 7 years (default) or longer if legal requirement
- Exception approvals and change logs: 10 years

Query templates (examples):
- Find all grant_role events by actor:
  SELECT * FROM auth_audit_cold WHERE actor_id = 'svc-deploy-123' AND action = 'grant_role' AND timestamp >= '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z';
- Evidence bundle retrieval:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
       https://evidence.internal/api/v1/bundles/{bundle_id} | jq '.'

Sample event JSON (simple contract example):
{
  "event_id": "uuid-1234",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-18T14:12:03Z",
  "actor_id": "alice@redwood",
  "actor_type": "human",
  "action": "revoke_role",
  "target_resource": "model:recommendation:v2",
  "outcome": "allowed",
  "evidence_refs": ["PR-1423", "TICKET-5819"],
  "locality_tag": "eu-west-1"
}

Operational Alerts & Automation:
- Missing evidence_refs: alert to submitter and Board secretary after 24 hours.
- Timebound approval expiry: automated reminder 7 days before expiry.
- Post-approval verification: scheduled job at expiry to confirm deprovisioning ran.

Acceptance criteria for auditability (must be met before approval):
- Events are searchable by event_id and actor_id for the required retention period.
- Evidence-bundles include at least one immutable artifact (log snapshot) plus change metadata.
- Residency requirements validated by Legal/Compliance for affected tenants.

Appendix A — Board templates and checklists (links):
- Exception request template: /templates/authz-exception-request
- Evidence bundle checklist: /templates/evidence-bundle-checklist
- Audit event schema docs: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025.json

Appendix B — Contact matrix:
- Authorization Board Secretary: security-board@redwood.internal
- Observability Slack: #observability
- Incident Pager: PagerDuty rotation: sec-oncall

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05: Created by Marisol Rivera
- 2026-01-12: Added SDLC gate checklist and emergency patch flow (Elena Gomez review)
- 2026-02-18: Tuned retention mapping and added automated alert rules (Jonah Patel review)

End of document.

title: dsid_cbf169441b3f4f78beff251d82f91ec5__gpu-burst-replication-and-anti-entropy-spec.txt
text:
GPU burst replication and anti-entropy IaC spec

Summary:

This document defines an infrastructure-first pattern for multi-region / multi-pool checkpoint replication and anti-entropy for GPU-backed inference workloads. It pairs a Terraform module surface with an operator contract and a runbook for degraded states. The goal is to ensure KV/cache and checkpoint consistency in the face of burst spilling, preemptions, and region failovers while minimizing egress and storage cost.

Scope:
- Applies to model-serving pools that maintain on-disk checkpoints or large shardable KV stores (e.g., per-tenant checkpoints, tokenized KV-cache snapshots).
- Covers Terraform module interface, operator behavior, SLO mappings, observability, testing matrix, rollout and rollback steps.
- Does NOT prescribe model-level format or epoch semantics; assumes a checkpoint can be made atomic via manifest files (checksum + metadata).

Why this matters:
- During burst or preemptive evictions, tenants may need warm backups in a remote pool to avoid cold-start latency and lost KV-snapshot progress.
- Naive replication increases egress and storage costs and can cause write amplification under noisy bursts. This spec balances safety vs. cost with a tiered replication policy + anti-entropy reconciliation.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Primary pool: the pool where the checkpoint is authored during normal serving.
- Replica pool: one or more pools that hold copies for fast failover or warmup.
- Async tiered replication: metadata (manifests, small indexes) replicated fast; large checkpoint blobs replicated opportunistically to avoid egress spikes.
- Anti-entropy pass: background, idempotent reconciliation that verifies checksums and repairs missing or stale blobs.

Design overview:
1) Tiered replication model:
   - Manifest-first: writers create a small JSON manifest (blob keys, checksums, size, sequence) and write it to the primary object store.
   - Metadata replication (manifest) is pushed to control-plane metadata service immediately via the replication-controller.
   - Blob replication: large blobs (>= 50MB) are scheduled into a rate-limited, priority queue; critical blobs (latest seq) are preferred.

2) Replication policies (configurable via IaC):
   - policy.mode: off | metadata-only | staged | full
   - policy.priority: latest-first | heatmap-driven | tenant-critical
   - policy.bandwidth_cap: bytes/sec per-region (defaults: 20MiB/s for non-enterprise tenants)

3) Anti-entropy reconciliation:
   - Periodic pass runs a manifest diff between primary and replica pools.
   - Discrepancies spawn idempotent repair jobs that copy missing blobs or re-validate checksums.
   - Repair jobs are constrained by tenant egress budgets and global daily caps to avoid cost surprises.

Operational primitives (exposed by Terraform module and operator):
- resource redwood_gpu_replication_target { pool_id, region, storage_bucket, max_daily_egress }
- resource redwood_gpu_replication_policy { mode, priority, manifest_ttl_days, blob_threshold_bytes }
- data redwood_gpu_pool_health { pool_id }

Example Terraform interface (usage snippet):
```hcl
module "replication_demo" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.redwood.ai/infra/modules//gpu-replication?ref=v1.2.0"

  primary_pool_id = "gpu-pool-prod-us-west-2"
  replicas = [
    { pool_id = "gpu-pool-warm-us-east-1", region = "us-east-1", storage_bucket = "rwd-replica-us-east" },
  ]

  policy = {
    mode = "staged"
    priority = "latest-first"
    bandwidth_cap = "20MiB/s"
    manifest_ttl_days = "7"
  }

  labels = { owner = "infra/gpu" }
}
```

Operator contract and behavior:
- The replication operator consumes CRDs/tf-state and ensures the desired replica resources exist (storage buckets, IAM bindings, per-replica leases).
- Write path: when a manifest appears in primary store, operator creates a replication job record and attempts metadata push within 5s.
- Blob copy path: operator evaluates blob size and policy; for staged mode, only latest N (configurable) are queued immediately; the rest are queued to the low-priority window (00:00–06:00 UTC by default).
- Idempotency: all copy/repair jobs include source manifest checksum and target object etag. Replay-safe; failed jobs are safe to retry.

SLOs and safety thresholds:
- Metadata replication latency SLO: 99% within 10s.
- Critical blob replication SLO (staged mode for latest checkpoint): 95% within 120s.
- Anti-entropy convergence SLO: 95% of divergence cases resolved within 24h, subject to egress cap.
- Cost safety: module enforces max_daily_egress and aborts non-critical jobs when cap exceeded; it surfaces telemetry alerts.

Observability (telemetry events and dashboards):
- Events emitted by operator: replication_job_created, replication_job_started, replication_job_completed, replication_job_failed, anti_entropy_pass_started, anti_entropy_repair_created.
- Essential metrics:
  - replication_jobs_in_flight (gauge)
  - replication_throughput_bytes/sec (per-region)
  - manifest_replication_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - anti_entropy_repair_count_by_tenant (counter)
  - egress_budget_remaining_bytes (gauge)
- Dashboards to ship:
  - Replication Overview: per-pool replication lag, job backlog, egress burn-rate heatmap.
  - Anti-entropy: reconciliation success rate, repair backlog, top failing tenants.

Runbook: degraded-state playbook (summary):
1) Symptom: replication_job_failed spikes or >10% of critical blobs missing in a pool.
2) Step 0 — Triage: check replication_jobs_in_flight, most recent replication_job_failed event, pod logs for operator (namespace infra-replication).
3) Step 1 — Isolate cause: network errors (S3 5xx), IAM errors (403), quota errors (403/429), or operator crashloops.
4) Step 2 — Short-term mitigation:
   - If IAM issue: revert the IAM change via terraform revert run (apply the previous terraform state or the attach-iam script).
   - If egress cap exceeded: temporarily increase max_daily_egress for affected tenant(s) using tf variable override (documented below), and mark the repair jobs as high-priority.
   - If operator crashloop: scale operator to 0/1 and restart, collect logs to S3 path s3://rwd-ops-logs/replication/<ts>.
5) Step 3 — Reconciliation
   - Kick manual anti-entropy pass: POST /internal/replication/antientropy?pool=us-west-2
   - Monitor anti_entropy_repair_count_by_tenant and ensure repair job completes.
6) Step 4 — Postmortem actions: increase test coverage for failing path, add integration test to canary grid, and schedule a follow-up runbook rehearsal.

Terraform quick recovery snippet (change max_daily_egress):
```hcl
resource "redwood_gpu_replication_target" "r1" {
  pool_id = "gpu-pool-warm-us-east-1"
  storage_bucket = "rwd-replica-us-east"
  max_daily_egress = "50GiB" # increased temporarily for mitigation
}
```

Testing and validation matrix (CI/CD integration):
- Unit tests: module validation for parameter ranges, IAM policy generation.
- Integration canaries: small-scale replication between two dev pools with synthetic manifests and deliberate checksum drift. Run nightly in the ephemeral-eval grid.
- Chaos-tests: simulate source pool preemption and verify that manifest-first handoff + replica warm-start completes within critical blob SLO. Use the existing gpu-chaos-day harness.
- Cost simulation: run a billing-simulator job that replays a week of burst traffic to verify egress caps and daily burn-rate alarms.

Rollout and migration plan:
1) Deploy module v1.0 to non-prod pools and run 14-day smoke to validate telemetry and anti-entropy behavior.
2) Invite two opt-in production tenants to pilot staged mode for a single warm replica pool.
3) After pilot (4 weeks), enable metadata-only mode for low-priority tenants and staged for high-priority tenants.
4) Full rollout gated on no more than 1% of replicas failing anti-entropy for two consecutive weeks.

Security and compliance considerations:
- All cross-region transfers must be encrypted in flight (TLS) and at rest using customer-managed KMS keys when tenant requires restricted mode.
- IAM least-privilege: replication operator uses a short-lived service account with signed-temporary tokens for object-store copies.
- Audit logs: every manifest write and anti-entropy repair must be recorded to the central audit trail for at least 90 days.

Ownership and contact matrix:
- Product owner: Marisa Chen (infra/gpu)
- Primary oncall for operator: infra-sre-runbook rotation (pager: infra-replication)
- Escalation to infra-team-leads: Diego Alvarez -> Priya Khatri.

Related pages and artifacts:
- Terraform module repo: git@git.redwood.ai:infra/modules/gpu-replication (README, integration tests)
- Canary job: ci/canaries/gpu-replication-smoke
- Billing simulator: jobs/eval/billing-replay/replication

Appendix: manifest example
```json
{
  "checkpoint_seq": 1432,
  "created_at": "2025-02-10T02:14:22Z",
  "blobs": [
    { "key": "ckpt-1432/shard-0", "size": 34567890, "sha256": "abc..." },
    { "key": "ckpt-1432/shard-1", "size": 43214567, "sha256": "def..." }
  ],
  "meta": { "model": "opt-12b", "tenant": "tenant-42" }
}
```

Document change log:
- 2024-11-05: created initial draft (Marisa Chen).
- 2024-12-12: added anti-entropy SLOs and egress cap semantics (review by Diego Alvarez).
- 2025-02-10: operational runbook updated with Terraform quick recovery snippet and rollout gating (review by Priya Khatri).

If you are implementing or operating a replica, follow the Terraform quickstart in the module README and contact infra-replication on Slack for onboarding help.

text:
sli-cost-latency-ablation-retrospective-2026

Summary
-------
This retrospective documents the ablation study we ran across Q4 2025 and early Q1 2026 that intentionally removed or degraded telemetry signals used in the token-latency and cost SLI system to understand sensitivity, false-positive rates, and operator cognitive load. The goal was to produce concrete runbook changes, dashboard improvements, and rollout guidance to reduce SLI churn during regional blips and model-variant rollouts.

Background
----------
- Context: Several oncall incidents in Oct–Nov 2025 showed oscillating SLI alerts tied to noisy cost-signal spikes (billing anomalies) and intermittent token-latency reports stemming from partial KV cache failures. We wanted to quantify which signals were essential and which amplified noise.
- Hypothesis: Some telemetry variants (per-tenant token-cost per-minute, short-window p50/p95 token latency computed at the ingress proxy) amplify transient noise. Ablating secondary signals and relying on orthogonal indicators (GPU-queue length, model-variant error-rate, KV-hit ratio) will reduce alert fatigue without increasing time-to-detect real regressions.

Study design
------------
1. Scope and targets
   - Services: routing-proxy, inference-runtime, kv-prefix-cache, cost-aggregator
   - SLIs evaluated: token-latency (user-facing tail), token-cost (per-tenant cost rate), request-error-rate, model-variant-fallback-rate
2. Ablation matrix
   - Full signal set (baseline)
   - Remove short-window p50/p95 at ingress (30s windows)
   - Remove per-tenant minute-level cost derivative alert (keep hourly)
   - Replace synthetic-sla synthetic checks with synthetic-sla-lite (less frequent)
   - Silence KV-hit ratio-derived micro-alerts (promote to advisory)
3. Duration and rollout
   - Canary region: us-west-2 (2 weeks)
   - Staged rollouts: canary -> 3 regions -> global (each stage 72h observation)
   - Automated rollback if combined SRE detection score > 0.7 (see detection scoring below)

Timeline and data collected
-------------------------
- Nov 20–Dec 04, 2025: Baseline observability capture (pre-ablation)
- Dec 06–Dec 20, 2025: Canary ablation in us-west-2
- Jan 05–Jan 19, 2026: Regional expansion and stress-testing during model-variant rollout
- Jan 20–Feb 10, 2026: Post-rollout monitoring and manual incident injections
- Data sources: Prometheus (metrics), ClickHouse traces, billing-tables (hourly), incident tickets, oncall annotations

Key findings
------------
- Removing short-window ingress p95 reduced alert volume by ~43% without increasing median time-to-detect for verified incidents (median time-to-detect increased from 3.8m to 4.2m).
- Silencing minute-level per-tenant cost derivative alerts cut false positives from noisy metering by 78% but allowed two low-impact cost leaks to persist 6–12 hours longer; both were detected by hourly summaries and manual audits.
- Promoting KV-hit micro-alerts to advisory reduced operator context-switching; when KV-hit advisory crossed 5% degradation coincident with GPU-queue growth > 12, it reliably predicted tail-latency regressions within 18 minutes.
- Synthetic-sla-lite (less frequent synthetic checks) caught only 60% of degradation events that affected <5% of traffic; use synthetic-sla-lite only when paired with additional internal-sided health checks.

Root cause and analysis
-----------------------
- Many false-positives originated from noise in short aggregation windows at the proxy (burst traffic patterns, backoff storms). The ingestion pipeline's downsampling amplified micro-bursts into perceived p95 regressions.
- Billing-metering noise was caused by short-lived quantization in our cost-aggregator and delayed reconciliation between per-token meter and hourly summary tables.
- The observability deck lacked cross-signal correlation at alert time; operators had to manually stitch the timeline across cost, latency, and queue metrics.

Decisions made
--------------
- Keep tail-latency SLI (token-latency p99/p95) but remove 30s short-window p95 from primary alerting rules. Short-window p95 will appear on a "fast-sight" dashboard only.
- De-prioritize per-tenant minute-level cost derivative alerts: move to advisory channel and require corroborating signals (e.g., billing reconciliation anomaly OR persistent token-inflation for 2 consecutive windows) before paging.
- Add a combined-rule: page only when (tail-latency SLI breach AND (gpu-queue > 10 OR model-variant-fallback-rate > 0.5%)). This reduces noise while preserving detection power.

Runbook changes (short list)
--------------------------
- New play: "Cost-Derivative Advisory Investigation" (see steps below). Owner: Platform Observability (pager duty: platform-observability rota).
- Update: "Tail-Latency Pager" flow now includes immediate checklist to check KV-hit advisory and GPU-queue before escalation to runtime owners.
- Add guidance for oncall: use the "fast-sight" dashboard when investigating sub-5min blips; do not escalate immediately unless corroborating signals exist.

Cost-Derivative Advisory Investigation (new play)
--------------------------------------------------
1. Observe advisory channel for per-tenant cost spikes.
2. Check hourly summary table: `SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as tokens_hour FROM billing.hourly WHERE ts >= now() - interval 2 hour GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY tokens_hour DESC LIMIT 10;`
3. Cross-check model-variant fallback rate and token-latency p99 for the same tenant and time window.
4. If both token-latency p99 and cost derivative are elevated for >2 windows, open an incident and follow standard cost-incident runbook.

Detection scoring and rollback guard
----------------------------------
- Each stage of rollout computed an SRE detection score (0–1) aggregated from: SLI-breach-rate (0.5), new incident count (0.2), manual operator escalation (0.2), noise ratio (false-alerts / total-alerts) penalty (0.1).
- If detection score > 0.7 within 72h, automatic rollback to previous alerting config triggered. We used this to protect regional rollout.

Dashboard and alerting changes (implementation plan)
---------------------------------------------------
- Dashboards
  - Create "fast-sight" dashboard (ingress-short-window-metrics, kv-hit-ratio, gpu-queue, model-variant-fallback) for first responders. Embed a small timeline correlator widget.
  - Add a cost-reconciliation panel showing hourly vs per-minute aggregates and a reconciliation delta heatmap.
  - Tag all relevant panels with "advisory" or "primary" to guide oncall focus.
- Alerts
  - Primary alerts updated in Prometheus rules: remove 30s p95-based alert rules; add combined-rule described above.
  - Advisory alerts routed to a different channel (platform-advisory) with a lighter notification policy (email + slack thread, no paging).

Operational impact and metrics
-----------------------------
- Alert volume (pager count) reduced 32% across platform owners during rollout windows.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for genuine incidents remained stable (median 3.9m pre, 4.1m post).
- Operator-reported cognitive load (post-deployment survey, n=34) improved: 67% reported fewer unnecessary escalations; 12% reported slower initial detection on low-impact cost leaks.

Follow-up actions (owners and deadlines)
---------------------------------------
- Platform Observability: implement fast-sight dashboard (due 2026-03-15). Owner: Marcus Green.
- Runtime: add a lightweight internal health-check endpoint in inference-runtime to supplement synthetic-sla-lite by 2026-04-01. Owner: Daniela Park.
- Billing: add a reconciliation job that writes a "reconciliation_delta" metric hourly to Prometheus by 2026-03-31. Owner: Diego Alvarez.
- SRE: codify detection scoring and automated rollback in rollout tooling by 2026-03-10. Owner: Priya Nair.

Guidelines for future experiments
--------------------------------
- Always pair ablation of a signal with at least one orthogonal guardrail (queue length, error-rate, or reconciliation delta).
- Use a detection score with at least four independent components (SLI, incidents, operator escalation, noise penalty).
- Reserve "advisory" channel for signals that historically cause >60% false positives and are actionable only with corroboration.

Appendix: queries and snippets
-----------------------------
- Ingress short-window p95 query (Prometheus example):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30s])) by (le, region))
```
- GPU-queue alert snippet (Prometheus rule example):
```
- alert: GPUQueueHigh
  expr: sum(queue_length) by (region) > 10
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU queue length > 10 (region={{ $labels.region }})"
```
- Reconciliation delta SQL (ClickHouse example):
```
SELECT toHour(ts) as hour, tenant_id, sum(per_minute_tokens) as minute_tokens, sum(hourly_tokens) as hourly_tokens, (hourly_tokens - minute_tokens) as reconciliation_delta
FROM billing.per_minute JOIN billing.hourly USING (tenant_id, hour)
WHERE ts >= now() - interval 24 hour
GROUP BY hour, tenant_id
ORDER BY reconciliation_delta DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Related artifacts and links
---------------------------
- Runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026
- Dashboard template: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/token-cost-attribution-and-explainable-trace-playbook-2026
- SLI economics guidance: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/sli-economics-mapping-and-runtime-decision-guide-2026

Conclusion
----------
The ablation experiment validated that careful de-emphasis of short-window ingress and minute-level per-tenant cost signals materially reduces operator noise while preserving detection of genuine regressions when combined with orthogonal guardrails. The changes above balance reduced pager fatigue with a modest increase in time-to-detect low-impact cost leaks. We recommend the configuration changes be rolled out broadly after the planned runbook and dashboard work is completed.

text:
Automated Error-Budget Salvage and Safeguard Runbook

Summary:
This runbook defines the automated "salvage" sequence Redwood uses when an SLO is at risk of breach due to sudden demand or cascading failures. It documents precise trigger thresholds, automated actions the Error-Budget Controller (EBC) performs, verification steps, and escalation criteria for human intervention. The goal is to preserve customer-visible SLOs while minimizing cost and avoiding risky manual changes during short-lived incidents.

Scope:
- Applies to platform-facing services that contribute directly to customer-facing SLOs: inference-gateway, request-router, kv-cache-service, batch-assembler, model-allocator, and autoscaler.
- Covers both Hosted API and Dedicated deployments where EBC is active.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance windows and long-running degradations (>72h) which require runbook escalation to Service Owners.

Key definitions:
- SLO Window: 30-day rolling window for availability and p95 latency.
- Error Budget: 1 - SLO (e.g., for a 99.9% availability SLO, error budget = 0.1%).
- Salvage Window: 30 minutes from first threshold crossing.
- EBC (Error-Budget Controller): automated component that evaluates telemetry and issues policy actions.

High-level policy & thresholds:
1) Watcher thresholds (continuous):
   - Watcher-Alert (early): projected error budget burn rate > 5x for next 24 hours (based on last 15-minute trend).
   - Salvage-Trigger (automatic): projected error budget burn rate > 15x and projected remaining budget < 6 hours.
   - Critical-Escalate: projected remaining budget < 1 hour OR sudden p95 spike > 3x baseline

2) Priority ordering for automated remediation (executed by EBC):
   - Level A (fast, reversible, low-risk): enable cross-region routing to standby region for low-latency tenants, temporarily relax tenant-specific throttles by 10% for Class B tenants, activate short-lived balloon capacity (burst GPUs) with auto-expire 45m.
   - Level B (moderate risk/cost): force-prefix-cache warm (pre-warm KV entries for hot prefixes), increase batch size heuristics for background non-interactive requests up to safe limit, open read-only fallback for non-critical model variants.
   - Level C (higher cost/impact): spin up additional model-allocator pools (quantized model variants), preempt lower-priority background jobs and throttled training tasks, switch to higher-cost low-latency instance types for the next 30 minutes.

Automated Salvage Sequence (step-by-step):
1) Detection & Validation (0–90s):
   - EBC detects Salvage-Trigger via SLO prediction job (15s cadence).
   - Validate signal: cross-check with telemetry pipeline (prometheus, traces) and synthetic canaries. Must see at least 2 corroborating signals (latency, error-rate or canary fail).
   - If validation fails, EBC records anomaly and re-checks at 30s, abort salvage if signals subside.

2) Pre-emptive Announcement (90–120s):
   - Post internal incident note to #sre-ops channel with automated summary: affected SLO, projected remaining budget, actions planned.
   - Create ephemeral incident in Incident Manager with severity=warning so SREs are aware.

3) Level A actions (120–300s):
   - Command: redwoodctl ebc action enable-cross-region --from=us-west-2 --to=us-east-1 --tenants=all-low-latency
   - Command: redwoodctl throttle relax --tenant-selection=classB --percent=10 --duration=45m
   - Command: redwoodctl capacity balloon --pool=inference-burst --size=gpu-t4x8 --duration=45m
   - After each action, EBC waits 30s, then asserts service-level telemetry improved (p95 reduced or error rate declined).

4) Level B actions (if Level A insufficient, 5–15m):
   - Pre-warm KV cache: redwoodctl kv prewarm --prefixes=@hotlist --parallel=8
   - Tune batching: redwoodctl runtime set-batching --service=request-router --batch-size=adaptive --max-inflight=512
   - Promote read-only fallbacks for non-critical model variants: redwoodctl model promote-fallback --service=kv-cache-service --variants=ro-quantv1

5) Level C actions (if still insufficient, escalate and execute with approvals):
   - Spin up quantized allocator pools: redwoodctl allocator create --type=quant-8bit --count=4
   - Evict non-critical workloads: redwoodctl schedule evict --workload=training-jobs --grace=60s
   - Notify Finance/Capacity-owners for approval if estimated cost delta > $5000 in 24h.

Telemetry & Safety checks (always run):
- After each automated action the EBC uses these checks before proceeding further:
  * Canary verification: 3 sequential canary requests succeed for each critical path (generation, embedding).
  * Latency regression guard: no more than 10% p95 increase for unaffected tenants in 5m window.
  * Error amplification guard: if system error-rate doubles post-action, EBC rolls back the last action immediately.

Fast rollback rules (automated):
- Any Level A or B action that does not produce measurable improvement within 3 minutes is rolled back automatically.
- Any action causing collateral regressions (latency regressions for unaffected tenants or >1.5x increase in internal error events) is rolled back immediately.

Manual escalation criteria (immediately page rotating SRE):
- EBC cannot restore projected error budget burn below 5x within 20 minutes of Salvage-Trigger.
- Projected remaining budget drops below 1 hour at any point.
- Automated rollbacks occur more than 2 times for the same sequence within 30 minutes.

On-call checklist for SRE who takes ownership:
1) Acknowledge incident in Incident Manager and set severity based on projected remaining budget.
2) Review EBC action log (redwoodctl ebc show --incident-id=<id>) and the timeline of telemetry.
3) If Level C actions required, coordinate with Product & Capacity team and document approval in incident.
4) If root cause appears unrelated to capacity (e.g., infra networking or model corruption), switch to debugging checklist in "Forensic playbook: service-level causation" (see related pages).

Configuration examples (EBC policy snippet):

{
  "policy_name": "salvage-policy-default",
  "slo_window_days": "30",
  "watcher_threshold_factor": "5",
  "salvage_trigger_factor": "15",
  "salvage_window_minutes": "30",
  "level_a": "enable-cross-region,relax-throttles,balloon-capacity",
  "level_b": "prewarm-cache,adjust-batching,promote-readonly",
  "level_c": "create-quant-pools,evict-background,raise-instance-class"
}

Note: the internal EBC policy is stored in YAML in the config repo. Example YAML fragment stored at: configs/ebc/salvage/policy-default.yaml

Operational run commands (quick reference):
- View current EBC state: redwoodctl ebc status --service=inference-gateway
- Show recent actions: redwoodctl ebc actions --since=1h --json
- Force a sandboxed salvage (test mode): redwoodctl ebc action --simulate --policy=salvage-policy-default
- Rollback last EBC action: redwoodctl ebc rollback --action-id=<id>

Ownership & responsibilities:
- Primary owner: SRE Platform (on-call rotation).
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime (for runtime/batching changes).
- Alerting & Telemetry: Observability team maintains Prometheus rules and canary tests used by EBC.
- Cost approvals: Capacity Finance liaison (on-call list in Capacity playbook).

Post-incident workflow (after salvage concluded):
1) Incident triage meeting within 24 hours (required if error budget usage exceeded > 20% of monthly budget).
2) Artifact collection: EBC logs, promql queries, canary traces, redwoodctl action history.
3) Root-cause analysis (assign to owner) and proposed mitigations (capacity changes, runtime fixes, model variant rollouts).
4) Update the EBC policy if runbook actions caused collateral risk or were ineffective.

Runbook test exercises (recommended cadence):
- Monthly simulated salvage drills using redwoodctl ebc --simulate with injected telemetry patterns.
- Quarterly cross-team tabletop to validate approval flows for Level C actions.

Related pages & references:
- SLO oncall escalation and capacity triggers (operational reference)
- Error budget orchestration and traffic throttle playbook
- Forensic playbook: service-level causation and replay guidance
- configs/ebc/salvage/policy-default.yaml (config repo)

Appendix: quick SLO thresholds (for reference)
| Service             | SLO (p95 latency) | Error budget (30d) | Salvage-Trigger (projected) |
|---------------------|-------------------:|--------------------:|-----------------------------:|
| inference-gateway    | 250ms             | 0.1%               | <6 hours remaining           |
| request-router      | 120ms             | 0.2%               | <8 hours remaining           |
| kv-cache-service    | 30ms              | 0.05%              | <4 hours remaining           |

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Priya K. Rao.
- 2025-12-04: Added Level B actions and pre-warm cache commands (reviewer feedback).
- 2026-02-03: Hardened rollback rules and added cost approval threshold.

Footer:
For questions or to propose a policy change, contact SRE Platform lead (sre-platform@redwood.com) and open a PR against configs/ebc/salvage/policy-default.yaml.

title: dsid_56e219ae04294cd5b5ce144095aa1cb1__sdk-integration-resiliency-canonical-fixes-and-checklist-2027.txt
text:
SDK Integration Resiliency: Canonical Fixes, Telemetry Alignment, and Publishing Checklist

Summary

Purpose: This playbook consolidates pragmatic, field-proven fixes and a prescriptive checklist for SDK integrations that cause the majority of support cases. It is intended for SDK maintainers, integration engineers, and support engineers who triage canonical failure modes.

Scope: Covers HTTP/streaming generation clients, embeddings/encode flows, adapter-layer failures, client-side batching/backoff, telemetry alignment (schema + cardinality), and the docs-site publishing steps for canonical fixkits. Does not replace product-level release notes or security incident response procedures.

Owner and contact
- Owner: SDK Platform (eng-devx)
- Primary contact: maya.patel@redwood.com
- Pager (support triage escalation): #sdk-support (Slack)

Quick reference: 3-minute triage
1) Identify symptom signature (error strings, status codes, stream abort reason).
2) Check last-deployed SDK version and release notes (git tag).
3) Query telemetry for corresponding trace_id / request_id to validate upstream timing and retries.
4) Apply canonical fix from table below; if no match, escalate to L2.

Canonical failure matrix (symptom -> root cause -> recommended fix)
| Symptom | Probable root cause | Recommended quick fix | Owner | Rollout urgency |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Repeated 502s during burst test | Upstream gateway timeout + synchronous client retries | Switch client to non-blocking streaming path; enable jittered exponential backoff and reduce retry count to 2 | SDK Platform | high |
| Partial streaming output then stream stops with ECONNRESET | Incompatible keepalive/TCP idle settings on customer infra | Add client-side resume token support + instruct ops to increase TCP keepalive to 30s | Integrations | medium |
| High token cost from duplicated generation calls | Misconfigured callback / webhook causing duplicate call path | Add idempotency-key header and dedupe in server-side middleware; add test in sample-app | SDK Samples | high |
| Telemetry missing request_id or has multiple request_ids per operation | SDK emits telemetry before request-id binding or uses transient IDs | Align SDK telemetry schema to include request_id and parent_id; add schema validation in CI | Observability | high |
| Latency spikes for batched requests | Batch sizing mismatch and variable model seq length | Enable adaptive batch sizing and configure max_batch_tokens=4096; add per-tenant batch metrics | Serving Runtime | medium |

Detailed triage playbook (step-by-step)
1) Collect artefacts
   - Logs: full client log, server trace id, timestamp, and network layer logs.
   - Telemetry: trace_id, span ids, sampling rate, batch size metric.
   - Repro harness snippet: minimal request that reproduces the error.

2) Reproduce in isolation
   - Use the local-sdks-sandbox to replay the exact request with captured headers.
   - If streaming: run --stream-debug to emit low-level frames. Example:

   ```bash
   ./sdk-replay --source capture.json --stream-debug --region=us-west1
   ```

3) Apply targeted fixes (examples)
   - Retry/backoff tuning (recommended default):

     ```json
     {"retry": {"max_attempts": 2, "backoff_base_ms": 200, "backoff_multiplier": 2.2, "jitter": "full"}}
     ```

   - Idempotency headers (HTTP sample):

     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
       -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \\
       -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

   - Streaming resume token pattern (pseudo):

     ```js
     // client keeps last-good-offset and sends on reconnect
     const resume = { resume_token: lastGoodOffset }
     ws.send(JSON.stringify({ op: 'resume', metadata: resume }))
     ```

4) Validate metrics post-fix
   - Check 5xx rate, mean latency (p50/p95), and token-per-request for the affected route.
   - Use redwood-console query: route="/v1/generate" and tag customer_id=<id> for 72h window.

Telemetry alignment checklist (why this matters)
- Goal: ensure every user-visible operation is correlated with a single request_id and a trace that spans SDK -> Gateway -> Serving runtime.
- Minimum viable telemetry fields (schema):
  - request_id (string)
  - client_sdk.name (string)
  - client_sdk.version (string)
  - route (string)
  - model (string)
  - tokens_requested (int)
  - tokens_returned (int)
  - error.code (string)
  - upstream_latency_ms (int)

Telemetry enforcement steps
1) SDK CI should validate that emitted telemetry contains the minimum fields. Add a Pytest assertion that loads a local telemetry sample.
2) Docs-site: publish the telemetry contract page and version it at v1.2.
3) Sampling: ensure span sampling for retries is sampled at 100% for first 30s after a release that touches SDKs.

SDK-specific defensive patterns (templates)
- Connection handling
  - Exponential backoff with bounded maximum delay (no more than 10s).
  - Active ping/keepalive with configurable interval (default 20s).
- Batching
  - Expose max_batch_tokens and per-request token ceiling.
  - Provide a `batch_estimator` hook for clients to provide sequence-length distributions.
- Streaming
  - Provide resume tokens and ack windows.
  - Avoid re-emitting events on reconnect without dedupe tokens.

Canonical fixes and test cases (developer checklist)
1) Add a unit test that simulates gateway 502 and asserts the client backoff reduces retries and surfaces a clear error to the caller.
2) Add an integration test for the streaming resume flow that replays a disconnect in the middle of a response and validates the resume token path.
3) Add a golden telemetry sample to the repo under `tests/telemetry/golden` and fail CI on schema drift.

Publishing a canonical-fix kit to docs-site (ops steps)
1) Draft the docs page under docs-site/content/sdk-canonical-fixes/<issue-shortname>.md using the canonical template.
2) Attach minimal repro code and a mini-release patch (cherry-pick) to the SDK repo.
3) Run the docs-site preflight: `make docs-lint && make snippet-check`
4) Open PR against docs-site with the label `doc:fixkit` and request reviewers: @dx-docs, @sdk-owner.
5) After merge, trigger docs-site canary publish and smoke test the example.
6) Communicate on #sdk-releases and include a short blurb for release notes.

Ops runbook for high-severity customer cases (SLA influence)
1) Immediate steps (0-30m): gather trace IDs, reproduce, and apply a temporary client-side mitigation (reduce concurrency or force single-threaded path).
2) Short-term (30m-4h): ship a hotfix to SDK branch with a flag-based mitigation and provide a patched wheel/npm tarball to customer.
3) Medium-term (4h-72h): complete the full fix, add tests, merge release, and update release notes and docs.
4) Postmortem: publish a blameless incident review within 7 days, include root cause, telemetry gaps, and corrective actions.

Example incident timeline (realistic)
- 09:03: spike observed in 5xx. Automatic alert created.
- 09:09: triage: found matching telemetry; cause: a new gateway deployment changed header forwarding.
- 09:18: mitigation: released SDK v2.14.1 with header-stable fallback and published docs-site fixkit.
- 14:00: incident declared resolved. Postmortem drafted.

Appendix: common error patterns and fix snippets
- Error: "stream aborted: 1006" -> fix: enable resume tokens and increase ws keepalive; add server-side graceful-shutdown hook.
- Error: "duplicate webhook delivery" -> fix: require X-Redwood-Delivery-Id and dedupe in the webhook handler.
- Error: "missing request_id" -> fix: inject request_id at SDK boundary before any telemetry emission.

Maintenance and cadence
- Quarterly review of canonical-fixes matrix by SDK Platform and Observability teams.
- Telemetry contract bump policy: minor bumps for additional optional fields; major bump requires SDK client upgrades (announce 8 weeks in advance).

Feedback and improvement
- To propose additions, open an issue in the eng-developer-experience repo with label `canonical-fix-request`.
- For urgent gaps, ping @maya.patel or file a support ticket with priority P0.

Related resources
- SDK CI telemetry validator: /internal/repos/sdk-ci/actions/telemetry-validate
- Repro harness: /internal/tools/sdk-replay
- Docs-site canonical templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/canonical-templates

Document history
- 2026-11-15: Created by Maya Patel.
- 2026-12-03: Added streaming resume template and retry defaults (Liam Chen).
- 2027-01-18: Expanded telemetry contract and publishing workflow (Sofia Alvarez).

title: dsid_bfd3c949492a4ab48d1211b06c889c72__operator-empowerment-decision-canvas-and-telemetry-unification-roadmap-2027.txt
text:
Operator Empowerment: Decision Canvas and Telemetry Unification Roadmap

Summary:

This roadmap describes a two-phase program to unify operator-facing telemetry, codify an actionable decision canvas, and progressively hand autonomy to platform operators. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-resolution for platform degradations by 35% and decrease high-severity incident recurrence by 50% within 12 months of the rollout baseline.

Context and motivation:
- Over the last two years telemetry streams have proliferated: runtime traces (trace-ingest), token cost signals (cost-telemetry), SLI windows, and operator notes. Operators spend an average of 22 minutes aggregating signals before making remediation decisions.
- Multiple teams (serving-runtime, eng-platform, eng-sre) maintain fragmented dashboards. This program will consolidate a canonical operator view, a decision canvas (templated remediation playbooks), and an operator capability growth plan.

Primary objectives:
1. Telemetry Unification: build a fused operator telemetry layer (telemetry-fuse) that ingests traces, SLI time-series, and token/cost signals and exposes a single query surface for operator UIs and automations.
2. Decision Canvas: author a structured, team-wide remediation decision canvas (decision-canvas-service) with priority heuristics, impact estimates, and quick-action runbooks.
3. Operator Empowerment: evolve operator tooling so runbooks become first-class, verifiable assets with automated runbook validation and operator certification pathway.

Scope (in / out):
- In: platform-level incidents affecting multi-tenant inference, token-cost spikes, KV prefix/cache failures, model-variant fallback misfires, and regional capacity shortages.
- Out: product-level feature bugs, customer-specific integration bugs (handled by customer-success), and product roadmap feature development.

Key deliverables and timeline (high level):
| Quarter | Deliverable | Owner | Success metric |
| Q4 2025 | Telemetry ingestion prototype (telemetry-fuse v0) + canonical SLI schema | eng-platform | End-to-end ingest test w/ 3 services; 95% event fidelity |
| Q1 2026 | Decision Canvas MVP + 8 templated runbooks | eng-platform + eng-sre | 60% operator adoption in synthetic drills |
| Q2 2026 | Operator UI + single-pane incident dashboard | eng-platform | 50% reduction in time-to-evidence collection during drills |
| Q3 2026 | Runbook validation pipeline and automated regression tests | eng-platform | Runbook tests included in PRs; 0 false-positive failures in 4-week window |
| Q4 2026 | Operator certification and phased autonomy pilot | eng-sre | 35% faster incident mitigations in pilot cohort |

Detailed milestones and activities:
- Telemetry-fuse (MVP to GA):
  - Define canonical SLI/event schema (fields, cardinality, cost attributes). Owner: telemetry team. Target schema: service, region, tenant_priority, token_delta, slo_window, trace_id, sample_rate.
  - Implement adapters for: trace-ingest, cost-telemetry, slo-synth, prefetch-cohort signals.
  - Provide a PromQL-like query surface + a stable gRPC API for operator tools.
  - Deliver a quiet-day ingestion run to validate fidelity and cost.

- Decision-canvas-service:
  - Create a JSON-based decision grammar that maps signals -> hypotheses -> actions. Example grammar fragment (simplified):

  ```json
  {
    "trigger": {"signal": "token_spike", "threshold": 1.2},
    "hypotheses": ["model-variant-swap", "kv-cache-degradation", "billing-anomaly"],
    "actions": ["invoke-model-swap", "escalate-billing"],
    "playbook_refs": ["runbooks/model-swap-operator-stepby-step"]
  }
  ```

  - Author canonical templated runbooks for: model swap, KV prefix cache reconstitution, regional failover, token-cost surge mitigation, and tenant throttling. Each runbook should include: preconditions, impact estimate, step-by-step actions, automated checks, rollback steps, and postmortem triggers.

- Operator UI and dashboards:
  - Single-pane incident dashboard should present: active hypothesis, supporting evidence, SLO burn chart, token cost timeline, and quick actions (UI-triggered runbook steps).
  - Dashboard rules: SLO burn > 2%/5min, token-cost delta > 15%/15min, tail-latency p99 > 200ms for 5min.

- Runbook validation pipeline:
  - Add unit/integration gates for runbook-side effects. Example CI step: validate-runbook.yaml checks that every automated action has a dry-run mode and a <= 90s verification probe.
  - Example CI snippet:

  ```bash
  # validate runbooks prior to merge
  ./scripts/validate_runbook.sh runbooks/model-swap.yaml
  ```

- Operator certification and autonomy pilot:
  - Certification tracks: visibility, decision-canvas mastery, safe-rollback proficiency. Operators must pass 3 synthetic deception drills and one live supervised incident to be certified.
  - Pilot: 12 certified operators across three shifts; supervised autonomy (operators can run automated runbook steps without SRE approval).

Ownership and roles:
- Eng-Platform (owners): telemetry-fuse, operator-UI, runbook CI integration.
- Eng-SRE (co-owners): runbook definitions, operator drills, certification criteria.
- Serving-Runtime (integrations): adapters for model-swap and KV cache actions.
- Security (advisor): review runbook actions that touch KMS/HSM or customer crypto materials.

Operational constraints and SLOs:
- Telemetry-fuse must maintain 99.9% ingest availability and <3s propagation latency for high-priority signals (region-local).
- Decision-canvas lookups should return within 200ms for operator UI calls.
- Runbook automated actions must include a verifiable dry-run and a human-confirmation step for destructive actions.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: Automated runbooks cause unintended cross-tenant impact.
  - Mitigation: Require tenant-scoped checks, and restrict destructive actions to certified operators during pilot. All automated actions run in safe-mode by default.
- Risk: Telemetry-fuse cost growth due to high-cardinality signals.
  - Mitigation: Enforce cardinality caps, sampling rules, and adaptive retention. Provide a cost dashboard and quota alerts.

Rollout procedure (numbered):
1. Prototype telemetry-fuse and run a 2-week ingest-only experiment using 3 non-critical services. Measure cost and fidelity.
2. Ship decision-canvas-service MVP and author 3 core runbooks (model-swap, kv-cache, token-surge).
3. Wire the operator UI to telemetry-fuse and decision-canvas; run tabletop drills with eng-sre.
4. Implement runbook CI validations and require them in runbook PRs.
5. Certify pilot cohort and enable supervised automated actions in a single region.
6. Monitor KPIs for 8 weeks; expand region and scale cohort if KPIs meet thresholds.

KPIs and success criteria (quantitative):
- Mean time to evidence collection reduced from 22m -> <12m in drills.
- Time to mitigation (for pilot cohort) reduced by 35%.
- Runbook false positive activation rate < 2% over 60 days.
- Telemetry ingest cost growth <= 12% while supporting unified queries.

Dependencies and integration checklist:
- trace-ingest (team: telemetry)
- cost-telemetry (team: finance-telemetry)
- slo-synth (team: eng-platform)
- decision-canvas-service API contract (documented in /api/decision-canvas/v1)
- runbook action adapters in serving-runtime: model-swap, kv-cache-drain, tenant-throttle

Testing and validation plan:
- Synthetic drills every 4 weeks with changing hypotheses and seeded noise.
- Chaos-runbook tests to ensure runbooks can be rolled back in <10 minutes.
- Cost gate in CI: any change that increases telemetry ingest cost by >8% must include compensating cardinality or sampling improvements.

Open questions (for review):
- Do we want runbook automation to support scheduled throttles (time-windowed) or only immediate operator-triggered actions?
- Which team will own the long-term SLAs for telemetry-fuse (eng-platform versus telemetry)?
- What guardrails are required before expanding autonomy to customer-facing production changes?

Appendix: sample runbook excerpt (text table form):
| Field | Example |
| Name | model-swap-operator-stepby-step |
| Preconditions | model-variant A p99 > 500ms AND p99 delta vs variant B > 20% |
| Automated checks | validate-variant-compatibility.sh; traffic-slice-sanity-check (<= 5% population) |
| Actions | 1) dry-run model swap; 2) promote variant B; 3) monitor p50/p95/p99 for 15m; 4) rollback if p99 increases > 10% |
| Rollback | human-confirmed rollback via operator UI |

Links and references:
- Decision Canvas API spec: /api/decision-canvas/v1 (internal)
- Runbook CI: git@repo:platform/runbooks
- Operator training curriculum: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-onboarding-certification-pathway-2026

Next steps (immediate action items):
- [ ] Telemetry team: finalize canonical SLI schema by 2025-11-01.
- [ ] Eng-Platform: create telemetry-fuse prototype board and invite serving-runtime for onboarding by 2025-12-01.
- [ ] Eng-SRE: draft 8 templated runbooks and host the first tabletop on 2026-01-12.

If you are reviewing, please leave feedback in the inline comments or add reviewers to the document. The roadmap will be updated monthly and the next major checkpoint is the Q1 2026 tabletop drill.

title: dsid_3f33530c07474a00b13bf9abf67b27c6__congestion-control-and-degradation-orchestration-playbook-2026.txt
text:
Congestion Control and Degradation Orchestration Playbook

Summary
-------
This playbook defines a standardized approach for detecting, orchestrating, and remediating congestion and capacity-driven degradations across Redwood's inference runtime. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, and platform owners to ensure predictable behavior during high-load scenarios while protecting SLOs and minimizing user impact.

Goals
-----
- Detect emergent congestion early and attribute root cause (hardware, network, scheduling, noisy tenant).
- Apply deterministic degradation strategies (traffic shaping, graceful tail-latency throttles, model-quality fallbacks) tied to error-budget policy.
- Preserve latency and availability targets for high-priority tenants while enabling fair-share for multi-tenant pools.
- Provide reproducible post-incident analysis artifacts for incident reviews and capacity remediation.

How this doc is organized
-------------------------
1) Detection & telemetry thresholds
2) Immediate mitigations and routing choreography
3) Degradation strategies and ordering
4) Escalation and human-in-the-loop procedures
5) Post-incident actions and capacity retrofit checklist
6) Runbook CLI snippets and play examples

1) Detection & telemetry thresholds
-------------------------------
Primary signals (evaluated at 1m and 5m windows):
- p99 latency for token-generation API > 750ms for 5m (critical)
- p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10m (warning)
- GPU utilization > 90% sustained on > 30% of pool hosts (warning)
- Queue depth (request backlog) > 50 requests per shard for 3m (critical)
- Error rate (500/502/504) > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 5m

Telemetry-derived context to collect automatically:
- Affected model and variant, sequence length percentiles, average KV cache hit-rate
- Tenant(s) with high qps, per-tenant token/memory usage, and recent rollout events
- Recent autoscale events and model-compilation cache misses

2) Immediate mitigations and routing choreography (automated first)
---------------------------------------------------------------
Automated actions (run by the traffic controller) in order: 
1. Apply token-level soft rate-limit for noisy tenant(s) at 95th percentile of recent traffic.
