  Body: The issue has been resolved at <time>. Root cause: <short summary>. Impacted customers: <list>. Postmortem will be published in X business days.

Sample internal pager message (short)

[ALERT] KV-Cache-Pressure canary-kv p50 latency spike > 250ms (3m window)
Triage: runbook: kv-cache-pressure
Action: scale ingest pool + enable bypass
Owner: @oncall-engineer | Bridge: #bridge-1245

Postmortem / evidence checklist

- Incident timeline with timestamps (UTC).
- Evidence: dashboard links, logs (trace ids), bridge transcript, customer messages.
- Root cause hypothesis and validation steps performed.
- Rollback/mitigation timeline and why chosen.
- Action items with owners and due dates (include verification plan).
- Regulatory evidence pack (if customer-impacting): signed by Continuity Owner.

Game day scoring and pass/fail criteria

- Completion of runbook steps within target windows (ack within 5m, mitigation attempted within 20m).
- Quality of evidence captured (screenshots, links) scored 0–5.
- Handoff fidelity (outgoing: 5 checks present) scored pass/fail.
- Customer comms template used correctly (language and cadence).
- Overall pass = 80%+ on combined criteria. Failures create a remediation ticket assigned to continuity owner.

Onboarding a new responder (quick checklist)

1. Shadow two weekly labs (observe and run one under mentor).
2. Pass a synthetic-signal scenario with independent execution and evidence capture.
3. Confirm access to bridge, status page, and runbook editor.
4. Sign the Continuity Manifest and provide emergency contact.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and integrations

- Trigger a test status page update (internal test endpoint):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -d '{"status":"internal-test","message":"shadow-lab ping"}' https://status-internal.redwood/api/v1/test-publish

- Fetch recent bridge transcript:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-bridge-logs/bridge-1245/transcript.txt - | tail -n 200

- Evidence automation: add evidence link to incident ticket (example):
  curl -X POST https://internal-issue.redwood/api/issue/12345/evidence -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"link":"https://dash.redwood/model/trace?id=abc123","note":"kv-cache smoke check"}'

Ownership and contact points

- Continuity Owner: Maya Carter (platform-ops) | maya.carter@redwood.com
- Program Lead: Elena Park (eng-sre) | elena.park@redwood.com
- Status Page Operator: Customer Success on-call (rotating)

Related artifacts and links

- Central runbook index: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks-index
- Oncall ledger and rota: /tools/oncall/rota
- Synthetic scenario repo: git@github.com:redwood/ops-synthetic-labs.git

Notes and next steps

- Immediate: run first synthetic scenario for batcher on 2026-03-07 and notify oncall roster.
- Q2 OKR: reduce median mitigation time by 30% using Shadow Lab remediation tickets.

Document history

- 2025-09-12: created by Elena Park
- 2025-12-08: added synthetic scenarios catalog (Ravi Nair)
- 2026-03-01: continuity manifest updates and new status templates (S. Liu)

End of document

title: dsid_3587c5f08d934360898aeec9dc1ff0da__tenant-segmentation-onboarding-scenarios-2027-02-14.txt
text:
Tenant segmentation and onboarding scenarios: consumption & fidelity paths

Summary
-------
This document defines recommended tenant segmentation, onboarding scenarios, and the default consumption + fidelity paths we should present during self-serve and sales-assisted onboarding. It is intended for Product, Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, and Developer Success to standardize the first 30–90 days of a new customer with the goal of predictable cost-to-value, controlled SLAs, and measurable quality validation.

Scope
-----
- Applies to hosted and dedicated customers onboarding to Redwood Inference.
- Focuses on initial tenancy segmentation, recommended fidelity (model variant + quantization profile), quota and warm-capacity suggestions, and telemetry checkpoints.
- Does not replace contract-level SLA negotiation for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.

Key definitions
---------------
- Tenant: a single billing/account entity in the Redwood platform.
- Fidelity: tradeoffs in model family, variant, quantization, and runtime execution path that affect latency, cost, and output quality.
- Consumption Path: a recommended default for tokens/embeddings/requests, warm capacity and fallback behaviors assigned during onboarding.

Customer segments and onboarding personas
---------------------------------------
We group inbound customers into four operational personas. Each persona maps to a recommended onboarding flow and default fidelity/consumption path.

1) Developer Sandbox (self-serve, exploratory)
- Characteristics: Low sustained traffic, high experimentation, using free credits or small token budgets.
- Goals: fast time-to-first-success, discoverability, low friction.
- Recommended defaults: hosted API, low warm-capacity (on-demand), canonical small model variant (economy variant), 90% prefix caching enabled, sampling-friendly generation config.

2) Product Pilot (PLG -> early production)
- Characteristics: intermittent production traffic, product team trying feature in-app, cost sensitivity but needs predictable latency.
- Goals: stable latency under light traffic, measurable quality.
- Recommended defaults: hosted or Dedicated trial, modest warm-capacity reservation, medium-fidelity variant, KV caching enabled, 95th percentile latency target 300–500ms for short completions.

3) Transactional Production (high-throughput, low-latency)
- Characteristics: sustained traffic, strict latency SLAs, regulated data.
- Goals: deterministic throughput, SLO-backed behavior, engineering-grade observability.
- Recommended defaults: Dedicated or Private, reserved GPU pools, high-fidelity variant with conservative quantization, persistent KV cache, proactive batching settings, canary routing rules.

4) Cost-sensitive Batch / Embeddings (analytics-heavy)
- Characteristics: large offline/nearline workloads for embeddings or reranking, lower latency requirements but high throughput.
- Goals: minimize $/embedding while preserving vector quality.
- Recommended defaults: batch-oriented instance pools, aggressive quantization profiles validated by embedding-similarity tests, local prefetching of embeddings, bulk ingest telemetry.

Onboarding flows (high level)
----------------------------
Each persona follows a 5-phase onboarding flow with explicit checkpoints.

1. Intake & Segment assignment (0–2 days)
  - SE/automation collects: primary use case, expected QPS, latency & cost targets, data residency needs, PII sensitivity.
  - System maps tenant to persona and applies baseline profile.

2. Baseline Configuration (day 0–3)
  - Apply default model variant, quantization profile, warm-capacity, caching policy, and telemetry flags.
  - Send welcome email with recommended SDK code snips and cost-estimator link.

3. Instrumentation & Sanity Tests (day 1–7)
  - Run a validated sample prompt set (provided by Redwood) to establish baseline quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine distributions and generation hallucination checks).
  - Validate telemetry flows (token counts, latency percentiles, error rates).

4. Optimization & Ramp (day 7–30)
  - Apply suggested batching and cache tuning from Redwood Optimize; run quick quantization A/B tests with synthetic traffic.
  - For Product Pilot -> encourage 2-week canary route to higher-fidelity variant if quality drift < configured threshold.

5. Guardrail & SLA handoff (day 30–90)
  - If tenant meets traffic and security thresholds, recommend Dedicated or lower-latency routing tiers; document SLO entitlements and expected cost delta.
  - Sign-off checklist completed by Solutions Engineering.

Default fidelity & consumption mapping (table)
--------------------------------------------
The table below is a condensed mapping of persona -> starter config. Use it as the default placement during self-serve or first SE contact.

Persona | Default runtime | Model variant | Quantization | Warm capacity | SLO target (short) | Notes
-------|-----------------|---------------|--------------|---------------|--------------------|------
Developer Sandbox | Hosted (on-demand) | variant-econ-1 | 8-bit dynamic | 0 | best-effort | Fast iteration, enable dev credits
Product Pilot | Hosted / Dedicated trial | variant-mid-1 | 8-bit mixed | small reserve (1–2 GPUs equiv) | p95 300–500ms | Enable KV cache, telemetry preflight
Transactional Prod | Dedicated / Private | variant-high-1 | 16-bit or int8 conservative | reserved pools | p99 150–300ms | Canary routing, SLA negotiation
Batch Embeddings | Dedicated batch nodes | emb-quant-2 | int8 aggressive | ephemeral pool | throughput-based | Bulk ingest tooling + drivers

Technical integration checklist (for Solutions Engineering)
----------------------------------------------------------
1) API keys and RBAC: ensure tenant keys scoped to routes and quotas.
2) Network & VPC (if Private): validate firewall rules, KMS integration, and egress policies.
3) Telemetry hooks: verify token-level and route-level metrics stream to customer console and Redwood telemetry service.
4) Prompt set & sample data: run Redwood baseline prompt set and capture gold/reference outputs.
5) Cost estimator run: execute the cost estimation tool with expected QPS and sequence-length distribution.

Example cost-estimator CLI invocation:
$ redwood cost-estimate --qps 50 --avg-tokens 120 --model variant-mid-1 --duration 30d --output report.pdf

SLA & pricing implications
-------------------------
- Starter profiles are priced at the hosted per-token rates with quota protections.
- Transition to Dedicated increases predictability at the cost of reserved-CPU/GPU fees — map the step-up tiers in the onboarding wizard.
- When moving from a low- to high-fidelity variant, present the estimated cost delta (per million tokens) plus expected latency improvements and a short A/B test plan.

Telemetry & success metrics (30 / 60 / 90 day)
--------------------------------------------
- 30d: integration completed; telemetry coverage > 95% of routes; baseline quality metrics recorded.
- 60d: cost vs baseline within expected envelope; p95 latency trending toward target; fewer than 5% regeneration requests.
- 90d: decision milestone (stay hosted, purchase Dedicated, request Private). Customer success NPS check.

Rollout plan & ownership
------------------------
- Product: maintain persona-to-profile mapping and UI for self-serve selection (owner: Product).
- Solutions Engineering: own pilot validation and canary run books (owner: Solutions Eng).
- Developer Success: monitor telemetry SLOs and close 30/60/90 checkpoints (owner: Dev Success).
- Engineering: provide Optimize suggestions and telemetry endpoints (owner: Eng-Platform).

Decision matrix: when to recommend Dedicated/Private
---------------------------------------------------
- Recommend Dedicated when: sustained QPS > 300, p99 latency requirement < 400ms, or tenant requests data isolation.
- Recommend Private when: regulated data (PII/PHI), strict on-prem requirements, or contractual security needs.

Appendix A: sample API request and preflight test
------------------------------------------------
- Sample generation request to validate latency and token accounting:
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <TENANT_KEY>
Body:
{
  "model": "variant-mid-1",
  "input": "Summarize customer support thread and extract intent",
  "max_tokens": 120,
  "temperature": 0.2
}
- Preflight pass criteria:
  1) Successful request within p95 latency target.
  2) Token accounting matches estimator (+/- 5%).
  3) Output quality above threshold on reference prompts.

Appendix B: quick decision FAQ
-----------------------------
Q: If a tenant wants to reduce cost immediately, what do we do?
A: Suggest enabling prefix caching and switching to an economy variant for non-critical routes. Run a 7-day A/B to validate quality delta.

Q: How aggressive should quantization be for embeddings?
A: Start with int8 mixed for pilots. For bulk ingestion, run a 2-week embedding-similarity validation against a held-out set and only move to int8 aggressive if cosine similarity degradation < 0.01.

Related docs and artifacts
--------------------------
- Developer onboarding SDK snippets (link pinned in welcome email).
- Cost estimator UI and backend (internal API ID: cost-est-2026).
- Redwood baseline prompt set (rbw-baseline-prompts-v2).

Ownership & next steps
----------------------
- Product to add persona selection into the new onboarding UI by 2027-03-14.
- Solutions Engineering to produce three persona-specific onboarding templates by 2027-03-01.
- Engineering to expose an API flag to auto-apply persona profiles (ticket: ENG-4268).

title: dsid_b0e6bd57f56c4f8f91a806acf3f3e39a__technical-health-sentinel-and-ops-handbook-2026.txt
text:
Technical Health Sentinel: Enterprise Post-Provision Monitoring & QBR Feed Playbook

Summary
=======
This playbook defines the Technical Health Sentinel (THS): a prescriptive set of telemetry monitors, smoke checks, and QBR signal extractions that Customer Success (CS) uses for enterprise post-provision monitoring (first 90 days + quarterly health reviews). THS is intended to catch operational, performance, and quality regressions before they impact the customer and to provide a repeatable set of artifacts and dashboards for QBRs.

Goals
-----
- Detect regressions in availability, latency, correctness, and cost within 1 business hour of occurrence.
- Provide a structured triage path to resolve common classes of customer-impacting issues within SLOs.
- Standardize QBR inputs so CS and Product can make data-driven decisions.

When to use this playbook
------------------------
Use THS for:
- All enterprise customers during the 90-day post-provision window.
- Any Dedicated or Private deployment cutoff (when handing over to customer ops).
- Ongoing QBR preparation for customers with >$5k/month spend or latencies close to SLO.

Definitions and ownership
-------------------------
- THS Owner: Customer Success (Primary) — Maya Chen (authored).
- Technical Escalation: Eng-SRE (secondary) — Pager rotations in #oncall-redwood.
- Model/Quality Escalation: Applied ML & Evals team.
- Observability & Dashboards: Eng-Platform owns instrumentation.
- Data retention for QBR artifacts: Finance/Legal policy defines how long telemetries can be stored, default 18 months.

High-level workflow
-------------------
1. Post-provision (days 0–14): enable THS baseline monitors and run onboarding smoke tests.
2. Stabilization (days 15–90): monitor trends, perform weekly health reviews, fix configuration/backfills.
3. Handover / QBR (day 90 and quarterly): produce QBR packet with THS extracts and recommendations.

Automated sentinel monitors (recommended list)
----------------------------------------------
We recommend creating these monitors in the customer’s telemetry workspace (or forward via telemetry-gatekeeper):
- Availability check (heartbeat) — frequency: 30s; threshold: missing 3 samples -> P1 alarm.
- Request error rate — window: 5m; P99 target: < 0.5% (critical if > 1.5% for 5m).
- Tail latency (95th/99th) — window: 5m; thresholds: 95p > 350ms for hosted small models or > 700ms for long-context models -> P2.
- Token-level throughput / saturation — window: 1m; alert when GPU utilization > 88% and queue length grows > 12 requests.
- Model quality delta (eval set drift) — daily job comparing baseline eval set (seeded prompts) -> trigger when BLEU/ROUGE/metric drops > 4 points or human-quality score drops >10%.
- Cost per 1k tokens anomaly — daily; notify on >30% variance vs baseline 7-day median.
- KV cache hit rate — window: 15m; target: depends on workload, recommend > 60% for chat-heavy prefixes; alert if < 40% and latency increases.
- Telemetry forwarding lag — window: 5m; alert if event lag > 2m (indicates tracing / ingestion problem).

Alert severity mapping
----------------------
- P1 (customer-visible outage): availability fail, persistent error rate >5% for 15m, or model-serving API returning 5xx for >10% of requests. Assign to Eng-SRE tower.
- P2 (degradation): tail latency exceeded, cost spike, or quality regression in golden set; owner: Customer Success + Eng Platform.
- P3 (informational): telemetry lag, non-impacting config drift. Owner: Customer Success.

Pre-go-live health gates (checklist)
-----------------------------------
Run these before the customer is marked "go-live" in the billing system:  
1) Smoke traffic test — ramp to 2x expected peak for 10m with synthetic prompts (document payloads).
2) Model correctness gate — run golden prompt set (example: 100 prompts) and compare aggregated pass rate vs baseline (>92%).
3) Latency SLO verification — 95p latency under target for 30m sustained.
4) Telemetry sanity — traces, logs, and metrics flowing; sample trace includes request id, model version, node id.
5) Failover drill — force a single-node outage and validate automatic fallback to warm pool within 60s.
6) Billing & quotas check — verify token accounting matches expected.

Playbook: Common scenarios and triage steps
-----------------------------------------
Scenario A: Latency spike on customer route
1. Confirm alert and scope: check route_id, model_version, region.
2. Validate ingestion: Confirm no ingestion lag (telemetry lag monitor).
3. Check GPU & host metrics: utilization, memory errors, host load. Command examples:
   - kubectl -n runtime get pods -l route=<route_id>
   - query: sum(rate(gpu_utilization[1m])) by (instance)
4. Verify KV cache hit rate and batching behavior; if hit rate drops, identify cache-miss prefix regression.
5. If hosts saturated and autoscale not triggering, run: rwdctl scale --route <route_id> --delta 2 (Eng-Platform only).
6. If root cause is model variant change, rollback to previous pinned model_version via console or API.
7. Communicate to customer: status update within 15 minutes for P1/P2.

Scenario B: Quality regression detected by eval harness
1. Confirm regression on seeded prompts and a random sample of live requests (sanitized).
2. If reproducible, pin traffic to previous model variant immediately and open a ticket to Applied ML.
3. Run localized A/B (5% traffic) comparing outputs and log label for failed prompts.
4. Produce QBR-quality artifact: sampling of 30 representative failures + 5 human annotations.

Scenario C: Unexpected cost anomaly
1. Validate anomaly: cross-check billing pipeline and usage catalyst (7-day median).
2. Check client-side changes: prompt length, new embeddings/long-context usage, and new batch jobs.
3. If runaway jobs present, temporarily apply quota hold at route level and notify customer.
4. Reconfigure batching or suggest quantization profile (Eng-Platform assisted).

Escalation & communication templates
----------------------------------
Use the following cadence and channels:
- T+0–15m: Acknowledge to customer via designated channel (Slack/email) with immediate mitigation steps.
- T+15–60m: Cause analysis summary and expected ETA.
- T+60m+: Regular updates every 30–60m until resolved.
- Post-mortem: deliver within 3 business days for P1; 7 business days for P2.

Template: initial customer message (P1)
"We’ve detected an availability issue impacting your inference route <route_id>. Our mitigation team is engaged; we’ve rerouted traffic and are working on a fix. We will follow up within 15 minutes with an ETA. Contact: Maya Chen (CS), Eng-SRE oncall."

Observability artifacts & queries (examples)
-------------------------------------------
Prometheus/Datadog example queries you should include in the shared dashboard: 
- 95th latency: p95(api_request_duration_ms{route_id=\"<route_id>\"})
- Error rate over 5m: increase(error_count{route_id=\"<route_id>\"}[5m]) / increase(request_count{route_id=\"<route_id>\"}[5m])
- Token cost: sum(rate(token_emitted_total{route_id=\"<route_id>\"}[1m])) * cost_per_token
- KV cache hit rate: sum(kv_cache_hits{route_id=\"<route_id>\"}) / sum(kv_cache_lookups{route_id=\"<route_id>\"})

Example alert JSON (ingestable by gatekeeper)
---------------------------------------------
{
  "name": "THS - High 95p latency - <route_id>",
  "expr": "p95(api_request_duration_ms{route_id=\\\"<route_id>\\\"}) > 350",
  "for": "5m",
  "severity": "P2",
  "owners": ["customer-success:maya.chen", "eng-platform:oncall"]
}

QBR feed and required metrics
----------------------------
Prepare the following artifacts for every QBR packet:
- Executive summary (1 page): availability, cost delta, net customer impact.
- Key metrics (30/90/365 day views):
  - Availability (percent uptime), target: 99.95% for hosted; 99.9% for Dedicated.
  - 95p / 99p latency by route and model.
  - Error rate (5m and 30d rolling).
  - Cost per 1k tokens and trend delta vs prior quarter.
  - Quality regressions count and triaged outcomes.
- Recent incidents and status of action items.
- Recommendations: batching, cache tuning, suggested model quantization, or Dedicated capacity increase.

Dashboard export checklist (what to attach)
- Time-range: include 30-, 90-, and 365-day graphs.
- Raw samples: 200 sample request/response pairs with PII removed (sanitization script included below).
- Alert history: print last 90 days of alerts with state changes.

Sanitization script (python snippet)
-----------------------------------
# This script removes obvious PII fields from JSON payloads. Run before attaching samples.
import json, re
PII_KEYS = ["email", "ssn", "phone", "credit_card"]
pat = re.compile(r'\\b\\w+@\\w+\\.\\w+\\b')

def sanitize(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: ("<REDACTED>" if k in PII_KEYS else sanitize(v)) for k,v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return [sanitize(x) for x in obj]
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        return pat.sub('<REDACTED_EMAIL>', obj)
    return obj

Operational handoff & runbooks
------------------------------
- Day-90 handoff package must include: route configuration export, pinned model_version, telemetry dashboard links, escalation contacts, and artifact bundle (sanitized samples + eval results).
- Handoff checklist: owner signs off that remaining action items have owners and due dates.

Template: Day-90 Handover checklist (table)
- Route config export: yes/no
- Golden set baseline: attached
- Alerts enabled: list
- SLOs documented: yes/no and values
- Cost controls: quotas set (amount)

Known limitations & caveats
--------------------------
- Quality regression detection relies on seeded prompt sets — novel prompts from end-users may still cause silent regressions.
- Telemetry sampling rates may omit cold-start anomalies; we recommend 100% sampling for first 24 hours post-go-live.
- Private deployments with restricted networking may delay telemetry; adjust lag thresholds accordingly.

Appendix: Quick links & contacts
--------------------------------
- Oncall channel: #oncall-redwood (Slack)
- Incident creation: /inc create (internal CLI)
- Telemetry gatekeeper doc: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts
- CS leads: maya.chen@redwood.com, diego.alvarez@redwood.com

Change log
----------
- 2025-11-10: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2026-01-22: Added KV cache guidance and cost anomaly playbook (review: Diego Alvarez).
- 2026-02-15: Finalized QBR feed list and added templated alert JSON (published).

Acknowledgements
----------------
Thanks to Eng-SRE (Jordan Blake) and Eng-Platform (Priya Nair) for monitoring requirements and thresholds.

title: dsid_ff703ca648084e8c90eb628f2a4e650a__postmortem-automation-and-action-tracker-playbook-2026.txt
text:
Postmortem Automation and Action Tracker Playbook

Overview:

This playbook defines a repeatable, partially automated postmortem and action-tracking workflow for LLM-serving incidents. It is intended for SREs, service owners, responders, and incident reviewers. The goal is to reduce manual overhead during incident writeups, ensure forensic evidence is captured consistently, and close post-incident actions within defined SLAs.

Goals:
- Reduce postmortem turnaround time (trigger -> draft) to under 48 hours for Sev2+ incidents.
- Ensure automated capture of the evidence pack with >95% fidelity for tokenized requests, KV cache state, autoscaler events, and model rollbacks.
- Track and close actions with measurable SLAs (see Action SLAs).
- Provide standard templates for internal review and customer-facing summaries.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all incidents that meet the severity threshold: Sev2 (partial customer impact) and Sev1 (major outage).
- Does not replace runbook-specific operational remediation steps; it complements incident runloop documentation and the existing runbook library.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Evidence Pack: A timeboxed collection of logs, traces, config snapshots, model version manifests, and autoscaler metrics gathered automatically at incident detection + user-specified time window.
- PM Draft: A skeleton postmortem automatically generated with timeline, evidence pointers, and initial action items.
- Action Tracker: A canonical table (tracked in JIRA/Confluence) with closure SLAs and owner assignments.

Automated evidence collection (recommended implementation):
1) Trigger points
   - On active incident creation in PagerDuty (PD), an automation webhook triggers the Evidence Pack collector.
   - Manual trigger from the bridge operator is supported (slash command: /collect-evidence).
2) Collector outputs (zip)
   - service-logs.jsonl (NGINX/ingress, api-gateway)
   - inference-requests-sample.ndjson (sampled requests with redaction)
   - kv-cache-snapshot.json (state for hot clients within timeframe)
   - model-manifest.txt (model versions and quantization profile in use)
   - autoscaler-events.csv (scale-up/scale-down events)
   - trace-span-ids.txt (top 100 slow traces)
   - metrics-export.prom (time-windowed Prometheus slice)
3) Storage and access
   - Collected evidence is pushed to S3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/<timestamp>/ with a lifecycle tag 'incident:hold' for 90 days.
   - A signed read-only URL is attached to the PM Draft and to the incident ticket.

Collector example (CLI):
- To run manually from ops laptop:
  ./tools/collect-evidence 
    --incident-id PD12345 
    --start "2026-07-03T02:00:00Z" 
    --end "2026-07-03T03:30:00Z" 
    --samples 200 
    --redact-keys authorization,credit_card

Automated postmortem draft generation (workflow):
1) Incident declared (PagerDuty severity >= 2) -> webhook triggers PM generator.
2) PM generator creates a Confluence page under /oncall-and-incident-response/incidents/<incident-id> with the following seeded sections: 
   - Summary (1-2 sentences auto-composed from incident title and tags)
   - Timeline (auto-extracted events from traces and autoscaler events)
   - Evidence Pack link(s)
   - Initial action suggestions (automatically inferred using keywords: rollback, configuration, capacity, model-quality)
   - Suggested owners (based on oncall roster and recent commit metadata)
3) Bridge operator fills gaps and marks PM as "draft ready".

Timeline extraction heuristics (implementation notes):
- Use trace sampling + ingress timestamps. Prefer the earliest request timestamp with error response rate >5% as the start marker for partial degradations.
- Autoscaler spikes that correlate with latency > p95 are annotated as contributing events.

Action Tracker schema (single canonical table stored in Confluence and mirrored to JIRA project RID-ACT):
| action_id | summary | owner | severity | due_date | status | evidence_link | closure_notes | created_by | created_at |
|----------:|---------|-------|---------:|---------:|-------:|---------------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| ACT-0001  | Rotate model to v2 | @mxavier | 2 | 2026-07-10 | open | s3://... | | ada.team | 2026-07-03 |

Notes on fields (must be applied to every action row):
- action_id: Prefer JIRA issue key when mirrored; if not present, canonical ACT-000n id is assigned.
- severity: 1 (urgent), 2 (important), 3 (nice-to-have).
- due_date: ISO format. Actions without a due_date default to 30 days for severity 3, 14 days for severity 2, and 7 days for severity 1.
- evidence_link: link back to Evidence Pack or a specific file within it.

Action SLAs and escalation:
- Severity 1: owner must acknowledge within 4 hours, provide a mitigation plan within 24 hours, and close or transition within 7 days.
- Severity 2: owner acknowledges within 48 hours, mitigation plan within 7 days, close within 14 days.
- Unresolved actions beyond SLA are auto-escalated to the incident steward and copied to the owner’s manager on day+1 overdue.

Runbook: Automated PM generation — step-by-step (operator-facing):
1) Confirm incident classification and PD ticket.
2) Run or verify Evidence Pack collection (CLI or /collect-evidence). Verify S3 link is present.
3) Execute PM generation job (internal script):
   - /scripts/generate_pm --incident PD12345 --evidence s3://... --template standard
4) Review auto-populated sections, correct factual errors, add human-readable context, and list any immediate action items.
5) Assign actions in the Action Tracker and create linked JIRA issues for severity 1 items (use project RID-ACT).
6) Mark the postmortem state: draft -> in_review -> published. Assign 2 reviewers (one SRE, one Service Owner).

Reviewer expectations and checklist:
- Verify timeline accuracy: confirm timestamps and event causality.
- Validate evidence pack completeness: logs, traces, model metadata.
- Assess action quality: clear owner, measurable acceptance criteria, and due date.
- Confirm customer-facing summary is concise and avoids technical noise.

Customer communication templates (brief & editable):
- Short status update (to use on status.redwood.ai or customer e-mail):
  Subject: Incident PD12345 — Degraded API latency (Resolved)
  Body: 
  Hello —
  We experienced increased latency for text generation requests between 02:15 and 03:25 UTC on 2026-07-03 affecting ~12% of requests. Root cause: an autoscaler configuration regression that delayed warmup for burst traffic.
  What we did: Rolled back the most recent autoscaler config and restarted the gateway group.
  Next steps: We have created an action to add pre-warm scaling in our autoscaler policy (ACT-0001); estimated remediation complete by 2026-07-10.
  If you experienced client errors, please reach out to support@redwood.ai with your request IDs.

Internal status page copy (concise):
- Title: PD12345 — Inference latency spike (Resolved)
- Short: Latency spike caused by autoscaler regression; rollback applied.
- Impact window: 2026-07-03T02:15:00Z -> 2026-07-03T03:25:00Z

Game day and continuous improvement loop:
- Quarterly game day should include at least one scenario where the Evidence Pack collector is the primary verification tool (failure to collect is a failure mode).
- Post-game-day artifacts: ensure PM generator templates are updated and action tracker is pruned.

Operational ownership and tooling map (examples):
- PagerDuty: service-oncall@redwood (PD schedule: SRE rotation)
- Bridge: #incident-bridge channel in Slack; use react :triage: to indicate bridge operator presence.
- Evidence collector: tools/collect-evidence (owned by eng-infra)
- PM generator: jobs/generate_pm (owned by eng-sre)
- Action mirror: JIRA project RID-ACT (owned by eng-platform)

Retention and compliance notes:
- Evidence packs are retained 90 days by default, flagged for longer retention on customer-sensitive incidents (escalate to security/legal for 2-year retention).
- Redaction is required for PII and secrets. The collector supports a redact-keys list; default redact list: authorization, cookie, credit_card, ssn.

Metrics and KPIs (dashboard suggestions):
- PM generation latency (incident -> draft) median and 95th percentile.
- Percentage of incidents with Evidence Pack present at draft creation.
- Action closure rate by severity at 7/14/30 day marks.

Appendix A — Implementation tips and sample queries:
- Prometheus slice example: 
  curl -s 'https://prometheus.redwood/api/v1/query_range?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="inference-api"}[5m])) by (le))&start=...&end=...&step=30s' 
- Trace extraction (example): query traces with error count > 5 in timeframe and export top 100 trace ids: 
  ./tools/trace-cli export --service inference-api --start ... --end ... --errors-only --top 100 > trace-span-ids.txt

Appendix B — Sample PM skeleton (auto-produced):
- Title: PD12345 — Inference latency spike (Resolved)
- Summary: Short auto-summary here
- Timeline: auto-extracted events (timestamps and short descriptions)
- Evidence: S3 links to evidence pack
- Actions: seeded actions with suggested owners
- Reviewers: auto-suggested reviewers (SRE oncall, Service Owner)

Appendix C — Troubleshooting collector failures:
1) Common failure: missing logs for a region. Action: verify log ingestion agents (fluentd) and re-run collector with --force-historical-fetch.
2) Common failure: redact keys removed important request headers. Action: re-run collector with redact-keys override and keep derivative token IDs only.

Contact and escalation list:
- Incident steward: oncall-steward@redwood.ai
- Evidence tooling owner: eng-infra@redwood.ai
- Legal & compliance (for retention overrides): compliance@redwood.ai

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: Created by Maya Chen (initial automation spec).
- 2026-07-03: Updates to Action SLA and evidence retention (reviewed by Ethan Brooks).

End of document.

title: dsid_4b1ea86f575f4a8ab1c0abc51572ca05__lifecycle-growth-experiments-sprint-brief.txt
text:
Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (4 weeks) — Sprint Brief

## Summary
This sprint is a 4-week, cross-functional Growth + Product effort to improve self-serve activation and early retention for the **Hosted API**.

We will run a tightly-instrumented set of experiments across:
- **Lifecycle email:** onboarding drip v2
- **Console:** contextual onboarding nudges (feature-flagged)
- **Paid retargeting:** conservative audiences focused on re-engaging non-activated and early-activated users

This is a measurement-first sprint: we are prioritizing clean event taxonomy, holdouts, and decision criteria to avoid “noisy” learnings.

---

## Sprint goals (what success looks like)
### Primary activation goals
Within **7 days** of signup:
1) Increase **% of new signups completing a first successful request**
2) Increase **% of new signups reaching the first 100k tokens milestone**

### Secondary goals
- Reduce **time-to-first-token (TTFT)** and “time-to-value” (time from signup to first successful response)
- Improve **D7 and D30 active usage** for new cohorts
- Improve downstream conversion signals (upgrade intent / sales-assisted handoff when appropriate)

### Decision outcomes required by end of Week 4
For each experiment, produce a clear **keep / iterate / kill** recommendation, plus the follow-on backlog.

---

## KPI definitions (operational)
**Activation funnel milestones** (all measured at the user + org level):
- **Signup**: account created event (deduped)
- **API key created**: first API key created via Console or API
- **First successful request**: first 2xx response from Hosted API generation/chat/embeddings endpoints (excluding health checks)
- **First 100k tokens**: cumulative tokens served for the org reaches 100k

**Primary metrics**
- **Activation-1 (A1)**: % of new signups with first successful request within 7 days
- **Activation-2 (A2)**: % of new signups reaching first 100k tokens within 7 days

**Secondary metrics**
- **Median time to first successful request** (and P75)
- **Median TTFT** for first request (and P75)
- **D7 active**: org has any Hosted API usage on day 7 (local time) after signup
- **D30 active**: org has any Hosted API usage on day 30 after signup

**Reporting notes**
- We will use cohort-based reporting by signup date; all funnel steps must use the standardized lifecycle event taxonomy and dedupe rules.
- We will always report overall + segmented by: region, SDK vs raw HTTP, use-case endpoint family (chat vs embeddings), and first-day token volume bucket.

---

## Hypotheses (what we believe)
1) **Reducing “first request” friction** will drive a measurable lift in A1 and reduce time-to-value.
2) **Contextual next-step guidance in Console** will reduce drop-off between API key creation → first request.
3) **Timely, targeted lifecycle email** will re-engage stalled signups (no API key / no first request) without harming deliverability or support load.
4) **Conservative retargeting** can bring back signup-no-activation users and activated-but-no-return users at acceptable CPA, without interfering with active enterprise opportunities.

---

## Scope
### In scope
- Email onboarding drip v2: copy, timing, trigger logic, segmentation, compliance hooks
- Console nudges: placements, targeting rules, feature flags, dismissal persistence, UX/copy iteration
- Retargeting: audience definitions, creative briefs, UTMs, spend caps, exclusions for enterprise opps
- Measurement: event taxonomy, dashboards, experiment design, weekly readouts

### Out of scope
- Major product re-architecture
- Pricing/packaging changes
- Large-scale docs replatforming (docs updates limited to onboarding alignment and quickstart fixes)

---

## Experiment principles
- **Holdout by default**: where possible, maintain a clean holdout group per channel.
- **No overlapping interventions without intent**: avoid sending multiple conflicting nudges/emails to the same cohort without explicitly testing the combination.
- **Guardrails are enforced**: deliverability and compliance thresholds can pause experiments.
- **Bias for fast iteration**: ship v1 quickly, learn, then iterate within sprint constraints.

---

## Experiments (planned)
The following experiments are the planned “spine” of the sprint. Details live in the linked design specs.

### Experiment list (overview table)
| ID | Channel | Hypothesis | Target cohort | Variants | Primary metric | Duration | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | Email | Triggered onboarding emails reduce stalled signup drop-off | New signups (self-serve) | Control vs Drip v2 | A1 within 7d | 7–10 days (rolling) | Ben Carter |
| E2 | Email | Segmented “stalled” sequences outperform generic onboarding | No API key at +2h; No first request at +24h | Timing/CTA variant A vs B | A1 within 7d + time-to-value | 7–10 days | Ben Carter |
| C1 | Console nudge | “Create API key” nudge reduces signup → key drop-off | Signed in; no API key | Nudge vs holdout | API key creation rate | 5–7 days | Marissa Cole |
| C2 | Console nudge | “Run first request” nudge increases first successful request | Has API key; no successful request | Nudge vs holdout | A1 within 7d | 5–7 days | Marissa Cole |
| C3 | Console nudge | Streaming guidance accelerates TTFT and perceived speed | First-time requesters | Nudge vs none | time-to-value + TTFT (P75) | 7 days | Marissa Cole |
| R1 | Retargeting | Retargeting recovers signup-no-activation at acceptable CPA | Signup-no-activation (7d lookback) | Creative set A vs B | A1 within 7d + CPA | 10–14 days | Tyler Benson |
| R2 | Retargeting | Retargeting activated-but-no-return increases D7 activity | Activated; inactive for 3–7 days | Creative set A vs B | D7 active + CPA | 10–14 days | Tyler Benson |

Notes:
- Email and Console experiments must share consistent event definitions and cohort IDs for attribution.
- Retargeting will use strict exclusions (see Guardrails) and conservative lookback windows.

---

## Measurement & instrumentation
### Event taxonomy and required properties
All lifecycle events must include, at minimum:
- user_id, org_id
- event_time (UTC)
- source (console | api | email)
- environment (prod)
- region
- experiment_cohort_id (if eligible)
- experiment_id + variant (when applicable)

### Funnel dashboard requirements
Dashboards must support:
- Funnel conversion rates (signup → key → first request → 100k tokens)
- Time-to-step distributions (median, P75)
- Breakdowns: region, acquisition source, SDK usage, endpoint family
- Alerts for sudden step regressions after experiment launches

### Attribution rules (high-level)
- Email: attribute to email variant if user was eligible and received the email prior to the relevant step.
- Console: attribute to nudge variant if user was eligible and saw the nudge prior to the relevant step.
- Retargeting: measure incremental lift using holdout where feasible; otherwise conservative interpretation with UTM-based directional signals.

---

## Guardrails (must not break)
### Deliverability (email)
Pause or ramp down if any threshold is exceeded (rolling 24–48h, Marketing Ops to validate):
- Complaint rate > **0.15%**
- Hard bounce rate > **1.0%**
- Unsubscribe rate > **1.5%** on any single send
- “Not receiving onboarding email” support tickets spike (qualitative escalation)

Mitigations:
- Throttle ramps by cohort size; warm-up domains; list hygiene checks
- Suppress re-sends for users who already activated (API key or first request)

### Compliance
- CAN-SPAM: functional unsubscribe in every lifecycle email
- GDPR: respect consent/opt-out; audience usage adheres to internal data handling policy
- Ensure preference updates propagate to all sending systems and are reflected in Console

### Retargeting safeguards
- Exclude:
  - Active enterprise opportunities (as defined by Sales leadership)
  - Sensitive/regulated accounts flagged by Sales/Compliance
  - Known high-intent inbound leads routed to sales-assisted flows (avoid conflicting messaging)
- Spend caps (initial): daily cap + total sprint cap per channel (approved by Exec Sponsor)

### Product/Support load
- If a nudge causes a functional regression (e.g., blocks API key creation), roll back within **2 hours** of confirmation.
- If support tickets for onboarding issues increase materially week-over-week, triage immediately with Console + Growth.

---

## Owners & operating cadence
### Core owners
- Experiment owner (overall): **Ben Carter**
- Executive sponsor: **Camila Reyes**
- Messaging review: **Soojin Lee**
- Console surface area: **Marissa Cole**
- Telemetry/rollout input: **Paula Mendes**
- Marketing ops & attribution: **Tyler Benson**
- Sales exclusions & handoff rules: **Jordan Blake**, **Stephanie Nguyen**
- Privacy/legal review: **Michael Grant**, **Olga Petrov**

### Weekly cadence
- Mon: instrument + launch checklist review; go/no-go decisions
- Mid-week: monitor guardrails and early signals (deliverability, CTR, funnel sanity)
- Fri: experiment readout and decisioning (keep/iterate/kill)

---

## Timeline (by week)
### Week 1 — Definitions + first email launch
Deliverables:
- Final KPI definitions + taxonomy alignment
- Dashboard v1 live with baseline cohort
- Email onboarding drip v2 copy finalized + compliance review
- Launch first email A/B (E1)

### Week 2 — Console nudge framework + first nudge
Deliverables:
- Nudge component + feature flag targeting + holdout mechanics
- QA pass on nudge placement and dismissal persistence
- Launch first nudge experiment (C1) and/or (C2)

### Week 3 — Retargeting launch + refine
Deliverables:
- Retargeting audiences live + exclusions validated with Sales
- Creatives shipped + landing pages mapped + UTMs standardized
- Spend/CPA monitoring; iterate creative/audiences as needed

### Week 4 — Consolidated analysis + recommendations
Deliverables:
- Consolidated readout with channel-by-channel and combined effects
- Recommendations and rollout plan for “always-on” wins
- Follow-on backlog with sizing + dependencies

---

## Launch checklist (minimum bar)
Before any experiment goes live:
1) Event emission verified in at least two regions; dedupe confirmed
2) Dashboard shows expected counts vs baseline (sanity check)
3) Holdout definition confirmed and documented
4) Guardrails monitored with named on-call owner (deliverability + funnel health)
5) Sales exclusions applied for retargeting audiences (signed off by Sales leadership)
6) Unsubscribe/preference handling validated end-to-end

---

## Risks & mitigations
- **Risk: Event tracking discrepancies skew results** → Mitigation: pre-launch sanity queries; compare API logs vs analytics; pause interpretation until resolved.
- **Risk: Email deliverability degradation** → Mitigation: conservative ramps, list hygiene, monitoring thresholds, escalation path to deliverability support.
- **Risk: Console nudge UX regressions** → Mitigation: feature flags + rapid rollback; QA for edge cases; monitor support.
- **Risk: Retargeting conflicts with enterprise motion** → Mitigation: strict exclusions and weekly sync with Sales; suppress by domain and active opp list.

---

## Open questions (tracked during Week 1)
- What is the default “time window” for considering a user “stalled” for each trigger (2h/24h/72h)?
- Which landing page performs best for retargeting: Console login, quickstart doc, or minimal “hello world” template?
- Do we treat “first successful request” as any endpoint or only chat/generation? (Default: any core inference endpoint; exclude health checks.)

---

## References
- Email onboarding drip v2 spec: /product-docs/design-specs/email-onboarding-drip-v2
- Console nudge framework: /product-docs/design-specs/console-onboarding-nudges-experiment-framework
- Activation/Retention theme (Q1 2026): /product-docs/roadmap-and-themes/q1-2026-activation-retention-theme
- Data handling policy (lifecycle + retargeting): /policies-and-process/data-management/lifecycle-email-retargeting-data-handling
- Messaging guidelines (Hosted API): /sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/onboarding-messaging-guidelines-hosted-api

title: dsid_fe766bb74c374d6b81b8d1e8c41c000b__probabilistic-capacity-forecasting-and-allocation-spec-2025.txt
text:
Probabilistic Capacity Forecasting and Allocation Spec

Summary
-------
This document specifies the probabilistic capacity forecasting and automated allocation system used to allocate GPU and CPU capacity across Redwood's inference pools. The aim is to convert time-series telemetry and business-level signals into a daily probabilistic demand distribution, map that distribution to allocation decisions (reserved, burst, and standby), and expose human-friendly dashboards and runbooks for operators.

Scope
-----
- Applies to: hosted/high-throughput inference fleets (all GPU classes), dedicated pools, and the regional burst fabric.
- Out of scope: spot-instance provisioning for experimental clusters, and per-customer pricing decisions (handled by finance).

Goals
-----
1. Provide a 7- and 30-day probabilistic forecast (median, 75th, 90th, 97.5th percentiles) for per-region and per-instance-type token throughput and concurrent sessions.
2. Produce allocation recommendations: reserved capacity commit and burst-capacity uplift with explicit confidence margins.
3. Flag forecast drift and provide actionable remediation runbooks for the Ops team.
4. Reduce overprovisioning waste by 12% year-over-year while keeping latency SLOs met 99.9% of the time.

Terminology
-----------
- Consumption window: 1-minute bucketing of token-generation requests (tokens/sec).
- P95 concurrency: 95th percentile of concurrent requests sampled every minute.
- Allocation unit: 1 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPU slot. All instance types are normalized to this unit via a compute equivalence table.
- Safety margin: the percent multiplier applied to a percentile forecast to set committed reservation.

Data sources
------------
- telemetry.ingest.tokens (1m) — token counts by tenant, region, model_variant
- infra.metrics.gpu_util (1m) — GPU utilization per instance
- routing.requests.latency (1m) — latency and tail percentiles per route
- tenant.contracts (daily) — reserved commitments and priority tiers
- calendar.holidays (region) — business day adjustments

Modeling approach
-----------------
1. Preprocessing
   - Normalize token throughput into allocation units.
   - Decompose signals: trend, weekly seasonality, daily seasonality, holiday adjustment, anomaly residuals (robust STL).
2. Probabilistic forecasting
   - Use a two-stage hybrid model:
     a) Hierarchical time-series model (Bayesian structural time series, BSTS) at per-tenant postcode aggregated level for long-range uncertainty.
     b) Gradient-boosted quantile regressor (LightGBM quantile objective) for short-term (1-7 day) fine-grained percentile estimates with features for routing hints and model changes.
   - Combine outputs via weighted ensembling with weight decay based on horizon. BSTS weight increases with forecast horizon.
3. Queuing layer
   - Convert throughput forecasts to expected concurrency using an M/G/c approximation per model family that accounts for average generation latency and KV-cache hit rates.
4. Decision layer
   - Map concurrency percentile -> allocation recommendation using capacity-smoothing rules and safety margins defined below.

Decision rules and safety margins
--------------------------------
- Reserved commit = round_up( predicted_concurrency_at_90th_percentile * (1 + reserved_margin) )
- Immediate-burst target = predicted_concurrency_at_97.5th_percentile * (1 + burst_margin)
- Standby (pre-warm) = if predicted P99 latency degradation > 5% at 90p, pre-warm standby nodes equal to 10% of reserved commit
- Default safety margins: reserved_margin = 0.08 (8%), burst_margin = 0.15 (15%). Owners may override per-tenant based on SLA tier.
- Minimum reservation floor: do not downscale reserved commits by more than 20% week-over-week to avoid oscillation.

Allocation API (config example)
-------------------------------
The allocation engine exposes a REST endpoint for proposals and a write API for committing reservations. Example proposal request body (JSON):

```
{
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "instance_type": "A100-80GB",
  "horizon_days": 7,
  "percentiles": [50,75,90,97.5]
}
```

Example response (abbreviated):

```
{
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "instance_type": "A100-80GB",
  "median_alloc_units": 124,
  "p90_alloc_units": 186,
  "recommended_reserved": 201,
  "recommended_burst_target": 234,
  "confidence": "0.90",
  "explanation": "p90*1.08 + tenant_safety_override"
}
```

Dashboards and alerts
---------------------
Dashboards are split into three views: Fleet Health, Forecast Quality, and Allocation Decisions.
- Fleet Health
  - Live GPU utilization heatmap by region and instance family.
  - Request tail latency P50/P95/P99 stacked.
  - Active burst capacity and pre-warmed standby count.
- Forecast Quality
  - Forecast vs actual banded plot (median, p75, p90) annotated with model version and major feature changes.
  - Calibration curve for probabilistic forecasts (expected exceedance vs observed).
  - Feature drift indicators: KV cache hit rate shift, model_variant mix change.
- Allocation Decisions
  - Time series of recommended_reserved vs committed_reserved.
  - Cost delta estimate (USD/day) vs baseline.
  - Owner annotations for manual overrides.

Alerting rules (examples)
- forecast_drift_high: if mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) on p90 > 12% over a 6-hour window AND calibration shows > 2x expected misses, severity P1 to oncall.
- undercommit_risk: if actual concurrency > recommended_burst_target for > 10 minutes and latency P99 > latency_slo*1.10, open P0 incident runbook.
- overcommit_waste: if committed_reserved > p75_alloc_units * 1.25 for 7 consecutive days, create a ticket to Capacity Optimization board.

Runbook: Forecast drift (operator steps)
----------------------------------------
1. Triage alert and open /incident/capacity with snapshot (automated from dashboard).
2. Pull model diagnostics (model_version, feature_histograms) from forecasting service.
3. Check for upstream events:
   - Deployment of new model variants in the last 24h
   - Marketing/partner events (customer list from tenant.contracts)
   - Cloud provider instance interruptions
4. Remediation paths:
   - Short-term: apply burst uplift (API) to region/instance_type and raise priority.
   - Medium-term: increase reserved_margin from 8% to 20% for affected tenants and schedule a capacity commit.
   - Long-term: retrain quantile model with the last 14 days and re-evaluate BSTS hyperparameters.
5. Postmortem: capture root cause and update the calibration chart explanation tag.

Simulation & validation
-----------------------
We require backtest validation over the previous 12 months and forward-simulation for 30 days using synthetic surge scenarios (1.5x and 3x sustained spikes). Acceptance criteria:
- Median absolute error on p90 < 10% across regions in backtest.
- No simulated scenario should cause tail-latency SLO breach > 0.5% when burst target is applied.
- Cost regression: expected cost must not increase > 5% relative to baseline for median demand.

Rollout plan (phases)
---------------------
1. Canary (2 regions): run forecasting in read-only 'proposal' mode for 14 days, surface dashboards, no automatic commits.
2. Operator-assist (4 regions): enable proposal -> manual-commit workflow for 30 days. Collect operator feedback.
3. Automated (global): enable automatic commit for non-enterprise tenants with an audit log and daily email digest.

Metrics tracked
---------------
- Forecast calibration (observed exceedance vs expected) per percentile
- Backtest MAPE per region/horizon
- Latency SLO burn attributable to allocation decisions
- Weekly committed_cost vs predicted_cost_savings

Open questions & future work
---------------------------
- Incorporate live queue micro-burst detection (<30s) into allocation decisions.
- Tenant-aware dynamic safety margins using contractual SLAs and historical elasticity.
- Integrate with pricing signals and spot-instance markets for long tail cost reductions.

Ownership & contacts
--------------------
- Primary owner: Platform Capacity & Cost team (pager: #platform-capacity)
- Doc owner: Maya Chen (mayachen@redwood.example)
- Reviewers: Arjun Patel, Leah O'Neil, Diego Alvarez

Appendix: sample queries & local config
---------------------------------------
Sample SQL to build 1m token ingestion series (Postgres/Timescale simplified):

```
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', received_at) as minute,
       region,
       model_variant,
       SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM telemetry_tokens
WHERE received_at >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY minute, region, model_variant;
```

Sample allocation override CLI: 

```
# propose
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","instance_type":"A100-80GB","horizon_days":7}' \
  https://platform-api.internal/v1/capacity/propose

# commit (operator)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","instance_type":"A100-80GB","commit_units":150,"reason":"operator_override - sales event"}' \
  https://platform-api.internal/v1/capacity/commit
```

Change log
----------
- 2025-10-12: Initial spec (Maya Chen)
- 2025-12-03: Added queuing layer and M/G/c conversion notes (Arjun Patel)
- 2026-02-10: Updated safety margins and rollout plan after pilot analysis (Leah O'Neil)

title: dsid_acded13e7fa542958ccb5b211298dd2d__sdk-accelerated-onramp-observability-quickstart-2026.txt
text:
SDK Accelerated Onramp: Observability & Fault Quickstart

Overview

This quickstart documents the recommended observability and fault-handling onramp for new SDK integrations (JS/Python/Go) with Redwood’s hosted and dedicated inference surfaces. It is written for SDK authors, developer productivity engineers, and support engineers who are responsible for onboarding third-party integrations or internal SDK consumers. The goal is a reproducible, low-friction integration that provides high-fidelity telemetry with actionable alerts and a short remediation playbook for common failure modes.

Key outcomes
- Instrumentation baseline: requests, responses, retries, latencies, token counts, and error taxonomy.
- Dashboards and pre-baked alerts for first-contact failures and degradation.
- A short triage checklist + canonical fixes for top 6 issues seen in SDK integrations.
- Safe rollout checklist (canary + dark-launch telemetry).

Owner and scope
- Owner: eng-developer-experience (contact: @aisha.patel).
- Implementation teams: SDK (client) teams and integration owners.
- Applies to: hosted (Redwood API) + Dedicated endpoints + local SDK runtime adapters.

Before you start (prereqs)
1) Access to DX telemetry: Grafana (dx-sdk-observability), Loki (logs), and Honeycomb/Tracing (dx-traces).
2) API key and example tenant environment (staging) with reserved dev tokens.
3) Basic CI with a smoke test that exercises generation and embeddings calls.

Telemetry contract (minimal fields)
- This section lists required events and metrics. Instrumentation must map to our ingestion schema so ingestion rules can reliably parse and route.

Required application metrics (names are canonical; implement exactly):
1) sdk.request.count - counter (tags: sdk_language, sdk_version, route, customer_tier, env)
2) sdk.request.success_count - counter (same tags)
3) sdk.request.error_count - counter (error_class tag; see taxonomy)
4) sdk.request.latency_ms - histogram (p50/p95/p99)
5) sdk.token.outbound - counter (tokens_sent, prompt_vs_prefix tag)
6) sdk.token.inbound - counter (tokens_returned)

Required structured logs (JSON lines)
- event: 'sdk.request'
- fields: timestamp, request_id, sdk_language, sdk_version, route, latency_ms, status_code, error_class, token_sent, token_returned, upstream_model, region

Example log line (JSON)
{"timestamp":"2026-02-10T15:04:05Z","event":"sdk.request","request_id":"req_1234","sdk_language":"python","sdk_version":"1.3.0","route":"generation","latency_ms":142.1,"status_code":200,"error_class":"none","token_sent":84,"token_returned":120,"upstream_model":"gpt-redwood-3b","region":"us-west-2"}

SDK instrumentation snippets
- Python (requests wrapper):

```python
# instrumentation snippet (python)
import time
import requests
import json

def send_with_telemetry(payload, ctx):
    start = time.time()
    r = requests.post(ctx.url, json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {ctx.api_key}"})
    latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
    # emit metric sdk.request.latency_ms and counters via SDK metrics client
    metrics.emit("sdk.request.count", 1, tags=ctx.tags)
    metrics.emit("sdk.request.latency_ms", latency, tags=ctx.tags)
    if r.status_code >= 200 and r.status_code < 300:
        metrics.emit("sdk.request.success_count", 1, tags=ctx.tags)
    else:
        metrics.emit("sdk.request.error_count", 1, tags={**ctx.tags, "error_class": classify_error(r)})
    logs.json("sdk.request", {
        "request_id": ctx.request_id,
        "latency_ms": latency,
        "status_code": r.status_code
    })
    return r.json()
```

Observability artifacts (deliverables)
- Dashboards: dx-sdk-quickstart-overview (latency histograms, success rate, token usage), dx-sdk-errors-by-class, dx-sdk-canary-health.
- Alerts (recommended):
  - ALERT A: SDK integration: error_rate_high
    - Query: increase in sdk.request.error_count over 5m, error_rate > 2% and > 100 calls in 5m.
    - Severity: P2
    - Notify: #sdk-integration, PagerDuty (oncall-sdk).
  - ALERT B: SDK integration: latency_p95_degrade
    - Query: p95(sdk.request.latency_ms) > 750ms for 10m.
    - Severity: P3
  - ALERT C: SDK integration: token_consumption_anomaly
    - Query: tokens_sent per request increases by >3x relative to a rolling 24h baseline.

Safe rollout checklist (canary + telemetry)
1) Dark launch: enable SDK telemetry in production but traffic routed to a canary model variant.
2) Validate p50/p95 against baseline within 10% for 30 minutes.
3) Check error_rate < 0.5% for the canary cohort.
4) Gradually increase to 10% traffic and hold for 60 minutes with A/B telemetry collection.
5) If any alert fires, abort and revert configuration.

Canonical failure modes and remediation (top 6)
1) Authentication failures (401/403)
   - Symptom: immediate error_count spike with error_class=auth_failed and status_code 401.
   - Root causes: expired API keys, token scope mismatch, misconfigured local environment secrets.
   - Fix: rotate staging key; confirm SDK picks up KEY via env var; verify scope via `redwood-cli auth check`.
2) Payload serialization errors (400 / schema mismatch)
   - Symptom: 400 with error_class=bad_request; often caused by malformed JSON or unsupported fields.
   - Fix: run local JSON schema validator (included in SDK: `redwood_sdk.validate(payload)`) and add schema unit tests.
3) Upstream model OOM or capacity fallbacks (5xx with transient spikes)
   - Symptom: 5xx errors with error_class=upstream_capacity or upstream_oom; higher latencies preceding errors.
   - Fix: switch route to a smaller model using routing hints, enable client-side retries with exponential backoff, notify infra (tag: runtime-team).
4) Unbounded token growth (cost anomalies)
   - Symptom: sudden rise in sdk.token.outbound and high token cost alerts.
   - Fix: enable prompt length caps in client, add pre-send token count sample, run regression tests for prompt templates.
5) Streaming connection failures (network flaps)
   - Symptom: stream disconnects, partial responses, repeated reconnection attempts.
   - Fix: implement resumable-streaming logic in SDK (sequence numbers), fall back to non-streaming endpoint, add backoff jitter.
6) Telemetry ingestion mismatch (logs not parsed)
   - Symptom: empty dashboard panels, missing traces for request_id.
   - Fix: confirm log schema keys match ingestion rules (see dx-telemetry-ingest rules), instrument library version used by SDK, redeploy ingestion mapping if required.

Fast triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Verify request_id and correlate logs -> traces -> metrics.
2) Check error class breakdown in last 15m.
3) Confirm SDK version and language tag in telemetry.
4) Reproduce in staging with identical payload if possible.
5) If production impact, follow incident escalation matrix and create an incident in PagerDuty.

Runbook excerpts (commands and dashboards)
- Grafana: open /d/dx-sdk-quickstart-overview?orgId=1&var-env=production
- Trace lookup (Honeycomb): query by trace.tag=request_id:req_1234
- Log tail (Loki): `{app="dx-sdk", env="production", request_id="req_1234"}`
- Rotation (safe key rotate): `redwood-cli keys rotate --env staging --service sdk-integration`

Testing and CI guardrails
- Add golden-case smoke tests that assert success_rate >= 99.5% and p95 latency < 700ms on CI against a staging endpoint.
- Include a telemetry regression test that sends synthetic traces and verifies ingestion within 30s.
- Block merges if telemetry events for an approved smoke request_id are missing.

Appendix: example alert rule (PromQL-like pseudo)
- error_rate_high: 
  sum_over_time(sdk_request_error_count[5m]) / sum_over_time(sdk_request_count[5m]) > 0.02 and sum_over_time(sdk_request_count[5m]) > 100

Common observability resources
- Dashboards: Grafana dx-sdk-quickstart-overview (owner: eng-developer-experience)
- Traces: Honeycomb dataset dx-sdk-traces (owner: eng-platform)
- Logs: Loki index dx-logs (owner: eng-infra)
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/sdk-telemetry-fidelity-audit-and-fix-runbook-2028

Contacts and escalation
- SDK oncall: #sdk-integration (Slack), PagerDuty: oncall-sdk.
- Developer XP owner: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.ai).

Change history
- 2026-02-10: created by Aisha Patel (initial quickstart and canonical fixes).
- 2026-03-01: updated reviewer feedback (added token anomaly thresholds and streaming fallback guidance).

Document notes
- This quickstart is intentionally prescriptive: SDKs should implement the telemetry contract verbatim to allow centralized dashboards and reliable alerting. If a different metric name is required for platform constraints, raise an exception with eng-developer-experience for mapping.

End of document.

title: dsid_1a4cc72fb29d4cb4ae1a957a572c0fb1__company-process-orchestrator-handbook-2031.txt
text:
Company Process Orchestrator Handbook

Overview
--------
This handbook consolidates company-wide processes and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. Its purpose is to provide a single reference for employees and team owners so processes are consistent, auditable, and aligned with Redwood Inference’s reliability, security, and cost objectives.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood staff, contractors, and third-party partners who interact with company systems, purchase goods or services, handle production or customer data, or travel on behalf of Redwood. Exceptions require documented approval from the owning team and People Ops.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege: grant only the minimum access required.
- Clear ownership: every process step must list an owner and an escalation contact.
- Auditability: all requests, approvals, and changes must be recorded in company systems.
- Risk-based controls: higher-risk activities require stronger approvals and more frequent review.
- Simplicity and self-service: common, low-risk tasks should be automated where possible.

1) Access & Permissions
------------------------
Summary: Centralized access requests and periodic access reviews reduce blast radius and help meet compliance requirements.

Roles and owners:
- Access Requester: employee requesting access.
- Approver: team owner or manager (usually the resource owner for the target service).
- Access Admin: identity team / IAM administrators who provision accounts.
- Owner: service or data owner listed in the internal service registry.

Standard process (request -> approval -> provisioning):
1. Submit an Access Request via the Access Portal (link: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/access-portal). Include justification, duration, and required privileges.
2. Manager or Owner approves within 3 business days. Approval must reference least-privilege justification.
3. Access Admin provisions within 24 business hours after approval (SLA).
4. Provisioning event logs create an audit record in the IAM log stream.

Periodic reviews:
- Quarterly access review for production systems. Team owners receive a checklist and must certify current access or submit change requests.
- Emergency access (break-glass) must be time-limited to a maximum of 8 hours and recorded with an incident tag.

title: dsid_a82e8d1c74364a59a73ff90a2625fd51__service-telemetry-and-supplychain-compatibility-matrix-2026.txt
text:
Service Telemetry & Supply-chain Compatibility Matrix for Private Deploys

Overview

This document defines a combined telemetry contract and hardware/software compatibility matrix that field engineers, SREs, and customer integration teams use to validate private (VPC and on-prem) Redwood deployments. The goal is to unify observability acceptance criteria, supply-chain hardware compatibility, and operational guardrails so private deploys meet product SLAs and regulatory requirements while minimizing day-2 surprises.

Scope

- Applies to: Redwood Private control-plane + runtime, customer-managed VPC branches, and on-prem appliance installs.
- Includes: telemetry schemas, retention and sampling contracts; required agent/collector versions; supported NICs, GPUs, firmware baselines; upgrade/rollback safety gates; post-install verification steps.
- Excludes: application-level prompts and customer data policies (see compliance-evidence pages).

Why this matters

- Inconsistent telemetry and unexpected firmware on GPUs or NICs are root causes for 45% of private-deploy incident escalations in 2025.
- A single compatibility matrix reduces ambiguous requirements during procurement and shortens field lead time by ~30%.

Telemetry contract (service-level)

Summary requirements:
- Mandatory metrics (all must be emitted to the local collector within 60s of boot): runtime.request.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), runtime.request.errors.count, runtime.kvcache.hits, runtime.kvcache.misses, gpu.utilization_pct, host.cpu_load_1m.
- Minimum span traces: request.received -> model.load -> token.stream -> response.sent. Span duration must include attributes: tenant_id, model_version, shard_id.
- Log levels: service logs must support structured JSON logs with keys: ts, level, svc, msg, trace_id, request_id.
- Sampling & retention: default trace sampling 5%; high-error routes sample 100% for up to 24 hours. Metric retention: 90 days at 1m resolution, 400 days at 1h resolution for customer-managed long-term retention packages.

Collector/agent versions and configuration

- Required collector: redwood-agent >= 2.4.0 (bundled with private-runtime image 2026.01+).
- Supported exporters: OTLP (gRPC), Prometheus remote_write (optionally to customer-prometheus).
- Example OTLP config snippet (YAML):

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
      http: {}
processors:
  batch: {}
exporters:
  otlp/remote:
    endpoint: "collector.redwood.local:4317"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/remote]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [prometheus, otlp/remote]
```

Compatibility matrix (hardware, firmware, drivers)

This simplified table is the canonical acceptance matrix. Customers must provide inventory with exact SKUs and firmware versions. Any deviation must be flagged to Redwood Professional Services prior to cutover.

| Component | Supported SKU / family | Min firmware / driver | Notes / known issues |
|---|---|---:|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA A100 (PCIe) | GPU firmware 55.XX, NVIDIA driver 525.85+ | PCIe variants require IOMMU workarounds if host BIOS < 2022.6 |
| GPU | NVIDIA H100 SXM | GPU firmware 65.XX, NVIDIA driver 530.30+ | H100 requires UEFI secure boot off for current image (planner: 2026.2 runtime patch) |
| NIC | Mellanox ConnectX-6 | FW 18.30+, OFED 5.6+ | RoCE requires DSCP/Priority map on branch switch |
| Disk | NVMe Samsung PM1733 | FW 3B2QCX0 | Ensure SMART TL margin set to 5% for endurance class C |
| BMC/UEFI | Supermicro X12 series | UEFI 4.1+, BMC 3.2+ | BMC must have remote syslog enabled for warranty telemetry capture |

Acceptance thresholds and tests

Field acceptance consists of the following checks (performed after base install and before tenant handover):
1) Inventory verification: checksum manifest comparing reported device-ids/firmware vs. inventory CSV.
2) Telemetry smoke: emit a full request trace across 1, 10, 100 token loads; verify p95 < 200ms for local L2 model variants and p95 < 400ms for pinned remote variants.
3) KV cache validation: synthetic workload generates 10k prefix requests, expected cache hit ratio >= 0.72.
4) Telemetry completeness: 100% of requests produce a trace_id and logs within 60s; metrics visible in Prometheus and retained for 1 minute at 10s scrape interval.
5) Stress burn-in: 4-hour soak at 60% of projected steady-state QPS with incremental GPU temperature and telemetry sampling checks.

Automated acceptance playbook (CLI)

Run the built-in acceptance script (operator privileges required):

```bash
# from operator host with SSH access to primary controller
./tools/acceptance/run-field-acceptance.sh \--inventory inventory.csv \--collector-endpoint 10.0.1.5:4317 \--soak-duration 14400

# output: acceptance-report-<date>.json
```

Acceptance report schema (flattened JSON fields in output file)
- report_id (string)
- cluster_id (string)
- operator (string)
- pass_fail (string: pass|fail)
- p95_latency_ms (string)
- kvcache_hit_ratio (string)
- missing_telemetry_keys (string, comma-separated)
- incompatible_hardware (string, comma-separated SKUs)
- remediation_action (string)

Day-2 operations: telemetry-first runbook

This runbook complements existing day-2 ops docs by focusing on telemetry-driven troubleshooting.

Alerting thresholds (recommended):
- runtime.request.errors.rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> P1 alert to oncall.
- gpu.utilization_pct > 98% for > 10m and queue-size growth -> action: scale-burst policy.
- telemetry.ingest.lag > 120s -> investigate network egress to collector.

Investigation steps (short):
1) Confirm agent health: `systemctl status redwood-agent` and `redwood-agentctl status`.
2) Check local metrics: `curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep runtime_request` for recent values.
3) Trace fetch: `otel-cli fetch --trace_id <id> --endpoint http://localhost:4318/v1/traces` to retrieve span chain.
4) If missing traces, check firewall rules (TCP 4317 and 4318) and MTU mismatch with NIC vendor drivers.

Upgrade & rollback safety gates for private deployments

Upgrade preflight checks (must pass before any coordinated upgrade):
- Inventory parity check (as above)
- Telemetry integrity: no missing mandatory keys in last 24 hours.
- Sufficient capacity: free GPU headroom >= 20% or validated burst policy.
- Upgrade window: customer-approved maintenance window and snapshot backup (if required by customer A/R policy).

Automated canary flow (recommended):
1) Canary subset: 5% of tenants routed to new runtime image and collector config.
2) 60-minute monitoring window: key metrics (p95 latency, error rate, kvcache hit ratio) compared to baseline using rolling 10m windows.
3) Automatic rollback triggers: p95 increases > 20% OR error rate increase > 0.3% sustained for 5 minutes OR consumer error types matching model-compatibility signature.

Rollback procedure (operator steps):
1) Trigger: Canary failed OR manual decision.
2) Execute: `k8s-rollback --deployment runtime --image <previous> --tenants all` (or use operator handoff for on-prem appliances).
3) Post-rollback verification: run telemetry smoke test and assert previous baselines restored.
4) Incident postmortem: attach acceptance-report and telemetry snapshots to the ticket.

Customer requirements library excerpts (inventory template)

Provide customers with the following CSV columns in advance of any private deployment engagement. Operators should reject manifests missing required fields.

Required CSV columns:
- host_id
- mac_address
- sku
- serial_number
- gpu_type
- gpu_fw_version
- nic_model
- nic_fw_version
- bmc_fw_version
- uefi_version
- nvme_fw
- os_image_tag

Optional but recommended columns:
- rack_position
- switch_port
- oncall_contact

Example (CSV first line):
host_id,mac_address,sku,serial_number,gpu_type,gpu_fw_version,nic_model,nic_fw_version,bmc_fw_version,uefi_version,nvme_fw,os_image_tag
redwood-node-001,00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e,SM-X12-2xA100,SN1234,H100,65.12,ConnectX-6,18.40,3.2,4.2,3B2QCX0,private-2026.01

Compliance & supply-chain notes

- Procurement: prefer vendors that provide signed firmware images and reproducible checksums. Record vendor-signed manifests in the deployment ticket.
- Evidence preservation: when a hardware incompatibility is detected during acceptance, capture a signed evidence blob (base64 of dmi + fw versions) and attach to the ticket for audit.

Appendix: troubleshooting matrix (common failure modes)

- Symptom: Missing traces only for large requests (> 10k tokens)
  - Likely cause: collector OOM or trace export batching misconfiguration
  - Action: increase collector memory to +2GB, lower batch export size to 200 events, re-run acceptance smoke.

- Symptom: High GPU temperatures during soak
  - Likely cause: incorrect thermal profile or chassis intake flow reversed
  - Action: confirm chassis airflow, apply OEM thermal firmware patch, re-run soak.

Ownership and contacts

- Document owner: Priya Nambiar (eng-private-deployments)
- Oncall for telemetry engineering: telemetry-sre@redwood.ai
- Professional Services pre-sales: ps-deploys@redwood.ai

Related pages and artifacts

- Field acceptance tool: repo `infra/field-ops/acceptance`
- Post-install telemetry checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026
- Hardware compatibility canonical list (internal): /confluence/eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/private-deploy-field-compatibility-matrix-2026

Change log

- 2025-11-04: Created initial draft for internal review (Priya N.).
- 2026-02-18: Updated GPU/NIC driver minimums and added automated acceptance CLI.

If you have questions or need a tailored compatibility review for an upcoming procurement, tag the page and request a field review with `@ps-deploys`.

title: dsid_fd948bf071e34234935872c10122a713__telemetry-action-catalog-and-operator-heuristics-2026.txt
text:
Telemetry-Driven Action Catalog and Operator Heuristics

Overview
-------
This document is an actionable catalog mapping platform telemetry signals to operator heuristics, automated remediations, and runbook play IDs. It is intended for platform SREs and operators who run the Redwood inference control plane and serving clusters. The goal is to reduce decision latency during incidents and to provide clear guidance for safe automation.

Context and scope
-----------------
- Scope: multi-tenant serving runtime, KV/prefix cache, GPU pools, request router, and telemetry-driven operator tasks.
- Audience: on-call SREs, platform operators, reliability engineers, and automation engineers.
- Alignment: complements the Observability SLI Onboarding Playbook and the Emergency Model Swap runbook.

How to use this catalog
-----------------------
1) Monitor: use the listed alert expressions and thresholds as the canonical starting point.
2) Triage: follow the heuristic decision tree to classify severity and likely root cause.
3) Act: choose manual steps or trigger the safe automation script referenced by play ID.
4) Post-incident: add notes to the incident ticket and update the catalog if new conditions are observed.

Signal categories and canonical plays
------------------------------------
1) Cache health signals
   - Signals: kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate, kv_prefix_cache_evictions_per_min, kv_prefix_cache_fill_latency_ms
   - Typical symptoms: increased per-request latency for cold prefixes, token cost spike for repeated re-generation, degraded throughput.
   - SLO guardrails: target kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate >= 0.85; alert when < 0.7 for 5m.
   - Play ID: C-REHYDRATE-01 (Rehydrate / Repair KV prefix cache)
   - Recommended operator heuristic: if evictions_per_min > 500 and hit_rate < 0.7: prioritize high-tenancy prefixes by weight and trigger targeted prefetch + backfill (automated), while enabling aggressive cache-retention for top 10 tenants (manual override option).
   - Safe automation: automated prefetch job that accepts a tenant whitelist and a max-rps budget. Example automation flag: --budget-tokens=50M --tenant-filter=top10-by-rps.

2) Tail-latency and headroom signals
   - Signals: inference_95th_latency_ms, inference_tail_percentile_spike_ratio, inflight_requests_per_instance
   - SLOs: 95th latency <= 220ms (small models), 95th <= 800ms (large models).
   - Play ID: L-TAIL-02 (Tail-latency soft-degrade and model-fallback)
   - Heuristic: if 95th latency breaches SLO by >20% and inflight_requests_per_instance > 75% capacity, first attempt adaptive batching reduction and KV rehydration; if still >2min, initiate model fallback to a compatible lower-latency variant with preserved semantics.
   - Manual safety checks: confirm fallback model has passed golden prompt-set checks (link in Related Pages) and that token cost delta is acceptable to the customer tier.

3) GPU pool and thermal/interference signals
   - Signals: gpu_temp_celsius, gpu_utilization_pct, gpu_context_switch_rate, gpu_preemption_events
   - Play ID: G-ISOLATE-03 (GPU interference isolation and live-evacuation)
