- Ownership: model-onboarding team owns the manifest and validation pipeline; applied-ml owns probe design and quality metrics; eng-serving-runtime owns kernel families and runtime flags.
- Audit: all decomposed promotions must include a signed promotion note in the registry and the eval artifacts attached.
- Observability: ensure per-component feature flags are instrumented and surfaced on the Redwood Console (tokenizer mismatch rate, quant-fallback counts, kv-truncation events).

10) APPENDIX: TROUBLESHOOTING QUICK HITS
- Tokenization mismatch: compare token ids for first 256 characters; if mismatch, check normalization table and byte-fallback mode.
- Stochastic divergence after quant: run 100 deterministic seeds and measure stderr of token logits at each layer.
- Streaming boundary artifacts: simulate chunk sizes of 1, 64, 256 tokens and compare decoder continuations.

REFERENCES:
- Link to eval harness orchestration: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Quantization profiles inventory: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024

CONTRIBUTORS:
Aisha Patel (author), Ravi Menon (reviewer), Claire DuBois (reviewer), Ethan Zhao (tester)

END OF DOCUMENT

title: dsid_1b86b0fd2e4d4d40b1fbb9086d637ce2__developer-docs-api-contract-breach-runbook-and-canonical-fixes-2026.txt
text:
developer-docs-api-contract-breach-runbook-and-canonical-fixes-2026

Overview:
This runbook describes detection, triage, and remediation steps for API contract breaches that surface in developer documentation, SDKs, and client integrations. It is intended for developer-experience engineers, SDK maintainers, docs owners, and on-call support engineers. The goal is to reduce time-to-repair, minimize customer impact, and provide reproducible canonical fixes and documentation patches.

Scope:
- Types of contract breaches covered: schema changes (required/optional fields), response shape regressions, header/case-sensitivity changes, streaming boundary changes, error-code changes, and semantics/enum value changes.
- Triage targets: SDKs (all official languages), docs (docs site snippets, quickstarts), API examples, and sample apps.
- Out of scope: backend-only bugfixes that do not change observable contract (handled by service oncall).

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (SDK/Docs team)
- Secondary owner: eng-serving-runtime (if breach ties to runtime behavior)
- Oncall escalation: follow standard oncall routing; if user-facing breaking change, escalate to oncall-sre and product manager within 60 minutes.

Signals and detection:
1) Automated signals (high-confidence):
   - API contract diffs from nightly contract-checker CI job (contracts/redwood-openapi.yaml)
   - SDK unit test failures flagged as contract mismatch (integration-tests/contracts-suite)
   - Docs snippet test failures from docs-validator (snippet-runner v2)
2) Support signals (customer reports):
   - Support ticket category "SDK: response shape mismatch" or "Docs snippet failing"
   - Slack mentions in #support-engineering or #devx-ops
3) Telemetry signals:
   - Spike in 400/422 errors for a client-request pattern (observability: per-route 4xx drift > 3x baseline for 15m)
   - Increased parsing exceptions in SDK telemetry (sdk-errors.counter with tag=contract-mismatch)

Immediate detection checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm source: CI alert, customer report, or telemetry signal.
2) Grab representative failing request/response pair. If customer provided, ask for raw HTTP log or curl -v output.
3) Run local contract diff: tools/contract-diff --baseline=main --candidate=staging.
4) Determine blast radius: which SDKs, docs snippets, endpoints, and customers are affected.
5) Set incident channel: #incident-docs-contract-<YYYYMMDD> and add owners.

Triage decision matrix:
- Severity P1 (breaks >5% of production callers or business-critical endpoints): immediate rollback or emergency patch within 4 hours.
- Severity P2 (narrow compatibility issue, limited to specific client versions): create targeted SDK hotfix and docs patch; rollout in 24–72 hours.
- Severity P3 (minor docs mismatch or new optional field): schedule regular release cycle patch; add a note in docs changelog.

Canonical fix patterns (examples and templates):
1) Field removed from response but used by default SDK deserializer:
   - Symptom: SDK throws KeyError/NullPointer while parsing model_name or id.
   - Canonical fix: update SDK deserialization to tolerate missing fields and provide a clear deprecation fallback. Example (Python):

   try:
       name = resp_json["model_name"]
   except KeyError:
       # back-compat: older responses used `modelId`
       name = resp_json.get("modelId") or "unknown"

   - Docs fix: add note to API reference: "model_name field deprecated in 2026-03; clients should use modelId OR update to SDK >= v1.4.2"

2) Enum value renamed (e.g., "fast" -> "latency-optimized"):
   - Symptom: clients submit enum and get 422 or default fallback.
   - Canonical fix (server): accept both values for 30 days, emit Deprecation header: X-Deprecation-Notice.
   - Canonical fix (SDK): map legacy value to new value client-side and log telemetry.
   - Docs patch: update examples, add migration snippet, and include a compatibility table.

3) Streaming chunk boundary change (delimiter changed or added metadata frames):
   - Symptom: local streaming clients hang or split tokens incorrectly.
   - Canonical fix: update streaming client parser to support both framing modes, add unit tests with both chunk formats.

Docs-site remediation steps (safe patch workflow):
1) Branching: create branch docs/contract-fix-<ticket>-<short> from docs/main.
2) Update snippets: edit snippet files under content/snippets/<language>/<endpoint>.md and run snippet-runner locally.
3) Add a "Compatibility" callout at the top of the reference page with an explicit migration example.
4) Create a small snippet-based smoke test that reproduces the failing request. Add to docs-validator tests with a @flaky tag if environment sensitive.
5) Submit PR, request expedited review from reviewers listed in this doc. Add label: emergency-docs-fix.
6) Merge and deploy via docs-site CI with canary (docs-canary) enabled for 10% of traffic, monitor errors for 30 minutes, then full rollout.
7) If regression occurs: rollback docs deploy and reopen incident channel.

SDK coordination and hotfix guidance:
- Patch philosophy: prefer client-side tolerant parsing over immediate server rollback when safe. Document tradeoffs.
- Versioning: follow semantic patch versioning and ship a patch release with the compatibility layer. Example release notes snippet: "v1.4.2 — tolerate missing response fields; map legacy enum names; back-compat for streaming framing."
- Telemetry: increment sdk-migration-attempt counter and include client-version metadata.
- Test matrix: run compatibility tests against the last three public server versions (vX-2..vX) and nightly staging.

Developer experience checklist for release PRs (mandatory items):
1) Reproduce failing curl request in developer VM.
2) Add unit/integration test that would have caught the change.
3) Update CHANGELOG.md with clear migration steps.
4) Add docs snippet or update sample app.
5) Add telemetry marker for migration success/failure.
6) Obtain signoff from oncall-sre for major runtime changes.

Example triage session (realistic timeline):
- 00:00 Alert: docs-validator fails on snippet for /v1/predictions (CI).
- 00:10 Channel created; owner assigned (Maya Chen).
- 00:20 Representative failing request captured; contract-diff shows server removed "usage.tokens" field.
- 00:40 Hotfix PR opened for SDK parsing fallback + docs note.
- 01:30 SDK patch merged to release/v1 and docs PR merged to canary.
- 02:15 Monitoring shows no new 4xx spikes; canary promoted.
- 03:00 Incident closed, follow-up action: add contract regression test to nightly.

Post-incident follow-up template (to be included in postmortem):
- Summary (1–2 lines): what changed, who discovered it.
- Impact: list customers, SDK versions, docs pages affected.
- Root cause: single-line technical cause.
- Timeline: bullet timeline of detection -> resolution -> follow-ups.
- Action items: prioritized list with owners and due dates.

Prevention and long-term mitigations:
- Expand contract-checker: add schema evolution rules that flag removals of non-deprecated fields.
- Snippet coverage: increase snippet-based tests for top-20 endpoints by traffic.
- SDK fuzzing: add a contract-fuzzer harness to simulate missing/renamed fields and ensure SDKs tolerate.
- Changelog automation: when API changes land, automatically create docs PR with a compatibility note placeholder.

Quick reference (cheat sheet):
- Key commands:
  - contract-diff --baseline=main --candidate=changeset-123
  - snippet-runner --file content/snippets/python/predictions.md --record
  - ./tools/repro-curl.sh --host staging --path "/v1/predictions" --body payload.json
- Severity mapping table (text):
  - P1: immediate rollback or patch (SLO: 4 hours)
  - P2: targeted hotfix (SLO: 72 hours)
  - P3: scheduled fix (SLO: next minor release)

Related pages:
- eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-local-cache-stub-and-graceful-degrade-playbook-2026
- eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-site-ops-and-canonical-fixes-2025
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/contract-versioning-guidelines

Appendix: sample email to customers for compatibility incident:
Subject: Important compatibility note for Redwood API /v1/predictions
Body:
Hello {customer},
We discovered a change in the /v1/predictions response that may affect SDK parsing in versions prior to v1.4.2. We have released SDK patch v1.4.2 and updated docs with migration steps. If you experience failures, please attach the raw HTTP request/response and we will prioritize support.

Owner notes and contact:
- Runbook owner: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)
- Pager/Oncall: eng-sre oncall (see internal rota)

title: dsid_650dcfe0b9bb4943b41472e842016c1d__hiring-for-impact-competency-sprints-and-100-day-outcomes-2029.txt
text:
hiring-for-impact-competency-sprints-and-100-day-outcomes-2029

Overview

Purpose: This playbook is designed for hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops partners who want a structured, repeatable path from role intake to first-100-day measurable outcomes. It formalizes short competency sprints during hiring and prescribes a manager-led feedback cadence to get new hires to independent impact faster while maintaining equitable assessment.

Scope: Applies to all individual contributor and manager-level hires at Redwood Inference. Exclusions: executive hiring (handled by Talent & Exec Recruiting) and very short-term contractors (<30 days).

Key definitions
- Competency Sprint: A two-week focused evaluation and onboarding sub-phase that defines 2–3 observable competencies to validate in hiring and to train during ramp.
- 100-Day Outcomes: A small set (3–5) of measurable outcomes a manager and new hire agree on during onboarding.

Roles & Ownership
- Hiring Manager: defines role-level outcomes, selects competency sprint goals, owns interview panel and final hire decision.
- People Ops Partner: validates hiring rubric equity, ensures diverse panels, schedules competency sprint tasks, owns offer & coordination.
- Interviewers: evaluate against rubric and provide calibrated written feedback within 48 hours.
- New Hire Buddy: peer from a neighboring team who provides day-to-day orientation for first 4 weeks.

Hiring intake -> Competency Sprint (3-step flow)
1) Intake & Outcome Draft (Manager pre-reqs)
   - Manager completes the Role Readiness brief (template below) in Greenhouse before the JD is posted. Required fields: primary 100-day outcomes (3), top 3 competencies for sprint, minimal technical screen criteria, salary band, escalation contacts.
   - People Ops validates banding and reviewer panel diversity within 48 hours.

2) Competency Sprint design (People Ops + Manager, 48–72 hours)
   - For IC roles, sprints are typically engineering tasks or product problem statements that can be completed asynchronously (4–12 hours of candidate work). For managers, sprints are a short case exercise and two structured interviews.
   - Each sprint includes: success rubric, timebox, data or artifact submission instructions, and reviewer rubric questions.

3) Candidate evaluation & calibration (Interviewers)
   - Interviewers score against the rubric (numeric 1–5) and add a short narrative. Scores and narratives must be in Greenhouse within 48 hours of stage completion.
   - Hiring manager runs a 30-minute calibration meeting with the panel within 72 hours of final interview. If calibration variance >1.0 on any competency, arrange a tie-break interview or sample work review.

Manager checklist: Pre-offer -> Day 1
- Pre-offer: confirm final 100-day outcomes, identify buddy, schedule first-week meetings, and confirm onboarding equipment and access with IT and Infra.
- Day 0 (Offer accepted): send Welcome note with first-week agenda and the Outcome Draft PDF.
- Day 1: 30-minute one-on-one to review the 100-day outcomes and competency sprint expectations.

100-Day outcome template (example)
- Outcome 1 (Product/Feature impact): Deliver a validated improvement to the inference logging pipeline that reduces mean tail latency for 95th percentile tail by 5% for synthetic benchmark workload. Acceptance criteria: PR merged to main, benchmark results in CI show reduction, and post-deploy monitoring shows no regression for 7 days.
- Outcome 2 (Operational mastery): Complete the Redwood infra runbook certification with two successful runbook drills signed off by oncall lead.
- Outcome 3 (Team & process): Lead a cross-team retrospective and produce an action list with owners and SLAs.

Performance & feedback cadence during first 100 days
- Weekly 30m 1:1s during first 8 weeks, with explicit agenda items: blockers, outcomes progress, learning needs.
- Bi-weekly written scorecard from manager (short rubric: Learning, Delivery, Collaboration) at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Each scorecard is shared with new hire and People Ops.
- Formal 100-day review (week 12): manager prepares a 2-slide summary of outcomes, evidence, and recommended ongoing development plan. People Ops uses this artifact for calibration and banding adjustments if needed.

Calibration and fairness checks
- People Ops will run a calibration pool for hires at the same band every quarter. Metrics monitored: offer acceptance rate, time-to-ramp (measured by % of 100-day outcomes achieved), and variance in interview scores across demographics.
- If a candidate’s competency sprint is scored with high reviewer variance or conflicting narratives, People Ops will trigger a post-hire audit and provide an independent assessor to reconcile scores.

Example competency sprint rubric (table rendered as text)
| Competency | Evidence | Success threshold | Evaluator notes |
|------------|----------|------------------:|------------------|
| Service design | Design doc + diagram | 3/5 or higher across all reviewers | Look for clear tradeoffs and rollout plan |
| Code quality | PR with tests | No critical issues, 2 reviewers signoff | Tests + CI passing |
| Cross-team comms | Presentation deck | Clear goals + next steps | Evidence of stakeholder mapping |

Manager decision tree: offer -> low confidence -> hire with ramp plan -> no hire
1) If panel consensus is strong (>=3 reviewers, median score >=4), proceed to offer.
2) If median score is 3 with low variance, manager may request a short follow-up assignment.
3) If panel is split (variance >1.0) and concerns are about fit, consider: a) a second look interview led by a neutral reviewer, or b) decline and record learnings in the hiring postmortem.

Onboarding accelerators (practical tools)
- Competency Sprint Library: curated tasks for common roles (engineering, infra, data infra, product ops) maintained in the People Ops repo: git@redwood-internal:people-ops/competency-sprints.git.
- Role Onboarding Checklist (automated): HR triggers account provisioning 7 days before start. SLA: 95% of hires have accounts provisioned by Day 0.
- Runbook certification: a short multiple-choice + live drill validated by SRE.

Escalation & remediation
- If a new hire is not meeting agreed 100-day outcomes at week 8, manager opens a 4-week Remediation Sprint: documented plan, weekly checkpoints, and People Ops involvement. Outcome options: success (stay), extended ramp (up to 8 additional weeks), or transition support (role change or exit).
- People Ops must be notified before any formal performance step (e.g., PIP) is initiated.

Metrics & KPIs (tracked quarterly)
- Median time-to-first-impact: target <= 75 days for IC hires.
- 100-day outcomes achieved: target 80% across organization.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 65% for priority roles.
- Onboarding provisioning SLA: 95% Day-0-ready.

Templates & artifacts (appendix)
1) Role Readiness brief (fields): Role summary; 3x 100-day outcomes; competency sprint items; interview panel; salary band; urgency level (1–3).
2) Example 100-day review slide (two bullets per slide): Evidence, Result, Next steps.
3) Competency sprint email template for candidates (includes timebox and submission link).

Implementation notes for managers
- Keep outcomes measurable and narrow. Avoid more than three 100-day outcomes.
- Use competency sprints to reduce interviewing noise — they standardize evidence across candidates.
- Document learning opportunities publicly in the team wiki so future hiring loops improve.

Related links
- People Ops competency-sprint repo: git@redwood-internal:people-ops/competency-sprints.git
- Onboarding automation: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-tasks-automation-and-skill-certification-catalog-2029
- Managers handbook (short): /confluence/people-ops/manager-accelerated-integration-and-feedback-sprint-2025

Revision history
- 2028-11-06: Draft authored by Elena Morales.
- 2028-12-12: Added remediation sprint process and metrics (reviewers: Jordan Lee).
- 2029-01-15: Finalized templates, updated SLA targets after Q4 2028 calibration (reviewers: Priya Desai).

title: dsid_1cdeab0ff7e54b34a0f7e3b28d91427e__unit-economics-dashboard-metrics-and-definitions.txt
text:
Unit Economics Dashboard: Metrics and Definitions (Canonical Dictionary)

## Purpose
This page is the canonical metric dictionary for the Internal Unit Economics Dashboard.

It defines:
- The primary KPI: **Blended $/1M output tokens**
- Inclusion/exclusion rules for both cost and tokens
- Dimension definitions used for drilldowns (model/version/quantization profile, region, customer tier)
- Interpretation guidance and common pitfalls

This document is used by Engineering, Product, SRE/Observability, and Finance to ensure the dashboard is consistent with FP&A reporting and reliable for exec-level usage.

---

## Primary KPI
### Metric name
**blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd** (display name: **Blended $/1M output tokens**)

### Definition (high-level)
The blended cost metric answers:
> “For a given time window and slice (e.g., model/region/tier), what did it cost Redwood (USD) to produce 1,000,000 output tokens?”

This is a **fully-loaded, allocated** cost metric (not marginal cost).

### Formula
For a given aggregation grain (see “Time and aggregation” below):

**Blended $/1M output tokens** = ( **Allocated inference cost (USD)** / **Attributed output tokens** ) * 1,000,000

Where:
- **Allocated inference cost (USD)** is computed per the cost attribution model in ADR-034 and the Finance methodology note.
- **Attributed output tokens** are derived from token metering events (including streaming parity) and attributed to dimensions using the rules below.

### Units and formatting
- Unit: **USD per 1,000,000 output tokens**
- Display rounding (UI guidance):
  - Default: 2 decimals for values < $1000
  - 0 decimals for values >= $1000
  - Always show the unit “$/1M output tokens”
- Internally stored as a floating-point numeric (warehouse), but values are presented with rounding to reduce over-interpretation.

---

## Inclusion / exclusion rules
### Token inclusion (denominator)
**Included:**
- Output tokens generated by Redwood inference for text generation/chat completion endpoints.
- Output tokens emitted via **streaming** and **non-streaming** response paths.
- Output tokens produced by tool/function calling responses (if the tokens are part of the model output stream).

**Excluded:**
- Input/prompt tokens (handled by separate metrics; see “Related metrics”).
- Embedding vectors and rerank results (not token-based output).
- Tokens generated by offline eval pipelines or internal benchmarks unless explicitly tagged as production traffic (see “Traffic classification”).

**Success/failure handling:**
- Tokens are counted for requests where output tokens are emitted. Partial outputs due to truncation/timeouts are included **if** tokens were produced and metered.
- Requests that fail before any model output is produced contribute **0 output tokens**.

**Streaming parity requirement:**
- Streaming output tokens MUST be counted using the same tokenizer/model config used for billing-grade tokenization.
- Any streaming undercount is treated as a Sev-2 data quality issue if it materially impacts blended cost trends (see SLO page for thresholds).

### Cost inclusion (numerator)
This metric uses **allocated** costs required to serve inference.

**Included cost buckets (v1):**
- GPU compute costs (primary): fleet spend allocated by region and capacity type (on-demand/reserved/committed as applicable).
- Supporting infra directly attributable to inference serving (e.g., GPU host overhead that is modeled in the rate card).
- Shared serving overhead as defined in the Finance methodology (e.g., a fixed % uplift or allocated overhead line, if included in the current rate card version).

**Excluded cost buckets (v1):**
- Non-serving R&D costs (engineering payroll, model research, etc.).
- Sales/marketing, G&A, and other corporate overhead not designated in Finance’s serving overhead model.
- Customer support and success costs.

**Idle capacity treatment:**
- Idle capacity is **included** in blended cost via the allocation model in ADR-034.
- Interpretation note: A spike in blended cost can be driven by reduced utilization even if per-request efficiency is unchanged.

### Traffic classification
To keep this KPI finance-aligned and stable:
- Default dashboard views include only **production inference traffic**.
- Internal test traffic is excluded when the request is tagged with `traffic_class=test` or `internal=true` (tag names are implementation-defined; the aggregation job normalizes these).
- If tags are missing, traffic is treated as production by default; this is monitored as a data quality signal.

---

## Time and aggregation
### Aggregation grain
- Primary aggregation grain: **hourly**, based on **event_time (UTC)**.
- Daily/weekly/monthly views are derived by rolling up hourly aggregates.

### Freshness expectations
- Near-real-time (“Live”) view is expected to be complete within the pipeline SLO.
- Finance reporting (“Finance”) view may apply a longer stabilization window depending on rate card and allocation cadence.

See: unit-economics-pipeline-slo for the current freshness and completeness SLOs.

### Rate card versioning
- All cost calculations MUST be reproducible with a **rate_card_version** and **allocation_model_version**.
- Dashboard UI should expose rate card version in an info panel (not as a primary filter) to avoid accidental comparisons across versions.

---

## Dimensions (drilldowns)
This section defines the canonical dimensions for grouping/filtering. All dimension values are normalized by the aggregation service.

### 1) Model
**Dimension names (canonical):**
- `model_id` (stable internal identifier)
- `model_display_name` (human readable; may change over time)
- `model_version` (serving version/build identifier)

**Definition:**
- `model_id` is the primary key used for grouping. It must not be a marketing alias.
- `model_version` identifies a materially distinct serving artifact (weights revision, tokenizer config change, runtime compile config change) that can impact cost/quality.

**Grouping guidance:**
- Default top-level views group by `model_id`.
- Drilldowns can include `model_version` to identify regressions from rollouts.

**Common pitfalls:**
- Do not group by raw routing names or gateway “route” identifiers; these are not stable and can create false fragmentation.

### 2) Quantization profile
**Dimension name (canonical):** `quantization_profile`

**Definition:**
A controlled vocabulary identifying the quantization/precision strategy applied at serving time (e.g., fp16, int8, awq-int4). Values are constrained to an allowlist to prevent high cardinality.

**Rules:**
- Must be present for all served requests for models where multiple quantization variants exist.
- If unknown, use `quantization_profile=unknown` (do not emit nulls).

**Interpretation:**
- Quantization changes often reduce cost but can shift latency/quality. Use this dimension alongside latency and quality guardrails to avoid optimizing cost alone.

### 3) Region
**Dimension name (canonical):** `region`

**Definition:**
A normalized serving region identifier used across runtime, gateway, and infra billing. Region normalization collapses cloud region labels and internal colo codes into a canonical set.

**Rules:**
- Unknown or unmapped values are assigned `region=unknown` and must trigger a mapping backlog item if volume is material.
- Region is defined by where inference execution occurs (not where the request originates).

**Examples (canonical format):**
- `us-east-1`
- `us-west-2`
- `eu-west-1`
- `eu-central-1`
- `ap-southeast-1`
- `colo-sjc1` (example internal colo naming; only if part of the canonical set)

### 4) Customer tier
**Dimension name (canonical):** `customer_tier`

**Allowed values (v1):**
- `self_serve` (PLG/hosted API, pay-as-you-go)
- `dedicated` (reserved capacity / dedicated GPU pools)
- `private` (VPC/on-prem private deployments)
- `enterprise` (enterprise contract on hosted/dedicated; used when contract terms require distinct reporting)
- `unknown` (should be rare; triggers data quality investigation)

**Derivation (summary):**
Tier is derived from a prioritized set of signals:
1) Explicit contract metadata / billing plan tier (authoritative where available)
2) Dedicated/private routing flags (workload served on dedicated pool or private control plane)
3) Fallback heuristics for legacy accounts

**Edge cases:**
- Pilots/credits: remain in their actual tier (e.g., `self_serve`) unless contract metadata indicates otherwise.
- Resellers: attribution depends on contract metadata; default is to attribute to the reseller’s tier, not end-customer.

### 5) Streaming flag (supporting dimension)
**Dimension name:** `is_streaming`

**Definition:**
- `true` if the response is delivered via streaming.
- `false` otherwise.

**Usage:**
Used to debug discrepancies (streaming parity), not usually shown as a top-level business breakdown.

---

## Related supporting metrics (diagnostics)
These metrics are used to explain changes in blended cost. They are expected to be present in drilldowns and/or the “Contributing Signals” panel.

1) **output_tokens**
- Definition: total attributed output tokens for the slice.

2) **allocated_cost_usd**
- Definition: allocated inference cost (USD) for the slice.

3) **cache_hit_rate** (runtime-derived)
- Definition: fraction of tokens served from prefix/KV cache (exact definition depends on runtime instrumentation; must be documented and stable).
- Interpretation: higher cache hit rate should generally reduce cost per output token, but can interact with batching and request mix.

4) **batching_efficiency** (runtime-derived)
- Definition: normalized measure of effective batch utilization during decode (and/or prefill), scaled 0–1.
- Interpretation: drops often correlate with higher blended cost.

5) **avg_output_tokens_per_request**
- Definition: output_tokens / request_count for the slice.
- Interpretation: larger outputs can increase decode time; whether it increases or decreases $/1M depends on batching/cache behavior.

6) **prefill_decode_ratio** (optional v1.1; shown if available)
- Definition: average prefill compute relative to decode compute.
- Interpretation: long-context workloads can shift cost structure even if output length is stable.

---

## Interpretation guidelines
### What this metric is good for
- Tracking **overall serving economics** over time for exec reporting.
- Identifying **outliers** by model, region, and tier.
- Catching **regressions** after rollouts (model_version/quantization_profile changes).
- Prioritizing runtime/infra work by quantifying impact.

### What this metric is NOT
- Not a customer billing metric.
- Not a marginal cost estimate for “one more request.”
- Not directly comparable across time windows if the **rate card version** or **allocation model version** changed (unless you intentionally control for that).

### Common causes of changes (and how to diagnose)
1) **Utilization / idle changes**
- Symptom: blended cost increases across many slices.
- Check: fleet utilization, allocated idle component (if shown), and whether traffic volume dropped.

2) **Streaming metering regressions**
- Symptom: output_tokens drop without traffic drop; blended cost rises.
- Check: `is_streaming=true` slices; compare request_count vs token counts; consult canary and completeness alerts.

3) **Region mapping issues**
- Symptom: sudden rise in `region=unknown` or missing major region.
- Check: normalization table updates; ingestion changes; recent deploys.

4) **Quantization rollout**
- Symptom: cost decreases but latency/quality concerns appear.
- Check: quantization_profile breakdown; confirm guardrails and model_version alignment.

### Confidence / data quality guidance
The dashboard should be treated as “reporting-grade” only when the following are true for the selected time window:
- Completeness SLO met (hourly coverage within threshold)
- Unknown dimension rates are below thresholds (region/tier/model_version)
- Reconciliation report (dashboard vs billing/spend) is within the expected tolerance

If any of the above are not met, the UI should display a visible caveat (e.g., “Partial data” / “Low confidence”), and users should follow the on-call guide for validation.

---

## Example calculation (illustrative)
For `2025-02-10 13:00–14:00 UTC`, slice: `model_id=rw-llama-70b`, `region=eu-west-1`, `customer_tier=self_serve`:
- allocated_cost_usd = 1,250.00
- output_tokens = 410,000,000

Blended $/1M output tokens = (1,250.00 / 410,000,000) * 1,000,000 = **$3.05 / 1M output tokens**

---

## Change management
Any change to:
- the primary formula,
- cost inclusion rules,
- token inclusion rules,
- or allowed dimension values

…requires:
1) Updated ADR (if cost attribution changes materially)
2) Finance sign-off (Laura Bennett or delegate; FP&A owner Rishi Malhotra)
3) Version bump (`allocation_model_version` and/or `rate_card_version` and/or metric semantic version)
4) A backfill plan (if historical comparability is required)

---

## Owners
- Metric definitions & Finance alignment: **Rishi Malhotra (FP&A)**, **Laura Bennett (CFO)**
- Telemetry/token metering correctness: **Nadia Rahman**, **Logan Wright**
- Aggregation service & warehouse views: **Mei Lin**, **Caleb Johnson**
- Dashboard reliability (SLOs/alerts): **Sean Gallagher**, **Allison Grant**

For operational issues and discrepancies, start with: Oncall Guide — Unit Economics Dashboard.

title: dsid_0eef3b482a54451eb3587850b6a5818d__runtime-stability-and-kernel-tuning-rc1-2026.txt
text:
Runtime Stability and Kernel Tuning RC1 — notes and rollout

Summary:

This document captures the RC1 release for the runtime stability and kernel-tuning initiative. RC1 bundles three coordinated changes: (1) the latency-priority preemptive kernel mapper v2 (LP-Mapper v2), (2) conservative batch-splitting heuristics for multi-model pods, and (3) expanded runtime telemetry + profiling helpers. The goal is to reduce p95 generation latency regressions and improve tail behavior on mixed workloads while retaining or slightly improving throughput for steady-state traffic.

Key goals and SLOs:
- p95 single-request generation latency for small sequence workloads (<=256 tokens) <= 120 ms on G4dn/RTX-5000 equivalent GPUs.
- p99 latency reduction target: -15% relative to baseline on mixed burst traces collected 2026-01-12 through 2026-01-18.
- Throughput impact: <= 6% reduction for steady 1000 qps T2-small workloads; aim for neutral impact after automated batching adjustments.
- No increased memory OOM incidents in canary window (see rollout plan).

What changed in RC1 (high level):

1) LP-Mapper v2 (latency-priority preemptive kernel mapper)
- Behavior: incoming low-latency requests get prioritized mapping to lightly loaded shards. If a long-running kernel is running on a GPU, LP-Mapper v2 can preempt queued batches that are not yet bound to a kernel invocation and reassign them to other available devices. Preemption is conservative: kernels already executing are not aborted; only pending batch assignments are moved.
- Configuration knobs introduced: runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled, runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.preemption_window_ms (default 40), runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.util_threshold (default 0.68).
- Expected benefit: reduces p95 by moving short interactive requests off hot shards; may increase cross-device transfer events when preemption occurs — mitigated by the batching heuristics below.

2) Conservative batch-splitting for multi-model pods
- Rationale: observed p99 spikes when large models and small chat assistants shared the same pod under bursty load. RC1 implements a cost model to split large batches only when expected per-token latency savings exceed data transfer overhead.
- New configs: runtime.batch.split_threshold_ms (default 18ms), runtime.batch.cost_per_token (default 0.002 ms/token).
- Example: a 1024-token batch for gpt-small will not be split if predicted split overhead > 18ms.

3) Expanded telemetry and profiling helpers
- New metrics emitted (timeseries names): runtime.latency.generation.p50/p95/p99, runtime.kvcache.hit_rate_p95, runtime.kernel.invocation_latency_ms.p95, runtime.kernel.queue_length, runtime.kernel.preempt_events.count, runtime.batch.split_events.count.
- New high-cardinality trace attributes (added to traces): model.variant_id, shard_id, kernel_version, lp_mapper_decision. Use these attributes in traces only for high-priority samples; defaults are sampled at 0.25%.
- Added a small CLI tool (rwd-rt-profile) to capture a 120s focused profile and upload to internal profiling store. Usage: rwd-rt-profile --target <pod> --duration 120 --label rc1-tuning. The tool ships in /opt/redwood/bin for canary agents.

Performance regression tests and results (canary summary):
- Canary window: 2026-02-15 to 2026-02-21 across us-west1 and eu-central1 test clusters.
- Workloads: interactive chat (median length 48 tokens), long-context summarization (median 1024 tokens), embedding bulk (batch size 128).
- Observed: interactive chat p95 improved by 18% (us-west1) and 13% (eu-central1); p99 improved by 12% average. Long-context throughput decreased 4% on average; embedding throughput unaffected. Memory utilization for multi-model pods increased by 1.8% median (within safe headroom).
- Canary incidents: two minor issues (see Known issues) triggered abort in 1 canary cluster; mitigations applied and rollout resumed.

Profiling playbook snippets (how to reproduce and inspect):
1) Capture focused profile with rwd-rt-profile
- Step 1: identify candidate pod (kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime,model=gpt-small)
- Step 2: run: /opt/redwood/bin/rwd-rt-profile --target pod/<pod-name> --duration 120 --label rc1-tuning
- Step 3: retrieve profile from profiling store UI or CLI: rwd-profile fetch --label rc1-tuning --since 2026-02-20

2) Quick kernel heatmap (local)
- Command: curl -sS http://localhost:7000/metrics | grep kernel.invocation | sort -nrk2 | head -n 40
- Interpretation: rows indicate kernels by id and invocation counts; high invocation / high latency kernels are the first candidates for specialized kernels or fused ops.

Rollout and rollback plan (operations playbook):
- Canary: deploy RC1 to 5% of serving fleet (us-west1/eu-central1 only) for 72 hours, with an accelerated sampling for latency SLOs (1s sampling window).
- Escalation thresholds (automated):
  - if p95 increases > 10% over baseline for > 10 consecutive minutes -> auto-pause rollout and open runbook incident.
  - if p99 increases > 20% or any OOM error count > 5 in 5 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous kernel mapper (artifact: rp/runtime-kmapper-v1@sha256:ab12ef...)
- Rollout steps (ops):
  1) Tag release: rwd-release tag rc1-kernel-tuning-2026-02-28
  2) Update config: kubectl apply -f patch-lp-mapper.yaml (example below)
  3) Monitor for 60 minutes with telemetry dashboards: Runtime / Kernel Tuning RC1 (dashboard id: rtd-rt-kernel-rc1)
  4) If stable, expand to 25% after 24 hours, then 60% after 72 hours, then full.
- Rollback steps: run rwd-deploy rollback --service runtime --tag previous --region <region> or apply kubectl set image to previous runtime image. Notify SRE channel #sre-runtime and tag incident with "rc1-rollback".

Known issues and mitigations (summary):
- Issue A: Preemption thrash on 8x A100 pods when many small jobs hit concurrently. Symptom: increased kernel.preempt_events.count and small rise in cross-device transfers; in canary this caused two short p99 spikes.
  - Mitigation: lower runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.preemption_window_ms to 20ms for 8x A100 pool (config override), and increase sampling of preemption traces to 2% for diagnostics.
- Issue B: Edge-case OOM on multi-model pods with pinned KV cache when batch-splitting engaged. Symptom: pod eviction with OOMKilled and memory footprint spike after split operation.
  - Mitigation: temporary: runtime.batch.split_threshold_ms -> 30ms (makes splits rarer). Long-term: add soft-limit on kvcache pinned bytes per-model in next patch.
- Issue C: Observability tag cardinality increase caused minor metrics ingestion churn in eu-central; fixed by sampling and batched emission.

Runbook excerpt (immediate responder steps if p95 jumps):
1) Confirm alert: open runtime kernel-tuning RC1 dashboard; check runtime.latency.generation.p95 by region.
2) Check pod-level preempt events: kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> | grep preempt_event
3) If preempt_events.count spike correlates with p95, temporarily set runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled=false for the region:
   kubectl -n redwood patch configmap runtime-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled":"false"}}'
4) If OOMs present, scale impacted nodepool with: gcloud container clusters resize <cluster> --node-pool <pool> --num-nodes +2 (or equivalent). Mark runbook incident and notify ownership.
5) Collect and upload profile: /opt/redwood/bin/rwd-rt-profile --target pod/<pod> --duration 120 --label incident-<id> then attach to incident.

Ownership, contacts, and followups:
- Code owner: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-team (primary: Marco Chen).
- SRE on-call for rollout windows: see oncall rota (link: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations).
- Followups planned:
  - v1.1: add soft kvcache per-model accounting and eviction policies (owner: runtime-memory-team).
  - v1.2: fuse common attention kernels for gpt-small/gpt-medium to reduce invocation latency (owner: kernel-ops).

Appendix A — example config patch (patch-lp-mapper.yaml):
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-config
  namespace: redwood
data:
  runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled: "true"
  runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.preemption_window_ms: "40"
  runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.util_threshold: "0.68"
  runtime.batch.split_threshold_ms: "18"
---

Appendix B — example quick diagnostics commands:
- pod heatmap (top 20 kernels): curl -sS http://<pod-ip>:7000/metrics | grep kernel.invocation | sort -nrk2 | head -n 20
- check queue lengths across shards: rwd-rt-cli shard-stats --start -10m --end now --metric kernel.queue_length
- fetch recent preemption traces (sampled): rwd-trace query --tag lp_mapper_decision=true --since 2026-02-14

Notes and writing conventions: this page is intended as the canonical RC1 release note, rollout playbook, and immediate troubleshooting guide. For design rationale, see the kernel mapper ADR page in related_pages. For profiling playbook canonical guidance, prefer the "runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025" page for full methodology.

Change log:
- 2026-02-04: Draft created (Aisha Banerjee).
- 2026-02-18: Canary results added; mitigations for thrash and OOMs documented (Marco Chen).
- 2026-03-01: Reviewed and published after minor config tweaks (Lena Ortiz).
